punctuated: 語之不惰，眞有欲罷不能者，視諸自畫願息，不亦大相十百者耶？世之論顏者，莫不曰：「步亦步，趨亦趨。」可以見其以實求孔子焉。又莫不曰：「墮體黜聰，心齋坐忘。」可以見其以虛求孔子焉。不知虛實有無之間，動靜形感之際，顏子殆難以形迹者拘矣。自今觀之，「非禮勿視，非禮勿聽，非禮勿言，非禮勿動」，非以中禮者聖人，而四勿復禮者爲求聖之功乎？「不遷怒，不貳過」，非以無過無怒者聖人，而不遷不貳者爲求聖之功乎？明以察幾，犍以致決，由不遷怒以求至於無怒，由不貳過以求至於無過，由復禮以求至於中禮，約其情以合於中，盡其性以契乎天。顏子之心，蓋得孔子之意而忘言者多矣。其動靜語默，用行舍藏，何莫不與孔子似耶？是故「庶乎屢空」，一孔子之浮雲富貴也；「願無伐善，無施勞」，一孔子之何有未能也；「終日如愚」，一孔子之無言默識也；「有若無，實若虛」，「得一善，拳拳服膺弗失」，一孔子之爲學不厭也。顏之去孔，特未達一間耳。曰
translation_en:
…and his tirelessness in speaking [?] truly showed that he could not stop even if he wished. Compared with those who set limits for themselves and wished to rest, was he not ten or a hundred times greater? Those in the world who discuss Master Yan all say, “When the master walked, he too walked; when the master hurried, he too hurried.” Here one can see him seeking to emulate Confucius through the substantial. They also all say, “Let the body fall away and dismiss keen perception; fast the mind and sit in forgetfulness.” Here one can see him seeking to emulate Confucius through emptiness. They do not understand that, between emptiness and substance, being and nonbeing, and amid activity, stillness, bodily manifestation, and response, Master Yan can scarcely be confined within outward traces.

Considered now, the injunctions “Do not look at what is contrary to ritual; do not listen to what is contrary to ritual; do not speak what is contrary to ritual; do not act contrary to ritual” surely mean that the sage accords with ritual, while returning to ritual through these four prohibitions constitutes the work of seeking sagehood. “He did not transfer his anger or repeat his faults”: does this not mean that the sage is without faults or anger, while neither transferring anger nor repeating faults constitutes the work of seeking sagehood? With clarity he discerned the first stirrings, and with firmness [?] he reached a resolution. From not transferring anger, he sought to reach freedom from anger; from not repeating faults, he sought to reach freedom from faults; from returning to ritual, he sought to reach accord with ritual. He restrained his feelings to accord with the Mean and fully realized his nature to accord with Heaven. Master Yan’s mind had surely often grasped Confucius’s meaning and forgotten the words. In activity and stillness, speech and silence, acting when employed and withdrawing when set aside, how was he not like Confucius in every respect?

Thus, “He came close, though often in want” was at one with Confucius’s regard for wealth and rank as floating clouds. “I wish neither to boast of my goodness nor to impose toil upon others” was at one with Confucius’s declarations, “What claim have I?” and “I have not yet been able.” “All day he seemed like a fool” was at one with Confucius’s wish to remain without words and his silently retaining what he learned. “Possessing, yet seeming to possess nothing; full, yet seeming empty,” and “Whenever he attained something good, he clasped it firmly to his breast and never lost it” were at one with Confucius’s tirelessness in learning. Master Yan fell short of Confucius by only a single interval. To say …

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
庶曰願曰如愚曰拳拳不其體段已具微有迹
之明徵乎易復之初九曰不遠復无祇悔元吉
而孔子繫之以辭曰顏氏之子其殆庶幾乎有
不善未嘗不知知之未嘗復行也孔子蓋器之
深矣高堅前後如立卓爾然則顏子喟然之歎
其深於道者乎何聖人之不可學而至也蓋有
見其優於湯武矣是學不止於湯武也有見其
同道禹稷矣是學不讓於禹稷也有見其有爲
若舜矣是學又可至於舜也孔子惟我與爾之
===
譽其有所試矣顏子之學何嘗異于人而人自
不能不異者其諸異乎人之好與雖然顏子之
賢固在於好學好學之要莫過於不貳過妄復
則無妄過不貳則無過象曰復其見天地之心
然則不遠之復其見聖人之心乎知天地之心
復于化則知聖人之心復于天顏子求純心于
天其知復于聖乎
同前
于邦棟
punctuated:
「庶」，曰「願」，曰「如愚」，曰「拳拳」，不其體段已具、微有迹之明徵乎？《易》復之初九曰：「不遠復，无祇悔，元吉。」而孔子繫之以辭曰：「顏氏之子，其殆庶幾乎！有不善，未嘗不知；知之，未嘗復行也。」孔子蓋器之深矣！高堅前後，如立卓爾，然則顏子喟然之歎，其深於道者乎？何聖人之不可學而至也？蓋有見其優於湯武矣，是學不止於湯武也；有見其同道禹稷矣，是學不讓於禹稷也；有見其有爲若舜矣，是學又可至於舜也。孔子「惟我與爾」之譽，其有所試矣。顏子之學何嘗異于人，而人自不能不異者，其諸異乎人之好與？雖然，顏子之賢固在於好學，好學之要莫過於不貳過。妄復則無妄，過不貳則無過。《象》曰：「復，其見天地之心。」然則不遠之復，其見聖人之心乎？知天地之心復于化，則知聖人之心復于天。顏子求純心于天，其知復于聖乎？

同前
于邦棟
translation_en:
…“nearly,” “I wish,” “as though foolish,” and “steadfastly”: are these not clear evidence that the full framework was already present, with only faint traces remaining? The initial nine of Return in the Book of Changes says: “Returning before going far; reaching no occasion for regret; supremely auspicious.” Confucius appended these words: “The son of the Yan family surely came close! Whenever there was anything un善 in him, he never failed to recognize it; once he recognized it, he never did it again.” How highly Confucius esteemed his capacity! Lofty and firm, before and behind, seeming to stand towering before him—was not Master Yan’s deep sigh an expression of profound understanding of the Way? Why should sagehood be unattainable through learning? Some indeed saw him as superior to Tang and Wu: thus his learning did not stop at their attainment. Some saw him as following the same Way as Yu and Ji: thus his learning did not yield to theirs. Some saw him as capable of becoming like Shun through effort: thus his learning could also reach Shun’s attainment. Confucius’s praise, “Only you and I,” surely rested on something put to the test. How was Master Yan’s learning ever different from other people’s? Yet what made others unable to avoid regarding him as different was perhaps that what he loved differed from what they loved.

Nevertheless, Master Yan’s worth certainly lay in his love of learning, and nothing is more essential to loving learning than never repeating a fault. When one returns from waywardness, there is no waywardness; when a fault is not repeated, there is no fault. The Commentary on the Images says: “In Return, one sees the heart of Heaven and Earth.” Then, in returning before going far, does one see the heart of the sage? Knowing that the heart of Heaven and Earth returns through transformation, one knows that the sage’s heart returns to Heaven. Master Yan sought to make his heart pure in accord with Heaven: did he understand how to return to sagehood?

Same as the preceding topic.
Yu Bangdong.

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教授萬　批〔總理真切無一贅辭宜録之〕
從
考試官教諭袁　批〔辭意圓融雋永得程子旨〕
考試官教諭顧　批〔渾融警健〕
天下之道不外於心也君子善事其心焉則作
聖之本立矣本立則心有所主而學得其要雖
不期于聖也而積之以久將有優入而不自知
者聖人之道有不可以至乎是非聖人之道也
道之統於吾心而與聖人同焉者也惟聖人能
===
主靜以立其體而用之動者自無弗和而學者
每淆於動以失其真靜之體而復役於外以求
之則其去聖人也始遠矣故君子之志於道也
必以聖人爲期而希聖之功則以治心爲要也
能治其心則性無不復情無不順靜固定動亦
定而萬事萬物無有不得其理者矣學之爲道
不外于是而聖人所以爲聖人者又豈有加於
是哉此顔子所以爲好學而程子推之以爲萬
世告也今夫人之生也必得天地之心以爲心
punctuated:
同考試官教授萬，批〔總理真切，無一贅辭，宜録之。〕從。
考試官教諭袁，批〔辭意圓融雋永，得程子旨。〕
考試官教諭顧，批〔渾融警健。〕
天下之道不外於心也。君子善事其心焉，則作聖之本立矣。本立，則心有所主而學得其要。雖不期于聖也，而積之以久，將有優入而不自知者。聖人之道有不可以至乎？是非聖人之道也，道之統於吾心而與聖人同焉者也。惟聖人能主靜以立其體，而用之動者自無弗和。而學者每淆於動，以失其真靜之體，而復役於外以求之，則其去聖人也始遠矣。故君子之志於道也，必以聖人爲期，而希聖之功則以治心爲要也。能治其心，則性無不復，情無不順，靜固定，動亦定，而萬事萬物無有不得其理者矣。學之爲道不外于是，而聖人所以爲聖人者，又豈有加於是哉？此顔子所以爲好學，而程子推之以爲萬世告也。今夫人之生也，必得天地之心以爲心，
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Wan, Professor, comments: 〔The reasoning throughout is sound and incisive, without a single superfluous phrase. It merits selection.〕 Agreed.
Examiner Yuan, Instructor, comments: 〔The language and meaning are rounded and harmonious, with lasting savor; the essay captures Master Cheng’s purport.〕
Examiner Gu, Instructor, comments: 〔Thoroughly integrated, striking, and vigorous.〕
The Way of all under Heaven does not lie outside the mind. If the gentleman tends his mind well, the foundation for becoming a sage is established. Once that foundation is established, the mind has a governing principle, and learning grasps its essentials. Even without setting his sights on sagehood, through prolonged accumulation he will enter it with ease, unaware that he has done so. Can the Way of the sages be unattainable? This is no Way belonging exclusively to the sages: it is the Way comprehended within our own minds, which we share with the sages. Only the sage can give primacy to stillness and thereby establish the mind’s substance, so that its functioning in activity is naturally harmonious in every respect. Learners, however, are often confused by activity and thus lose the substance of their true stillness. Then they labor over external things to seek it, and so begin to grow distant from the sages. Thus, when the gentleman sets his will upon the Way, he must take sagehood as his goal; and the essential work of aspiring to sagehood lies in governing the mind. If he can govern his mind, his nature will be fully restored and his feelings will all follow their proper course. In stillness he will assuredly be settled, and in activity he will also be settled; among the myriad affairs and things, none will fail to accord with its proper principle. The Way of learning goes no further than this. How could that which makes a sage a sage add anything to it? This is why Master Yan was said to love learning, and why Master Cheng elaborated upon this to instruct all generations. Now, when human beings are born, they necessarily receive the mind of Heaven and Earth as their own mind …

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
而所謂天地之心者于何見之易之復曰復其
見天地之心乎而于咸又曰觀其所感而天地
萬物之情可見矣蓋一陽初動雖足以少見乾
坤之蘊而發散之幾尚介乎有無之間至於咸
則與萬物交相感應而絪縕摩盪蓋有欲一之
而不能者而天地之和卒不爲之少戾焉此其
所以爲無心之感而天地萬物之情于是乎可
見也嗚呼知天地萬物之情見於感則人之所
以爲心者亦斷可識矣當夫客感之未形也思
慮之未起也廓然大公而已矣粹然至正而已
===
矣盎然太和而已矣如太虛然鬼神不得而知
之吾無所交于物而物亦不得以爲吾之病視
諸聖人之心無意必固我之私者何以異哉惟
夫一有所感而可喜可怒可哀可懼可愛可惡
可欲之事雜然而並交於前而吾之所以爲心
者不得其養而無以爲主宰之本則物交物引
之而去不難也以外物爲外將牽己而從之較
之聖人始不能不相遠耳情之公者或奪於私
punctuated:
而所謂天地之心者，于何見之？《易》之《復》曰：「復，其見天地之心乎！」而于《咸》又曰：「觀其所感，而天地萬物之情可見矣。」蓋一陽初動，雖足以少見乾坤之蘊，而發散之幾尚介乎有無之間。至於《咸》，則與萬物交相感應，而絪縕摩盪，蓋有欲一之而不能者，而天地之和卒不爲之少戾焉。此其所以爲無心之感，而天地萬物之情于是乎可見也。

嗚呼！知天地萬物之情見於感，則人之所以爲心者亦斷可識矣。當夫客感之未形也，思慮之未起也，廓然大公而已矣，粹然至正而已矣，盎然太和而已矣。如太虛然，鬼神不得而知之。吾無所交于物，而物亦不得以爲吾之病。視諸聖人之心無意必固我之私者，何以異哉？惟夫一有所感，而可喜、可怒、可哀、可懼、可愛、可惡、可欲之事，雜然而並交於前，而吾之所以爲心者不得其養，而無以爲主宰之本，則物交，物引之而去不難也。以外物爲外，將牽己而從之，較之聖人，始不能不相遠耳。情之公者或奪於私
translation_en:
…And where can this so-called heart of Heaven and Earth be seen? Of the hexagram Return (Fu), the Book of Changes says: “In Return, do we not see the heart of Heaven and Earth!” And of Influence (Xian), it also says: “Observe what they respond to, and the true dispositions of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things can be seen.” When the single yang line first stirs, it suffices to reveal something of what Heaven and Earth contain, but the incipient movement toward outward diffusion still lies between existence and nonexistence. With Influence, however, there is reciprocal stimulation and response among the myriad things, intermingling, friction, and agitation. These seem impossible to reduce to unity, even if one wished to do so; yet the harmony of Heaven and Earth is ultimately not disturbed in the slightest. This is why their response occurs without deliberate intention, and why the true dispositions of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things can be seen in it.

Alas! Once we know that the true dispositions of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things appear in their responses, we can also assuredly understand what constitutes the human heart-mind. Before responses to external stimuli take shape, before thoughts arise, it is simply expansive and utterly impartial, pure and perfectly upright, brimming with supreme harmony. Like the Great Void, it cannot be fathomed even by ghosts and spirits. I have no intercourse with things, and things likewise cannot become a source of affliction to me. How does this differ from the heart-mind of the sage, free of the selfishness of preconceptions, insistence, obstinacy, and egoism? But once something stimulates us, matters that occasion joy, anger, sorrow, fear, love, hatred, and desire crowd together before us. If that which constitutes our heart-mind has not been nourished and thus lacks a foundation for exercising mastery, then, when things come into contact with it, they can easily draw it away. Taking external things as external [?], one is pulled into following them; only then does one necessarily become distant from the sage. What is impartial in our feelings may be overcome by selfishness…

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
也正者或陷于偏也和者或乖其則也其不能
至聖人之道也固宜也然則欲求至乎聖人之
道者抑將絕物屛知如彼虛無寂滅者而後可
以言學乎亦惟曰善事其心而已矣昔之論心
者謂之天君言乎無所不主也謂之大體言乎
無所不統也是故存之則為五常發之則為四
端著之於身則為五倫所以統乎性情而妙動
靜之幾者也雖湛然至虛而七情之體段已具
雖寂然不動而未發之氣象可觀萬事萬物蓋
===
無一不在其中者然惟情之發也去心為不遠
而其幾為初動且其所感者皆在吾一身交接
之內而其約之也亦不難此固學者之於聖人
相去幾希之際而易之所謂感也於此約之則
辨之於早其復不遠而凡情之發也蓋有不待
强制力復而無有弗中節焉者矣是故其喜也
以物之當喜也其怒也以物之當怒也哀不至
於傷也懼不至於懾也不之其所親愛而辟也
不之其所賤惡而辟也不之其所歆羡而辟也
punctuated: 也，正者或陷于偏也，和者或乖其則也，其不能至聖人之道也，固宜也。然則欲求至乎聖人之道者，抑將絕物屛知，如彼虛無寂滅者，而後可以言學乎？亦惟曰善事其心而已矣。昔之論心者，謂之天君，言乎無所不主也；謂之大體，言乎無所不統也。是故存之則為五常，發之則為四端，著之於身則為五倫，所以統乎性情而妙動靜之幾者也。雖湛然至虛，而七情之體段已具；雖寂然不動，而未發之氣象可觀。萬事萬物，蓋無一不在其中者。然惟情之發也，去心為不遠，而其幾為初動，且其所感者皆在吾一身交接之內，而其約之也亦不難。此固學者之於聖人相去幾希之際，而《易》之所謂感也。於此約之，則辨之於早，其復不遠，而凡情之發也，蓋有不待强制力復而無有弗中節焉者矣。是故其喜也，以物之當喜也；其怒也，以物之當怒也；哀不至於傷也，懼不至於懾也；不之其所親愛而辟也，不之其所賤惡而辟也，不之其所歆羡而辟也。
translation_en:
…what is upright may lapse into partiality, and what is harmonious may depart from its proper rule. It is only natural that one should then fail to attain the Way of the sages. Must those who seek to attain the Way of the sages therefore cut themselves off from things and suppress knowledge, like those devoted to emptiness and extinction, before they can speak of learning? All that is required is to tend the heart-mind well. Those of old who discussed the heart-mind called it the “Heavenly Lord,” meaning that there is nothing over which it does not preside; they called it the “greater part,” meaning that there is nothing it does not govern. Thus, preserved within, it constitutes the Five Constant Virtues; expressed outwardly, it constitutes the Four Sprouts; manifested in one's person, it constitutes the Five Human Relationships. It thereby governs human nature and the emotions and wondrously orders the incipient workings of activity and stillness. Though limpid and utterly empty, it already possesses the full configuration of the seven emotions; though still and unmoving, its condition before the emotions arise can be discerned. Of all affairs and things, there is surely none that is not contained within it.

Now, when an emotion first arises, it has not moved far from the heart-mind, and its incipient impulse has only just stirred. Moreover, what moves it lies entirely within the encounters of one's own person, so keeping it within bounds is not difficult. This is precisely the point at which the learner differs only slightly from the sage, and it is what the Book of Changes calls “being moved.” If one keeps emotion within bounds at this point, one distinguishes it early and has not far to return. Thus, whenever emotions arise, they may all accord with their proper measure without awaiting forcible restraint or strenuous efforts at recovery. Hence one rejoices because something warrants joy, and becomes angry because something warrants anger. Grief does not reach the point of harm, nor fear the point of being overwhelmed. One does not become partial toward those one loves, prejudiced against those one despises, or biased toward what one admires and covets.

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
物之交於我也猶萬物聚散於太虛而氷之凝
釋於水也我之應乎物也猶鑑之空而無妍媸
也衡之平而無輕重也已發之和即未發之中
物來順應之妙即廓然太公之體無內外無將
迎合動靜兼體用其去聖人之道也夫何遠哉
惟不致慎於此或待其既發而後禁之失之既
遠而後復之情既蕩矣而後求所以約其情性
既鑿矣而後求所以養其性又其下者或求之
於威儀焉或求之於文辭焉或求之於詩書六
===
藝焉安於氣稟之性而無矯正擴充之功竊聖
人之近似而不得其精微之妙乃曰學之道盡
矣聖人之道在是矣聖人之道豈止於是哉嗚
呼聖人所以為聖人者固不外乎道而其所以
為道者亦何嘗外于心也故曰太和所謂道又
曰動而正曰道所謂和者自吾心發皆中節無
所乖戾者言之也所謂正者自吾心至正明達
無所偏倚者言之也苟無治心之功而用情之
際或乖而弗和或偏而匪正則我之所以為喜
punctuated: 物之交於我也，猶萬物聚散於太虛，而氷之凝釋於水也。我之應乎物也，猶鑑之空而無妍媸也，衡之平而無輕重也。已發之和，即未發之中；物來順應之妙，即廓然太公之體。無內外，無將迎，合動靜，兼體用，其去聖人之道也，夫何遠哉！惟不致慎於此，或待其既發而後禁之，失之既遠而後復之，情既蕩矣而後求所以約其情，性既鑿矣而後求所以養其性。又其下者，或求之於威儀焉，或求之於文辭焉，或求之於詩書六藝焉，安於氣稟之性，而無矯正擴充之功，竊聖人之近似，而不得其精微之妙，乃曰：「學之道盡矣，聖人之道在是矣。」聖人之道豈止於是哉！嗚呼！聖人所以為聖人者，固不外乎道，而其所以為道者，亦何嘗外于心也？故曰：「太和所謂道。」又曰：「動而正曰道。」所謂和者，自吾心發皆中節、無所乖戾者言之也；所謂正者，自吾心至正明達、無所偏倚者言之也。苟無治心之功，而用情之際，或乖而弗和，或偏而匪正，則我之所以為喜
translation_en:
Things coming into contact with me are like the myriad things gathering and dispersing in the Great Void, or ice forming and melting in water. My response to things is like a mirror’s emptiness, containing neither beauty nor ugliness, or a balance’s equilibrium, containing neither lightness nor heaviness. Harmony after the feelings have arisen is precisely the equilibrium before they arise; the subtle efficacy of responding appropriately as things come is precisely the substance of expansive impartiality [?]. There is no division between inner and outer, no anticipation or lingering attachment; activity and stillness are united, and substance and function are both encompassed. How far could this be from the Way of the sage?

Yet if one fails to exercise care here, one may wait until feelings have already arisen before restraining them, or until one has strayed far before returning. Only after the feelings have run wild does one seek a means of restraining them; only after one’s nature has been mutilated does one seek a means of nourishing it. Those at a still lower level may seek it in dignified comportment, in literary expression, or in the Odes, the Documents, and the Six Arts. Content with the nature endowed by their material constitution, they make no effort to correct it or to extend and develop it. They appropriate a semblance of the sage without grasping his subtle profundity, yet declare: “The way of learning is exhausted in this; the Way of the sage lies here.” Can the Way of the sage extend only this far?

Alas! What makes a sage a sage assuredly lies nowhere outside the Way; and how has that which constitutes the Way ever lain outside the heart-mind? Thus it is said: “Supreme harmony is what is called the Way.” It is also said: “To act and be correct is called the Way.” What is called harmony refers to everything issuing from my heart-mind attaining its proper measure, with nothing discordant. What is called correctness refers to my heart-mind being utterly correct, clear, and perceptive, without any bias or inclination. If one has done no work to govern the heart-mind, and in expressing feelings is sometimes discordant rather than harmonious, or biased rather than correct, then that by which I feel joy…

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
為怒為哀為懼為愛惡與欲者皆一人之私也
人將弗以為是而弗之由矣非天下之共由而
可以謂之天下之達道乎非天下之達道而可
以謂之聖人之道乎非聖人之道而可以謂之
學乎故曰學以至乎聖人之道蓋言治心也然
是心也又豈可以易治哉理之具者有萬殊焉
事之應者有萬變焉吉凶悔吝寓於紛綸交錯
之中而善惡之幾誠僞之辨天人之介差之乎
毫釐而謬之乎千里有不容以易察者故虞廷
===
授受以惟精為先而大學之教亦以格致為始
樂堯舜之道而獨得孔子之宗顏氏之子其殆
庶幾乎故孔子稱之曰回之為人擇乎中庸又
曰有不善未嘗弗知夫其擇之明則可與精義
也知之早則可與研幾也是以克復之目請事
之而無疑而過之不貳也怒之不遷也皆由於
至明有以察其幾故健以決之而其情自約於
中耳程子亦曰先明諸心知所往而後力行以
求其至嗚呼盡之矣然則學顏子之所學以求
punctuated:
為怒、為哀、為懼、為愛惡與欲者，皆一人之私也。人將弗以為是而弗之由矣。非天下之共由，而可以謂之天下之達道乎？非天下之達道，而可以謂之聖人之道乎？非聖人之道，而可以謂之學乎？故曰：「學以至乎聖人之道。」蓋言治心也。
然是心也，又豈可以易治哉？理之具者有萬殊焉，事之應者有萬變焉。吉凶悔吝寓於紛綸交錯之中，而善惡之幾、誠僞之辨、天人之介，差之乎毫釐而謬之乎千里，有不容以易察者。故虞廷授受，以惟精為先，而《大學》之教亦以格致為始。
樂堯舜之道而獨得孔子之宗，顏氏之子其殆庶幾乎？故孔子稱之曰：「回之為人，擇乎中庸。」又曰：「有不善，未嘗弗知。」夫其擇之明，則可與精義也；知之早，則可與研幾也。是以克復之目，請事之而無疑，而過之不貳也，怒之不遷也，皆由於至明有以察其幾，故健以決之，而其情自約於中耳。程子亦曰：「先明諸心，知所往，而後力行以求其至。」嗚呼！盡之矣！然則學顏子之所學以求
translation_en:
…anger, sorrow, fear, love, hate, and desire are all merely one person's selfish impulses. Others will not regard them as right and will not follow them. If this is not what all under Heaven follow in common, can it be called the universally applicable Way of all under Heaven? If it is not that universally applicable Way, can it be called the Way of the sages? If it is not the Way of the sages, can it be called learning? Thus the saying, “Learning is for attaining the Way of the sages,” speaks, in essence, of governing the mind.
Yet how could this mind be easy to govern? The principles it contains have myriad distinctions, and the affairs to which it responds undergo myriad changes. Good fortune, misfortune, regret, and humiliation lie amid this tangled interplay. In the incipient stirrings of good and evil, the distinction between sincerity and falsity, and the boundary between Heaven and the human, a discrepancy of a hair's breadth leads to an error of a thousand miles. These are things that cannot readily be discerned. Thus, in the transmission at the court of Yu, refinement of discernment came first; likewise, the teaching of the Great Learning begins with investigating things and extending knowledge.
Delighting in the Way of Yao and Shun and uniquely grasping the essential teaching of Confucius—was not the son of the Yan family close to this? Thus Confucius praised him, saying, “Hui, as a person, chooses the Mean.” He also said, “Whenever there was anything in him that was not good, he never failed to know it.” Because his choices were clear-sighted, he was capable of refining his understanding of what is right; because his awareness came early, he was capable of probing the first stirrings. Hence, when given the particulars of overcoming the self and returning to ritual propriety, he asked to put them into practice without hesitation. His never repeating a fault and never transferring his anger to others both arose from the utmost clarity with which he discerned those first stirrings. He therefore acted with strength and resolution, and his feelings naturally remained within the bounds of the Mean. Master Cheng also said, “First clarify it in the mind and know where to proceed; then exert yourself in practice to seek full attainment.” Ah! This says it all! Thus, to learn what Master Yan learned, in order to seek…

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
至乎聖人之道者必自致知始
表
擬宋以呂公著爲尚書右僕射謝表〔元祐元年〕
張鵬〔翰 幹〕
同考試官教諭林　批〔叙事有矩度發出呂公著忠愛之意造語精切文采蔚然傑作也〕
考試官教諭袁　批〔麗則與之佳者〕
考試官教諭顧　批〔駢麗典雅得臣子忠君體〕
===
元祐元年月日臣公著伏蒙
聖恩以臣爲尚書右僕射者伏以
天臺宥密
九重依咫尺之光
斗極崇高百辟倚鈞衡之重忽
三命之滋被顧四辭之未從人以爲榮臣則知
懼臣公著誠惶誠恐稽首頓首上言竊惟
尚書喉舌之職僕射丞弼之司糸攝百官
協宣庶績必有九德之並茂乃副兩府之
punctuated:
至乎聖人之道者，必自致知始。

表
擬宋以呂公著爲尚書右僕射謝表〔元祐元年〕
張鵬〔翰 幹〕
同考試官教諭林批〔叙事有矩度，發出呂公著忠愛之意，造語精切，文采蔚然，傑作也。〕
考試官教諭袁批〔麗則與之，佳者。〕
考試官教諭顧批〔駢麗典雅，得臣子忠君體。〕

元祐元年月日，臣公著伏蒙聖恩，以臣爲尚書右僕射者。伏以天臺宥密，九重依咫尺之光；斗極崇高，百辟倚鈞衡之重。忽三命之滋被，顧四辭之未從。人以爲榮，臣則知懼。臣公著誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首上言：竊惟尚書，喉舌之職；僕射，丞弼之司。糸攝百官，協宣庶績，必有九德之並茂，乃副兩府之
translation_en:
…those who would attain the Way of the sages must begin by extending their knowledge.

Memorial
A model memorial of thanks on the Song appointment of Lü Gongzhu as Vice Director of the Right of the Department of State Affairs [First year of Yuanyou (1086)].
By Zhang Peng [Han; Gan—annotation unclear [?]].
Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: [The narration is well ordered and brings out Lü Gongzhu’s loyalty and devotion. The phrasing is precise and apt, and the literary brilliance abundant. A masterly work.]
Examiner Yuan, Instructor, comments: [For elegance, I grant it approval: a fine piece.]
Examiner Gu, Instructor, comments: [Its parallel prose is elegant, classical, and refined, aptly expressing a subject’s loyalty to his sovereign.]

On this day and month in the first year of Yuanyou, your servant Gongzhu has humbly received your sagely favor appointing him Vice Director of the Right of the Department of State Affairs. I humbly reflect that the celestial terrace is profound and tranquil: within the ninefold palace, one draws upon your radiance close at hand. The Northern Dipper and the Pole Star stand lofty and exalted: the assembled officials rely upon the weighty authority that holds the balance of government. Suddenly, the favor of three successive commands has been bestowed upon me, while my four refusals have not been accepted. Others regard this as an honor; your servant knows only apprehension. Your servant Gongzhu, truly fearful and truly apprehensive, bows his head and knocks it upon the ground, submitting these words:

I venture to reflect that the Department of State Affairs serves as the sovereign’s throat and tongue, while its Vice Director holds an office of assistance and support. To oversee [?] the hundred officials and jointly bring all undertakings to fruition, one must possess all nine virtues in full measure; only then can one meet the expectations placed upon the Two Administrations …

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
具瞻歷稽前聞兼重其任納言愼始龍熙
舜采以亮虞功周德相終尹昭夏車而存
殷監自仲虺而後及君奭以來道或讓於
濟川業多虧於補袞聽華覆而獻牘僅標
譽於鄭子游排桂闥而停刑幸霽威於鍾
離意闢建禮以疇洛元俊誤擭雙龍策明
經而翼賛化機偶協三鱣然黼藻之治非
無可觀究啓沃之功竟亦何益仰惟
重熙之代益優六符之臣睠此崇階宜歸碩
===
彥豈謂桑榆暮景謬膺
綸綍新榮伏念〔臣公著〕學不足以澡身才未能
以經世猥懲
異數洊歷清華
仁廟察其朴忠
睿旨旌夫恬退慶曆之始懋承
龍渥於崇文嘉祐之中繼濫
鴻慈於待制嘗
英皇之嗣服重忤濮議而遂左遷逮
punctuated:
具瞻。歷稽前聞，兼重其任。納言愼始，龍熙舜采以亮虞功；周德相終，尹昭夏車而存殷監。自仲虺而後，及君奭以來，道或讓於濟川，業多虧於補袞。聽華覆而獻牘，僅標譽於鄭子游；排桂闥而停刑，幸霽威於鍾離意。闢建禮以疇洛元俊，誤擭雙龍；策明經而翼賛化機，偶協三鱣。然黼藻之治，非無可觀；究啓沃之功，竟亦何益？仰惟重熙之代，益優六符之臣。睠此崇階，宜歸碩彥。豈謂桑榆暮景，謬膺綸綍新榮！

伏念〔臣公著〕學不足以澡身，才未能以經世。猥懲異數，洊歷清華。仁廟察其朴忠，睿旨旌夫恬退。慶曆之始，懋承龍渥於崇文；嘉祐之中，繼濫鴻慈於待制。嘗英皇之嗣服，重忤濮議而遂左遷。逮
translation_en:
…the focus of all eyes. Examining the accounts of earlier times, I find that this responsibility has always carried exceptional weight. In receiving words, care was taken at the outset: Long brought lustre to Shun’s affairs and assisted the achievements of Yu. Zhou’s virtue was assisted to its culmination; Yin made manifest the Xia carriage [?] and preserved the warning furnished by Yin. From Zhonghui onward, and since Lord Shi, their adherence to the Way sometimes fell short of the ideal of helping the ruler cross a river, and their accomplishments often proved deficient in mending the royal robe—that is, correcting the ruler’s faults. Hearing of the overturned canopy [?], Zheng Ziyou presented a written remonstrance and gained some renown; pushing through the cassia gates to halt a punishment, Zhongli Yi fortunately succeeded in calming imperial wrath. Opening Jianli Gate to consult Luo Yuanjun [?], one mistakenly caught two dragons; examining candidates versed in the Classics to assist the workings of transformation, one happened to fulfil the portent of three large bream. Yet although such embellishments of government were not without merit, what benefit did they ultimately bring to the work of enlightening and nourishing the sovereign’s mind?

I reverently reflect that, in this age of accumulated splendour, exceptional favour is bestowed upon ministers corresponding to the Six Talismans in the heavens. Such an exalted rank should surely belong to men of outstanding worth. Who could have imagined that, in the evening twilight of my life, I would undeservedly receive this new honour through an imperial pronouncement!

I humbly consider that 〔your servant Gongzhu’s〕 learning is insufficient to purify his person, and his abilities inadequate to order the world. Undeservedly receiving [?] exceptional distinctions, I have successively held prestigious posts. Renzong discerned my plain sincerity and loyalty, and his sagacious command commended my quiet, retiring disposition. At the beginning of the Qingli era, I received abundant imperial favour at the Chongwen Academy; during the Jiayou era, I again undeservedly received his great kindness through appointment as an Auxiliary Academician. When Emperor Yingzong succeeded to the throne, I gravely incurred displeasure over the deliberations concerning the Prince of Pu and was consequently demoted. When…

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
神考之承祧力排新法而復外補衆言交譖以
為立異而干譽
清聽獨聰知其盡職而無罪河陽再入孤憤益
揚恥嬋媛之為容奮慨慷而議政銀臺罷
奏至決去留以正
朝綱彤管直書首辨直邪而應
明制昌陳十事罄竭寸忱内外出入者廿年顛
沛艱辛者六郡尚覺丹心之未沒自甘白
首以為期惟思上士之與齊詎意中臺而
===
寵憂深據蕨愧切循牆茲蓋伏遇
淵
睿啓冲年
德凝上智
赤光虎變夙昭
元聖之眞符
紫極龍飛茂協
重華之景運覲
punctuated:
神考之承祧，力排新法而復外補。衆言交譖，以為立異而干譽；清聽獨聰，知其盡職而無罪。河陽再入，孤憤益揚，恥嬋媛之為容，奮慨慷而議政。銀臺罷奏，至決去留以正朝綱；彤管直書，首辨直邪而應明制。昌陳十事，罄竭寸忱。内外出入者廿年，顛沛艱辛者六郡。尚覺丹心之未沒，自甘白首以為期。惟思上士之與齊，詎意中臺而寵！憂深據蕨，愧切循牆。
茲蓋伏遇淵睿啓冲年，德凝上智。赤光虎變，夙昭元聖之眞符；紫極龍飛，茂協重華之景運。覲
translation_en:
…when the late Emperor Shenzong succeeded to the ancestral throne, I vigorously opposed the New Policies and was again assigned to an outside post. Many voices joined in slandering me, claiming that I sought distinction through dissent and courted renown. Your discerning imperial hearing alone understood that I had discharged my duties and committed no offense. Returning once more to court from Heyang, I expressed my solitary indignation still more forcefully. Ashamed to assume a fawning manner, I discussed government with impassioned resolve. In my memorial concerning the abolition of the Silver Terrace office [?], I went so far as to stake my remaining in office or leaving upon the rectification of court discipline. Writing candidly with the vermilion brush, I first distinguished the upright from the wicked in response to the enlightened imperial command. I openly set forth ten matters, exhausting my humble sincerity. For twenty years I passed between court and provincial service; in six prefectures I endured hardship and adversity. Still conscious that my loyal heart had not perished, I willingly pledged myself to service into white-haired old age. I thought only of equaling men of superior worth; how could I have expected favor in the central administration! My anxiety is profound, as though resting upon ferns [?]; my shame is keen, so that I walk close against the wall in deference.
This is because I have humbly encountered Your Majesty, whose profound sagacity unfolded in tender youth and whose virtue embodies the highest wisdom. The red radiance and the tiger’s transformation early revealed the true portents of a supreme sage; the dragon’s ascent at the Purple Pole auspiciously accorded with the glorious destiny of Chonghua, the sage Shun. Beholding…

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
耿光於
六聖洽
大孝於
重闈乃知
帝王自有眞五色麗卿雲之彩會見
中和之兼備三階泫甘露之精
復賢良方正科讜論日聞乎格
心逆耳
罷老莊申韓學邪說遂息於畔道離經
===
孔庭爼豆孟顏周禮盡在是
魏闕羹牆堯舜
王道亦如斯
閔農祈雨於南郊瑞應
王綸之發
貴德却獅於西域
功深銅柱之標
蠲賦賑荒遐壤喜
一人能養掩骸減罪窮民歌四海多仁
punctuated: 耿光於六聖，洽大孝於重闈。乃知帝王自有眞，五色麗卿雲之彩；會見中和之兼備，三階泫甘露之精。復賢良方正科，讜論日聞乎格心逆耳；罷老莊申韓學，邪說遂息於畔道離經。孔庭爼豆，孟顏周禮盡在是；魏闕羹牆，堯舜王道亦如斯。閔農祈雨於南郊，瑞應王綸之發；貴德却獅於西域，功深銅柱之標。蠲賦賑荒，遐壤喜一人能養；掩骸減罪，窮民歌四海多仁。
translation_en: …the radiant glory of the six sagely predecessors, extending your great filial devotion throughout the inner palaces. Thus we know that an emperor possesses true worth: the five colors shine in the hues of auspicious clouds. We shall witness centrality and harmony fully realized, as the Three Steps constellation drips the essence of sweet dew. You restored the examination category for the Worthy, Good, Upright, and Correct; frank counsel, grating upon the ear yet rectifying the sovereign’s heart, is heard daily. You abolished the teachings of Laozi, Zhuangzi, Shen Buhai, and Han Fei; heterodox doctrines that depart from the Way and forsake the Classics consequently fell silent. In the court of Confucius, amid the ritual vessels, Mengzi, Yan Hui, and the rites of Zhou are all present here [?]. At the palace gates, as in the remembrance of sages evoked by soup and walls, the kingly Way of Yao and Shun is likewise manifest. Pitying the farmers, you prayed for rain at the southern suburban altar; an auspicious response followed the issuing of your royal decree. Esteeming virtue, you declined lions from the Western Regions; your achievement surpassed that commemorated by the bronze pillars. You remitted taxes and relieved famine, and distant lands rejoiced that the One Man could sustain them. You buried exposed remains and mitigated punishments, and impoverished people sang of the abundant benevolence throughout the Four Seas.

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
當五始謹求更化之端
簡三公用寄調元之任人維求舊治與圖新
尚有典刑慨前魚之盡棄
博延耆耇幸老馬之猶存
白麻驚
睿藻煇煌蒼玉恍
恩波流動遭逢一旦度越諸臣〔臣公著〕敢不益
勵初心求堅晚節理治繩以甦民命不競
不絿調
===
===
化鼎以解時癥無偏無黨西戎之兩議未決
羞虛名徒動乎不庭免役之五害尚行誓
微躬罔生於
明世故寧蹇諤訐切危身而拂衆不忍浮沉依
違悅人而誑
君上期謨明
國體以凝百工下思鑒別人材以愜羣望克
副承家之孝庶幾報
主之忠伏願
punctuated: 當五始，謹求更化之端；簡三公，用寄調元之任。人維求舊，治與圖新。尚有典刑，慨前魚之盡棄；博延耆耇，幸老馬之猶存。白麻驚睿藻煇煌，蒼玉恍恩波流動。遭逢一旦，度越諸臣。〔臣公著〕敢不益勵初心，求堅晚節？理治繩以甦民命，不競不絿；調化鼎以解時癥，無偏無黨。西戎之兩議未決，羞虛名徒動乎不庭；免役之五害尚行，誓微躬罔生於明世。故寧蹇諤訐切，危身而拂衆，不忍浮沉依違，悅人而誑君。上期謨明國體以凝百工，下思鑒別人材以愜羣望。克副承家之孝，庶幾報主之忠。伏願
translation_en: At the conjunction of the five beginnings, You have carefully sought a starting point for reform; You have selected the Three Dukes to entrust them with harmonizing the primal forces. In choosing men, seek those long tried; in governing, plan for renewal. Established models still remain: You lament that the earlier fish have all been discarded—the old servants cast aside. You have broadly summoned the aged and experienced, rejoicing that old horses still survive. On the white hemp-paper edict, Your brilliant imperial composition dazzles; upon the blue-green jade insignia, the waves of Your favor seem to flow. In a single day I have received this fortunate appointment, surpassing my fellow ministers. 〔Your servant Gongzhu〕 How could I fail to redouble my original resolve and seek steadfast integrity in my later years? I shall put the cords of government in order to revive the people’s livelihoods, neither forceful nor lax; I shall regulate the cauldron of transformation to remedy the maladies of the age, without partiality or faction. The two proposals concerning the western Rong remain undecided; I am ashamed that empty renown merely stirs those who refuse allegiance. The five harmful effects of the service-exemption system still persist; I vow that my humble person shall not live on in this enlightened age while they endure. Thus I would rather speak with unbending frankness and piercing directness, endangering myself and offending the multitude, than drift with the current and equivocate, pleasing others while deceiving my sovereign. Above, I hope to deliberate with clear understanding of the principles of state and thereby bring cohesion to the officials; below, I intend to distinguish men of talent and thus satisfy the expectations of all. By fulfilling the filial duty of carrying on my family’s legacy, I may hope to repay my sovereign with loyalty. I humbly wish that …

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
定保慎微
宅中圖大
一德交孚於上下幹蠱譽以成紹述之隆休
六學念典於始終核泰茅以廣粹精之大化
禮樂明而天地治
車書混而人物熙
祚頌日升月恒篤萬年丕丕之緒
治歌星輝海潤迓四方穆穆之衡臣無任瞻
天仰
===
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叄場
策
第一問
薛一鶚
同考試官學正黎 批 法祖敬天帝王治天下之道莫
punctuated:
定保慎微，宅中圖大。一德交孚於上下，幹蠱譽以成紹述之隆休；六學念典於始終，核泰茅以廣粹精之大化。禮樂明而天地治，車書混而人物熙。祚頌日升月恒，篤萬年丕丕之緒；治歌星輝海潤，迓四方穆穆之衡。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第叄場
策
第一問
薛一鶚
同考試官學正黎批：「法祖敬天，帝王治天下之道莫
translation_en:
…secure stability through vigilance over the smallest matters, and occupy the center while planning great undertakings. May a single virtue inspire mutual trust between those above and below, and may the praise earned by remedying inherited disorders bring the continuation of ancestral achievements to glorious fulfillment. May the six branches of learning keep the canons in mind from beginning to end [?], and may examination of the linked grass roots of the hexagram Peace [?] extend the great transforming influence of purest excellence. May rites and music shine forth, bringing order to Heaven and Earth; may carriage gauges and written script be unified, bringing flourishing to people and all things. May blessings be celebrated as the rising sun and waxing moon, strengthening the ever-growing legacy for ten thousand years; may good government be praised as the radiance of stars and the beneficent moisture of the seas, welcoming reverent harmony throughout the four quarters. Your servant, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Majesty, cannot contain his intense emotion and utmost trembling awe. I respectfully present this memorial to convey my thanks for Your Majesty’s hearing.
Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Xue Yi’e
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, School Instructor: “To emulate the ancestors and revere Heaven—among the principles by which emperors and kings govern All under Heaven, none…”

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
要於此而其本在於敬一子能根究而揄揚哉
聖祖
皇上之謨烈條答明盡非三晉之奇士耶
考試官教諭袁　批　敬天法祖爲祈天永命之本此
篇究極而揚厲
國家創守之盛其涵泳
聖化而有得者耶
考試官教諭顧　批　垂創宏規後守要道自古帝王
未有盛於我
===
皇祖
皇上者子能揄揚精詳而識其大旨可與言心學矣
大哉敬乎所以達于上下而妙乎感通之
機者也所以相爲後先而裕乎創守之道
者也其本存于一心而昭格之極則可以
先天而弗違其道豫于一時而垂裕之遠
則足以俟後而不惑其天人統會之樞而
千聖相傳之心法乎是故以此敬迓則大
命可集也休命可順也明命可承也哲命
punctuated:
要於此，而其本在於敬一。子能根究而揄揚哉聖祖皇上之謨烈，條答明盡，非三晉之奇士耶？

考試官教諭袁，批：敬天法祖爲祈天永命之本。此篇究極而揚厲國家創守之盛，其涵泳聖化而有得者耶？

考試官教諭顧，批：垂創宏規，後守要道，自古帝王未有盛於我皇祖皇上者。子能揄揚精詳而識其大旨，可與言心學矣。

大哉，敬乎！所以達于上下而妙乎感通之機者也，所以相爲後先而裕乎創守之道者也。其本存于一心，而昭格之極，則可以先天而弗違；其道豫于一時，而垂裕之遠，則足以俟後而不惑。其天人統會之樞，而千聖相傳之心法乎！是故以此敬迓，則大命可集也，休命可順也，明命可承也，哲命
translation_en:
…nothing is more essential than this, and its foundation lies in reverent single-mindedness. You have traced matters to their roots and extolled the plans and achievements of the sagely founder and His Majesty [?]; your answers, point by point, are clear and thorough. Are you not an exceptional scholar of the Three Jin regions?

Examiner Yuan, Instructor, comments: Revering Heaven and emulating the ancestors are the foundation for praying to Heaven for an enduring mandate. This essay explores the subject fully and eloquently celebrates the dynasty’s flourishing achievement in founding and preserving its rule. Surely its author has immersed himself in the sage ruler’s transforming influence and gained something from it?

Examiner Gu, Instructor, comments: In the grand design bequeathed at the founding and the essential way of preserving it thereafter, no emperors or kings since antiquity have surpassed our imperial ancestor and His Majesty. You have praised their achievements with precision and detail and grasped their central meaning. You are someone with whom one may discuss the learning of the mind.

Great indeed is reverence! Through it, communication reaches above and below, and the workings of mutual response operate wondrously. Through it, predecessors and successors complement one another, enriching the way of founding and preserving rule. Its foundation resides in the individual mind; yet, at the utmost reach of its manifest communion with Heaven, one may precede Heaven without contravening it. Its way is prepared in one age; yet the benefits it bequeaths extend so far that one may await later ages without doubt. Is it not the pivot that unites Heaven and humanity, and the teaching of the mind transmitted from sage to sage through the ages? Thus, when one reverently welcomes Heaven’s mandate, the great mandate may be gathered in, the gracious mandate followed, the luminous mandate received, and the wise mandate…

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
可貽也而天心其克享矣以此敬承則世
德可求也舊章可由也大法可循也典常
可師也而帝德其罔愆矣然統而論之仁
不違乎帝卽孝不違乎親也孝子之所以
事親者卽仁人之所以享帝者也其道有
二乎哉知此則古之帝王所以克享丕式
之道我
祖宗之
懿謨鴻範曁我
===
皇上所以纘承而時敘者可得而對揚其略矣
今夫人君之有天下也孰與之曰天與之
故位曰天位祿曰天祿賞曰天命罰曰天
討而槩謂之曰天子焉所以明有尊也其
土地人民孰自而有焉曰傳之先君也故
德曰世德功曰世功澤曰世澤臣曰世臣
而槩謂之曰世守焉所以明有始也天之
於君也寵綏既隆則敬之也自不容於不
至祖宗之於我也投遺者既艱且大則所
punctuated:
可貽也，而天心其克享矣。以此敬承，則世德可求也，舊章可由也，大法可循也，典常可師也，而帝德其罔愆矣。然統而論之，仁不違乎帝，卽孝不違乎親也。孝子之所以事親者，卽仁人之所以享帝者也。其道有二乎哉？知此，則古之帝王所以克享丕式之道，我祖宗之懿謨鴻範，曁我皇上所以纘承而時敘者，可得而對揚其略矣。
今夫人君之有天下也，孰與之？曰：天與之。故位曰天位，祿曰天祿，賞曰天命，罰曰天討，而槩謂之曰天子焉，所以明有尊也。其土地人民，孰自而有焉？曰：傳之先君也。故德曰世德，功曰世功，澤曰世澤，臣曰世臣，而槩謂之曰世守焉，所以明有始也。天之於君也，寵綏既隆，則敬之也自不容於不至。祖宗之於我也，投遺者既艱且大，則所
translation_en:
…may be bequeathed, and Heaven's heart will accept it. By reverently carrying on in this way, one can pursue ancestral virtue, follow established institutions, adhere to the great laws, and take enduring norms as one's model; thus imperial virtue will be without fault. Yet, considered as a whole, benevolence that does not depart from the will of the Lord on High is precisely filial devotion that does not depart from the will of one's parents. The means by which a filial son serves his parents are precisely those by which a benevolent person makes offerings to the Lord on High. Could these be two different Ways? Understanding this, we can set forth in praise an outline of the Way by which the ancient emperors and kings gained divine acceptance and furnished great models, of our imperial ancestors' excellent counsels and grand patterns, and of how our present Emperor continues their legacy and orders it according to the times.
Now, when a ruler possesses all under Heaven, who gives it to him? The answer is: Heaven gives it to him. Thus his position is called Heaven's position; his emolument, Heaven's emolument; his rewards, Heaven's commands; and his punishments, Heaven's chastisements. He himself is comprehensively designated the Son of Heaven, making clear that there is one above him whom he must revere. From whom does he obtain his lands and people? The answer is: they are transmitted from former rulers. Thus his virtue is called ancestral virtue; his achievements, ancestral achievements; his beneficence, ancestral beneficence; and his ministers, hereditary ministers. All this is comprehensively described as an inheritance guarded through the generations, making clear that it has an origin. Since Heaven's favor and protection of the ruler are so abundant, his reverence for Heaven must necessarily be utmost. Since what our imperial ancestors handed down to us was both hard-won and immense, then the means by which…

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
以仰副其燕翼之心者又豈可以或緩也
哉是故堯之欽若昊天也舜之勑天之命
也湯之欽崇天道也文王之昭事上帝也
事天不同而同於仁也而要其本則兢兢
業業昭假緝熙而聖人之所以求天於心
者固已至矣若夫詩書不事者因還沛而
作大風之歌播遷引咎者因天變而下改
元之詔偏安南渡者因有感而作敬天之
圖是皆無得於克享之實也而可以同日
===
語哉太甲之率祖攸行也高宗之監于成
憲也武王之繼志述事也成王之覲光揚
烈也法祖不同而同於孝也而要其本則
懋德時憲敬勝光明而諸君所以求祖宗
于心者固已素矣若夫內多慾而不能恭
儉者乃謂述文帝之故事泪羣議而明斷
不終者乃謂讀貞觀之政要治黨籍而大
索元氣者乃謂遵熙豐之遺志是皆無得
於丕式之實也而可以一致論哉洪惟我
punctuated:
以仰副其燕翼之心者，又豈可以或緩也哉？是故堯之欽若昊天也，舜之勑天之命也，湯之欽崇天道也，文王之昭事上帝也，事天不同而同於仁也。而要其本，則兢兢業業、昭假緝熙，而聖人之所以求天於心者，固已至矣。若夫詩書不事者，因還沛而作大風之歌；播遷引咎者，因天變而下改元之詔；偏安南渡者，因有感而作敬天之圖：是皆無得於克享之實也，而可以同日語哉？

太甲之率祖攸行也，高宗之監于成憲也，武王之繼志述事也，成王之覲光揚烈也，法祖不同而同於孝也。而要其本，則懋德時憲、敬勝光明，而諸君所以求祖宗于心者，固已素矣。若夫內多慾而不能恭儉者，乃謂述文帝之故事；泪羣議而明斷不終者，乃謂讀貞觀之政要；治黨籍而大索元氣者，乃謂遵熙豐之遺志：是皆無得於丕式之實也，而可以一致論哉？洪惟我
translation_en:
… how, then, could one ever slacken in fulfilling their intention to provide for their descendants? Thus Yao reverently followed August Heaven; Shun diligently attended to Heaven’s mandate; Tang reverently honored the Way of Heaven; and King Wen luminously served the Lord on High. Their ways of serving Heaven differed, but they shared the same benevolence. At their root lay vigilant reverence, radiant spiritual communion, and sustained illumination: the sages had indeed brought their search for Heaven within their own hearts to perfection. By contrast, one ruler who neglected the Odes and Documents composed the Song of the Great Wind upon returning to Pei; another, driven into exile and acknowledging his faults, issued an edict changing the reign title in response to a celestial portent; and another, who crossed south and settled for restricted dominion, was moved to compose a Diagram of Reverence for Heaven. None of these grasped the substance of serving Heaven acceptably. How could they be spoken of in the same breath as the sages?

Tai Jia followed the conduct of his ancestor; Gaozong took established statutes as his mirror; King Wu carried forward his predecessor’s intentions and undertakings; and King Cheng beheld his predecessors’ glory and proclaimed their achievements. Their ways of modeling themselves on their ancestors differed, but they shared the same filial piety. At their root lay vigorous cultivation of virtue and emulation of it, and the brilliance attained when reverence prevails: these rulers had long been grounded in seeking their ancestors within their own hearts. By contrast, one ruler, inwardly full of desires and unable to practice reverence and frugality, nevertheless claimed to perpetuate Emperor Wen’s precedents; another, swayed by the many opinions [?] and unable to remain clear and decisive to the end, nevertheless claimed to read the Essentials of Government of the Zhenguan Reign; and another, who maintained registers of political factions and gravely depleted the realm’s vital energies, nevertheless claimed to follow the intentions bequeathed by the Xining and Yuanfeng reigns. None of these grasped the substance of fully following ancestral models. How could they be judged on the same footing? We reverently reflect upon our …

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
太祖高皇帝聰明本于天縱
聖學益于日新其敬
天也
帝命已不違矣而所以基命者爲益密
天心已允合矣而所以畏天者爲愈誠觀其
諭博士許存仁曰天道微妙難知人事感通易
見天人一理必以類應
諭羣臣曰謹於修己誠以愛民庶可荅
天之眷此其抑畏之實祗若之誠揆之帝王其
===
心同也
仰觀俯察作
大明一統曆以立萬世常行之道焉分至啓閉
之宜盈虛朓朒之妙自有曆法以來未有
如是之精密者皇皇乎其敬授也哉其
詒謀也既以其一身而創乎丕顯丕承之業又
以其一心而立乎可久可大之規觀其
諭近臣曰日月之能久照萬世不改其明堯舜
之道不息萬世不改其行
punctuated:
太祖高皇帝聰明本于天縱，聖學益于日新。其敬天也，帝命已不違矣，而所以基命者爲益密；天心已允合矣，而所以畏天者爲愈誠。觀其諭博士許存仁曰：「天道微妙難知，人事感通易見。天人一理，必以類應。」諭羣臣曰：「謹於修己，誠以愛民，庶可荅天之眷。」此其抑畏之實、祗若之誠，揆之帝王，其心同也。
仰觀俯察，作《大明一統曆》，以立萬世常行之道焉。分至啓閉之宜，盈虛朓朒之妙，自有曆法以來，未有如是之精密者。皇皇乎其敬授也哉！其詒謀也，既以其一身而創乎丕顯丕承之業，又以其一心而立乎可久可大之規。觀其諭近臣曰：「日月之能久照，萬世不改其明；堯舜之道不息，萬世不改其行。」
translation_en:
…Emperor Taizu Gao possessed intelligence endowed by Heaven, and his sagely learning advanced through daily renewal. In his reverence for Heaven, he already accorded with the Supreme Lord’s mandate, yet became ever more meticulous in securing its foundations; he already fully accorded with Heaven’s mind, yet became ever more sincere in his awe of Heaven. Consider his admonition to the Erudite Xu Cunren: “Heaven’s Way is subtle and difficult to know; the workings of stimulus and response in human affairs are readily seen. Heaven and humanity share one principle and necessarily respond according to their kind.” He admonished his assembled ministers: “Be scrupulous in cultivating yourselves and sincere in loving the people; thus you may repay Heaven’s favor.” Such was the substance of his humility and awe, and the sincerity of his reverent compliance. Measured against the ancient emperors and kings, his mind was the same as theirs.
Observing above and examining below, he produced the Unified Calendar of the Great Ming, thereby establishing a system for constant use through ten thousand generations. In its proper determination of the equinoxes, solstices, and beginnings of the seasons, and its subtle treatment of waxing and waning and the moon’s advances and delays, nothing so precise had existed since calendrical methods began. How splendid was his reverent promulgation of the seasons! In laying plans for his descendants, he personally founded an enterprise that gloriously manifested and continued the inherited mandate, and through his own resolve established a framework capable of enduring and expanding. Consider his admonition to his close ministers: “The sun and moon can shine for so long because through ten thousand generations their brightness does not change; the Way of Yao and Shun never ceases because through ten thousand generations its operation does not change.” …

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
諭太子曰君道以事天愛民爲重其本在敬身
人君一言一行皆上通于天下繫于民必敬
以將之而後所行無不善也此其
燕翼之淵
鴻謨之遠揆之帝王其道一也而又
慮患防微作
皇明祖訓以爲萬世不刊之典焉紬繹歷夫六
年編謄至於七易自有謨訓以來未有如
是之周悉者洋洋乎其
===
聖謨也哉至我
成祖文皇帝製聖學心法以教
儲貳首以敬
天法
祖爲重是其心卽
高皇帝之心也我
宣宗章皇帝製帝訓以教
太子獨以奉
天尊
punctuated:
諭太子曰：「君道以事天愛民爲重，其本在敬身。人君一言一行，皆上通于天，下繫于民，必敬以將之，而後所行無不善也。」此其燕翼之淵、鴻謨之遠，揆之帝王，其道一也。而又慮患防微，作《皇明祖訓》，以爲萬世不刊之典焉。紬繹歷夫六年，編謄至於七易，自有謨訓以來，未有如是之周悉者。洋洋乎其聖謨也哉！
至我成祖文皇帝，製《聖學心法》以教儲貳，首以敬天法祖爲重，是其心卽高皇帝之心也。我宣宗章皇帝，製《帝訓》以教太子，獨以奉天尊
translation_en:
He instructed the heir apparent, saying: “The ruler’s way places foremost serving Heaven and loving the people; its foundation lies in maintaining reverence in one’s own conduct. Every word and deed of a ruler reaches upward to Heaven and bears upon the people below. He must guide them with reverence; only then will everything he does be good.” Such was the depth of his provision for his descendants and the far-reaching scope of his grand designs. Measured against the ancient emperors and kings, his way was one with theirs. Moreover, anticipating troubles and guarding against their slightest beginnings, he composed the Ancestral Instructions of the August Ming (Huang Ming zuxun) as an immutable canon for all ages. Its careful elaboration extended over six years, and its compilation and transcription underwent as many as seven revisions. Since the first sovereign counsels and instructions, none had been so comprehensive. How vast were his sagely counsels!
Coming down to our Emperor Chengzu Wen, he composed the Essential Methods of Sagely Learning (Shengxue xinfa) to instruct the heir apparent, placing foremost reverence for Heaven and emulation of the ancestors. His mind was thus the very mind of Emperor Gao. Our Emperor Xuanzong Zhang composed the Imperial Instructions (Dixun) to instruct the heir apparent, singling out the injunction to serve Heaven and honor …

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
祖爲言是其道郎
文皇帝之道也
神謨聖志符乎後先
睿藻奎章昭乎日月視諸唐虞之協帝重華文
武之稱德重光蓋媲美也至於我
皇上秉明聖之資
備帝王之道
兼創守之任
位天人之間
===
曰明日旦無一念而不對越乎
上帝
善繼善述無一事而不憲章乎
祖宗是故
圜丘特祀
皇穹躬享所以昭假者有素矣而又
親灑
宸翰以詔後世有
欽
punctuated:
祖爲言，是其道郎文皇帝之道也。神謨聖志，符乎後先；睿藻奎章，昭乎日月。視諸唐虞之協帝重華、文武之稱德重光，蓋媲美也。
至於我皇上，秉明聖之資，備帝王之道，兼創守之任，位天人之間。曰明日旦，無一念而不對越乎上帝；善繼善述，無一事而不憲章乎祖宗。是故圜丘特祀，皇穹躬享，所以昭假者有素矣。而又親灑宸翰，以詔後世，有欽
translation_en:
…and honoring the ancestors: these were his words. His Way was thus [?] the Way of Emperor Wen. Their divine counsels and sagely aspirations accorded across successive reigns; their imperial compositions and resplendent writings shone like the sun and moon. Compared with the sovereigns of Tang and Yu, whose accord brought successive brilliance, and Kings Wen and Wu, whose matching virtue brought successive radiance, they indeed rivaled them in excellence.
As for our present Emperor, he possesses an enlightened and sagely nature, embodies the Way of emperors and kings, combines the responsibilities of founding and preserving the dynasty, and stands between Heaven and humanity. In daily brightness and at each dawn [?], not a single thought fails reverently to attend the Lord on High. Skillfully continuing and carrying forward his predecessors’ work, he undertakes nothing without taking the imperial ancestors as his model. Thus he performs the special sacrifice at the Circular Mound and personally presents offerings to August Heaven; his means of manifesting sincerity and reaching the divine have long been established. Moreover, he personally wields the imperial brush to instruct later generations, producing a work entitled “Reverence …

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
天記頌之作焉
祇薦
宗祊以祈稼穡
敬獻
慈闈以祝遐齡
功惟歸
帝
善則稱
親三百
===
徽言數十
嚴韻
明禋備舉福祿竝綏渢渢乎其周人將享之
遺音乎
大祫毖祀
徽號隆稱所以尊崇者有素矣而又
躬製龍章以發潛蘊而有
祖德詩之和焉於
淳祖
punctuated:
天記頌之作焉，祇薦宗祊以祈稼穡，敬獻慈闈以祝遐齡。功惟歸帝，善則稱親。三百徽言，數十嚴韻，明禋備舉，福祿竝綏。渢渢乎，其周人將享之遺音乎！
大祫毖祀，徽號隆稱，所以尊崇者有素矣。而又躬製龍章，以發潛蘊，而有祖德詩之和焉。於淳祖
translation_en:
…the Record and Eulogy of Revering Heaven was composed. It was reverently presented at the ancestral temple to pray for harvests, and respectfully offered to the Empress Dowager to wish her long life. All achievement is attributed to the Supreme Deity, and all goodness credited to the imperial parent. Three hundred fine words and several dozen stately rhymes: the luminous sacrifices are fully performed, and blessings and emoluments alike bestowed. How majestic their sound! Are these not the lingering strains of the people of Zhou as they prepared to offer sacrifice?
The solemn observance of the grand combined ancestral sacrifice and the bestowal of exalted honorific titles had long manifested reverence for the ancestors. Moreover, His Majesty personally composed imperial verses to bring their hidden virtues to light, producing a matching composition to the Poem on Ancestral Virtue. With regard to Chunzu…

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
太祖
成祖
仁皇既茂揚
德業以溢其傳於
章皇
睿皇
純皇
敬皇
毅皇又特爲詩歌以紀其盛
===
九章之和
章皇頌述之志益光
五章之作
五聖功烈之休愈顯穆穆乎其商人濬哲之頌
聲乎
皇墳帝典鏗鍧而彪炳
河圖洛範玉振而金聲天下仰而頌之者蓋
不能擬諸形容而罄其揄揚也執事乃欲
求
punctuated: 太祖、成祖、仁皇，既茂揚德業，以溢其傳；於章皇、睿皇、純皇、敬皇、毅皇，又特爲詩歌，以紀其盛。九章之和，章皇頌述之志益光；五章之作，五聖功烈之休愈顯。穆穆乎，其商人濬哲之頌聲乎！皇墳帝典，鏗鍧而彪炳；河圖洛範，玉振而金聲。天下仰而頌之者，蓋不能擬諸形容而罄其揄揚也。執事乃欲求
translation_en:
…Taizu, Chengzu, and Emperor Ren: you have already splendidly extolled their virtue and achievements, enriching their transmitted legacy. For Emperors Zhang, Rui, Chun, Jing, and Yi, you have further composed poems expressly to record their grandeur. Through the matching composition in nine stanzas, Emperor Zhang’s intention to celebrate and recount ancestral deeds shines still more brightly; through the composition in five stanzas, the glory of the five sage emperors’ achievements becomes still more manifest. How solemn and majestic! Is this not the sound of the Shang people’s hymn praising profound wisdom?

The ancient sovereigns’ writings and the emperors’ canons resound sonorously and shine brilliantly; the Yellow River Chart and the Luo River’s Great Plan ring out like jade chimes and bronze bells. Those throughout the realm who look up to these works and praise them surely cannot find descriptions adequate to express their admiration fully. Yet you, sir, now wish to seek…

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
祖宗授受
皇上敬承所以祈
天永
命之本顧草茅愚士何足以知之雖然文王壽
考作人而成於譽髦者皆能矢緝熙敬止
之詩史臣之述二典也首以欽明溫恭以
槩堯舜之大愚固唐虞之共臣而被菁莪
之化者也敢終諉於不知乎竊以爲帝王
之治本於道而所以統會乎是道者心也
所以維持乎此心者敬也能敬則心無不
純心純則道無不聚而敬
===
天也法
祖也皆是道有以基之矣是故
諭曾魯求帝王之治而以執中爲要
召宋濂于觀心之亭而以操存爲難我
太祖之聖敬日躋者固已開心學之原矣是以
一傳而至
成祖有感於解縉正心之講退
punctuated: 祖宗授受、皇上敬承所以祈天永命之本，顧草茅愚士何足以知之？雖然，文王壽考作人，而成於譽髦者，皆能矢《緝熙敬止》之詩。史臣之述《二典》也，首以欽明溫恭以槩堯舜之大。愚固唐虞之共臣而被菁莪之化者也，敢終諉於不知乎？竊以爲帝王之治本於道，而所以統會乎是道者，心也；所以維持乎此心者，敬也。能敬則心無不純，心純則道無不聚，而敬天也、法祖也，皆是道有以基之矣。是故諭曾魯求帝王之治而以執中爲要，召宋濂于觀心之亭而以操存爲難，我太祖之聖敬日躋者，固已開心學之原矣。是以一傳而至成祖，有感於解縉正心之講，退
translation_en:
…the foundation transmitted and received by the imperial ancestors and reverently upheld by His Majesty, whereby Heaven is petitioned and the Mandate prolonged. Yet how could an ignorant scholar of the countryside know enough to understand it? Nevertheless, King Wen, blessed with longevity, nurtured men of talent; those thus perfected as eminent scholars could all recite the verse, “Continue in luminous virtue and abide in reverence.” When the court historians composed the Two Canons, they began with reverence, intelligence, gentleness, and respect to encompass the greatness of Yao and Shun. I am indeed a humble subject of a Tang and Yu age, one who has received the nurturing influence celebrated in “Luxuriant Southernwood.” How could I persist in pleading ignorance?

I venture to think that the government of emperors and kings is rooted in the Way. What unifies this Way is the mind; what sustains this mind is reverence. With reverence, the mind is wholly pure; with a pure mind, the Way is fully gathered within it. Thus, both revering Heaven and taking the ancestors as models have their foundation in this Way. Accordingly, when instructing Zeng Lu on seeking the government of emperors and kings, our Taizu made holding fast to the Mean its essential principle; when summoning Song Lian to the Pavilion for Contemplating the Mind, he identified maintaining one’s hold upon the mind as the difficult task. Our Taizu, whose sagely reverence advanced daily, had already opened the wellspring of the learning of the mind. Thus, after one transmission, it reached Chengzu. Moved by Xie Jin’s exposition on rectifying the mind, he withdrew …

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
朝默坐管束此心而
成祖之敬固
太祖之敬也繼傳而至
宣宗有感於鄰畿形勢之固而深戒宴遊世守
恭儉
宣宗之心卽
成祖之心也至我
皇上則益覲揚而光顯之有以發
列聖之所未發而
===
帝王精一之傳聖賢授受之妙至是無餘藴矣
是故
敬一有箴則敬以聚之而不忽也一以守之而
不雜也而所以收斂者無弗至五箴有註
則由中以應乎外也制外以養乎中也而
所以涵養者無弗純以此事
天則惟時惟幾夙夜之畏也以此法
祖則不愆不忘陟降之心也是以
臨御以來純政純心建諸天地而不悖大順大
punctuated:
朝，默坐管束此心，而成祖之敬固太祖之敬也。繼傳而至宣宗，有感於鄰畿形勢之固，而深戒宴遊，世守恭儉。宣宗之心卽成祖之心也。至我皇上，則益覲揚而光顯之，有以發列聖之所未發，而帝王精一之傳、聖賢授受之妙，至是無餘藴矣。
是故《敬一》有箴，則敬以聚之而不忽也，一以守之而不雜也，而所以收斂者無弗至；五箴有註，則由中以應乎外也，制外以養乎中也，而所以涵養者無弗純。以此事天，則惟時惟幾，夙夜之畏也；以此法祖，則不愆不忘，陟降之心也。是以臨御以來，純政純心，建諸天地而不悖，大順大
translation_en:
…from court, he sat silently, keeping this mind under control. Chengzu’s reverent attentiveness was indeed Taizu’s reverent attentiveness. The succession continued down to Xuanzong, who, reflecting on the strength of the terrain surrounding the capital region, sternly cautioned against feasting and pleasure excursions, so that reverence and frugality might be preserved through the generations. Xuanzong’s mind was precisely Chengzu’s mind. Coming to our present Emperor, he has further exalted [?] and illuminated this tradition, bringing forth what the succession of sage emperors had not yet brought forth. Thus the sovereigns’ transmission of refinement and single-mindedness, and the subtle teachings handed down among sages and worthies, now contain no meaning left unexpressed.
Thus, with the Admonition on Reverent Attentiveness and Single-mindedness (Jingyi), reverent attentiveness gathers the mind without negligence, and single-mindedness holds it fast without admixture: nothing is lacking in the thoroughness with which the mind is collected and restrained. With the commentaries on the Five Admonitions, one responds to external things from within, and regulates outward conduct to nourish what is within: nothing in this cultivation fails to be pure. Serving Heaven in this way means attending to the proper times and the incipient signs of change, maintaining awe morning and night. Emulating the ancestors in this way means neither transgressing nor forgetting, keeping their ascending and descending spirits in mind. Hence, since ascending the throne, the Emperor has purified government and purified the mind, establishing them in accord with Heaven and Earth, with great harmony and great…

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
化考諸
先聖而不謬上下會於皇極而遠近同乎率俾
德教洋溢四表莫不光被禮樂明備天地將
爲昭焉謂非一敬之所致哉然愚又有說
焉惟天聰明惟聖時憲
祖宗之道郎
天道也文王陟降在帝左右
天之心亦
祖宗之心也故書言明徵謨訓而必繼之以克
謹天戒惟后明明焉詩言上天之載而復
終之以儀刑文王萬邦作孚焉是敬
===
天也亦所以敬
祖也法
祖也亦所以法
天也此皆我
皇上已試之明徵而衍萬載之鴻休者要不出
乎此也愚也涵濡
聖化久矣雖有激于中而深懼其無以繪頌
punctuated:
化，考諸先聖而不謬。上下會於皇極，而遠近同乎率俾。德教洋溢，四表莫不光被；禮樂明備，天地將爲昭焉。謂非一敬之所致哉？然愚又有說焉。惟天聰明，惟聖時憲。祖宗之道郎天道也，文王陟降，在帝左右。天之心亦祖宗之心也。故書言「明徵謨訓」，而必繼之以「克謹天戒，惟后明明」焉；詩言「上天之載」，而復終之以「儀刑文王，萬邦作孚」焉。是敬天也，亦所以敬祖也；法祖也，亦所以法天也。此皆我皇上已試之明徵，而衍萬載之鴻休者，要不出乎此也。

愚也涵濡聖化久矣，雖有激于中，而深懼其無以繪頌
translation_en:
…transformation, when tested against the sages of old, proves free from error. Those above and below unite in the sovereign’s supreme standard, while those far and near alike follow and obey. Moral instruction spreads abundantly, its radiance reaching every quarter; rites and music are clear and complete, and Heaven and Earth will thereby be made manifest. Could one say that this was not brought about by single-minded reverence? Yet I, in my ignorance, have something further to say. Heaven is discerning and perceptive; the sage takes it as his model. The way of the imperial ancestors is [?] the Way of Heaven. King Wen ascends and descends, remaining at the Supreme Lord’s side. Heaven’s heart is also the heart of the imperial ancestors. Thus, when the Book of Documents speaks of “clearly verifying the counsels and instructions,” it necessarily follows this with “being fully attentive to Heaven’s warnings,” and “the ruler makes his understanding bright.” When the Book of Odes speaks of “the workings of Heaven above,” it concludes with “taking King Wen as a model, the myriad states come to trust.” Thus, revering Heaven is also the means of revering the ancestors; taking the ancestors as models is also the means of taking Heaven as a model. All these are clear proofs already established in practice by Our Emperor. The means of extending magnificent blessings for ten thousand years essentially lie within these principles.

I, in my ignorance, have long been steeped in the sage’s transforming influence. Though inwardly stirred, I deeply fear that I lack the means to depict and praise…

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
天地之大也惟執事進而敎之
第二問
張鵬翰
同考試官敎諭林　批〔剖析六經同歸一致發揚諸儒〕
〔表章之功條分明備無如此篇〕
考試官敎諭袁　批〔六經同道於聖人之心執者判之〕
〔此作會經以心折疑以道斷案嚴非真知道者耶〕
考試官敎諭顧　批〔考據精詳評騭確當非潛心〕
〔理學者不能〕
===
六經之有異議也君子當略其迹而會之
以心諸儒之無定見也君子當存其說而
折之以道夫心者經之原也經者心之著
也聖賢以其原于心者而著之經雖有作
有述之不同要之發吾之心焉耳諸儒之
傳經也不求其道而求其文徒泥其迹而
不原其心雖其功不容以盡泯而其說則
不可以盡信是故訓詁愈煩而去道彌遠
象數雖陳而精蘊益晦皆非所以衛道而
punctuated:
天地之大也，惟執事進而敎之。

第二問
張鵬翰
同考試官敎諭林，批〔剖析六經，同歸一致；發揚諸儒〕〔表章之功，條分明備，無如此篇。〕
考試官敎諭袁，批〔六經同道，於聖人之心，執者判之。〕〔此作會經以心，折疑以道，斷案嚴，非真知道者耶？〕
考試官敎諭顧，批〔考據精詳，評騭確當，非潛心〕〔理學者不能。〕

六經之有異議也，君子當略其迹而會之以心；諸儒之無定見也，君子當存其說而折之以道。夫心者，經之原也；經者，心之著也。聖賢以其原于心者而著之經，雖有作有述之不同，要之發吾之心焉耳。諸儒之傳經也，不求其道而求其文，徒泥其迹而不原其心，雖其功不容以盡泯，而其說則不可以盡信。是故訓詁愈煩，而去道彌遠；象數雖陳，而精蘊益晦，皆非所以衛道而
translation_en:
…the greatness of Heaven and Earth. I ask only that you, Sir, guide me onward and instruct me.

Second Policy Question
Zhang Penghan

Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: 〔In analyzing the Six Classics, he brings them together in a single underlying unity; in elucidating the various scholars’〕〔achievements in bringing their meaning to light, no essay equals this one in the clarity and completeness of its organization.〕

Examiner Yuan, Instructor, comments: 〔The Six Classics share the same Way in the mind of the sage; those who cling to fixed views divide them.〕〔This composition unites the classics through the mind and resolves doubts through the Way. Its judgments are rigorous—is its author not someone who truly understands the Way?〕

Examiner Gu, Instructor, comments: 〔His textual research is meticulous and thorough, and his assessments sound and appropriate. Only someone who has devoted himself〕〔to the Learning of Principle could achieve this.〕

Where divergent interpretations of the Six Classics arise, the gentleman should set aside their outward traces and bring them into unity through the mind. Where the various scholars have reached no settled view, the gentleman should preserve their explanations and adjudicate them by the Way. For the mind is the source of the classics, and the classics are the manifestation of the mind. The sages and worthies set forth in the classics what originated in their minds. Although there is a distinction between creating and transmitting, ultimately these activities simply give expression to our own minds. In transmitting the classics, the various scholars seek their wording rather than their Way; they merely cling to outward traces without tracing them back to the originating mind. Although their achievements cannot be wholly effaced, their explanations cannot all be trusted. Thus, the more elaborate the philological glosses become, the farther they depart from the Way; although images and numbers are set forth, their subtle import becomes ever more obscure. None of this serves to safeguard the Way and…

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
繼往極深以淑來也循往聖之格言會吾
心之精義質眞儒之要論救諸說之異同
豈非博古之指歸明辨之正學哉執事之
問六經蓋將以稽核道眞疏觀疑貳望末
學也令夫經以載道而道無異統潔淨精
微易道深矣而河圖則之以畫卦較之則
洛書以叙疇者不一致乎溫柔敦厚詩教
深矣而吟咏諷誦之章較之合君臣以賡
歌者有二道乎至于春秋之褒貶三百篇
===
之美剌也禮經之從違十二公之予奪也
跋氏謂六經之道同歸不信然乎易之剛
柔雜居吾心之動靜也書之典謨訓誥吾
心之經綸也詩之歌詠比興吾心之性情
也春秋之勸善懲惡吾心之賞罰也三禮
之度數儀則吾心之節文也胡氏謂人心
之所同然又不信乎語易而盡于陰陽自
卦畫言耳作之伏羲者以先天名演之周
文者以後天名不過無言有言之間其實
punctuated:
繼往極深以淑來也。循往聖之格言，會吾心之精義，質眞儒之要論，救諸說之異同，豈非博古之指歸、明辨之正學哉？執事之問六經，蓋將以稽核道眞，疏觀疑貳，望末學也。
令夫經以載道，而道無異統。潔淨精微，易道深矣，而河圖則之以畫卦，較之則洛書以叙疇者，不一致乎？溫柔敦厚，詩教深矣，而吟咏諷誦之章，較之合君臣以賡歌者，有二道乎？至于春秋之褒貶，三百篇之美剌也；禮經之從違，十二公之予奪也。跋氏謂六經之道同歸，不信然乎？
易之剛柔雜居，吾心之動靜也；書之典謨訓誥，吾心之經綸也；詩之歌詠比興，吾心之性情也；春秋之勸善懲惡，吾心之賞罰也；三禮之度數儀則，吾心之節文也。胡氏謂人心之所同然，又不信乎？
語易而盡于陰陽，自卦畫言耳。作之伏羲者，以先天名；演之周文者，以後天名。不過無言有言之間，其實
translation_en:
…to carry forward the legacy of the past and plumb its depths, thereby benefiting those to come. To follow the exemplary sayings of the sages of old, comprehend the subtle principles within our own minds, consult the essential arguments of true Confucian scholars, and remedy the discrepancies among the various interpretations—is this not the purpose of broad learning about antiquity and the proper pursuit of discerning judgment? In asking about the Six Classics, you presumably expect this humble student to examine the truth of the Way and clarify doubtful or conflicting points [?].
Now [?], the Classics convey the Way, and the Way has no divergent lines of transmission. Purity, refinement, precision, and subtlety: profound indeed is the Way of the Changes. Yet when the River Chart was taken as a model for drawing the trigrams, did this not accord with taking the Luo Writing as a model for arranging the categories? Gentleness, kindness, sincerity, and generosity: profound indeed is the teaching of the Odes. Yet do its verses, chanted and recited, embody a different Way from the songs in which ruler and ministers joined, each continuing the other's song? As for the praise and blame of the Spring and Autumn Annals, these are the commendation and criticism of the Three Hundred Odes; the prescriptions and prohibitions of the Classic of Rites are the approval and disapproval expressed in the annals of the twelve dukes. Master Ba [?] said that the Ways of the Six Classics converge upon the same end. Is this not indeed so?
The intermingling of the firm and yielding in the Changes is the activity and stillness of our own minds. The canons, counsels, instructions, and proclamations of the Documents are our minds' ordering and governing. The songs, comparisons, and evocative images of the Odes are our minds' nature and feelings. The encouragement of good and chastisement of evil in the Spring and Autumn Annals are our minds' rewards and punishments. The measures, enumerations, ceremonies, and rules of the Three Rites are our minds' regulated forms of expression. Master Hu spoke of what all human minds alike acknowledge as right. Is this not also true?
To speak of the Changes as wholly encompassed by yin and yang is merely to speak from the perspective of the lines of the hexagrams. What Fuxi created is called “Prior to Heaven”; what King Wen of Zhou elaborated is called “Later than Heaven.” The distinction amounts only to the absence or presence of words; in substance …

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
一而已矣語書而盡于政事自紀錄言耳
授之伏生者以今文稱出之孔壁者以古
文稱不過隷書蝌蚪之變其實亦一而已
矣國風雅頌謂之四詩微辭奥義均之爲
經而關雎二南朝廷歌樂見盛世之音焉
是爲風雅之正邶風祈父板蕩之什有世
道之感焉則變風變雅之由名斯非說詩
者不易之定論耶禮儀威儀謂之三禮經
曲數度均之爲禮而儀禮諸篇皆先王之
舊茲欲以之爲綱領而爲經郊特牲冠義
===
諸篇多七十子所記茲欲以之爲義說而
爲傳是非朱子更定之確議耶春秋始魯
隱而終獲麟仲尼之筆削在焉左丘明氏
取列國之史而係之書法之下重序事而
寡釋義亦庶幾于見知者然其失也誣至
于公羊則又以祭仲廢立爲行權妾母稱
夫人爲合正穀梁以衛輒拒父爲尊祖不
納子糾爲內惡其失左氏之意遠矣而乃
punctuated: 一而已矣。語書而盡于政事，自紀錄言耳。授之伏生者以今文稱，出之孔壁者以古文稱，不過隷書蝌蚪之變，其實亦一而已矣。國風雅頌謂之四詩，微辭奥義均之爲經。而關雎二南、朝廷歌樂，見盛世之音焉，是爲風雅之正；邶風祈父、板蕩之什，有世道之感焉，則變風變雅之由名。斯非說詩者不易之定論耶？禮儀威儀謂之三禮，經曲數度均之爲禮。而儀禮諸篇皆先王之舊，茲欲以之爲綱領而爲經；郊特牲、冠義諸篇，多七十子所記，茲欲以之爲義說而爲傳。是非朱子更定之確議耶？春秋始魯隱而終獲麟，仲尼之筆削在焉。左丘明氏取列國之史而係之書法之下，重序事而寡釋義，亦庶幾于見知者，然其失也誣。至于公羊，則又以祭仲廢立爲行權，妾母稱夫人爲合正；穀梁以衛輒拒父爲尊祖，不納子糾爲內惡。其失左氏之意遠矣，而乃
translation_en: …are one and the same, that is all. To say that the Book of Documents concerns itself entirely with affairs of government is to speak only of what it records. What Fu Sheng transmitted is called the New Text; what emerged from the wall of Confucius’s house is called the Old Text. The difference is merely between clerical script and tadpole script; in substance, these too are one and the same. The Airs of the States, the Lesser and Greater Odes, and the Hymns are called the four divisions of the Book of Songs. In their subtle expressions and profound meanings, they equally constitute a classic. In “The Ospreys,” the two Southern sections, and the songs and music of the court, one hears the sounds of a flourishing age: these constitute the orthodox Airs and Odes. The Airs of Bei and such pieces as “Minister of War,” “Oppression,” and “Turmoil” express feelings about the condition of the age; hence the names “changed Airs” and “changed Odes.” Is this not the settled judgment, admitting no alteration, of those who interpret the Songs? Ritual forms and ceremonial deportment are spoken of as the Three Ritual Classics; their major principles, detailed observances, numerical prescriptions, and standards all constitute ritual. The chapters of the Ceremonies and Rites preserve the ancient institutions of the former kings; the proposal here is therefore to make them the guiding framework and treat them as the classic. Chapters such as “The Single Victim at the Suburban Sacrifice” and “The Meaning of the Capping Ceremony” largely contain records made by the seventy disciples; the proposal is therefore to treat them as explanations of meaning and make them the commentary. Is this not Master Zhu’s well-founded proposal for revising the arrangement? The Spring and Autumn Annals begins with Duke Yin of Lu and ends with the capture of the qilin; therein lies Zhongni’s work of writing and excision. Zuo Qiuming took the histories of the various states and attached them beneath the Annals’ formally worded entries. He emphasized narrating events and offered few explanations of their meaning. He thus came close to one whose knowledge came from direct observation, yet his failing was misrepresentation. As for the Gongyang Commentary, it further regarded Ji Zhong’s deposition and installation of rulers as an exercise of discretionary judgment, and calling a ruler’s mother who had been a concubine “Lady” as conforming to what was proper. The Guliang Commentary regarded Zhe of Wei’s rejection of his father as honoring his grandfather, and the refusal to admit Ziju as an instance of wrongdoing within the state [?]. These depart very far from the intent of Master Zuo, and yet…

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
欲以窺聖人之意得乎自是而後秦政奮
豺狼之心滅先哲之迹制挾書之令極坑
焚之慘儒生抱業以竄學亡無復存者漢
興馬上之習未泯而挾書之令郎下齊魯
之間稍稍興起然業有專門而互相詆訾
疏有異義而輒以名家其紕繆踳駁不可
勝言所謂博而寡要勞而少功者也鄭夾
漈氏謂秦人焚書而書存諸儒窮經而經
絶彼蓋慼于秦燔之餘而經有遺文義疏
===
之起而道無嫡統云爾亦未免于言之已
甚也今以漢儒考之孟喜梁丘之易原于
商瞿子木而受之田何猶未免好自稱譽
箴應近幸之非濟南伏生之書口授鼂錯
而謂天地人四時爲七政夏侯勝承之復
倡爲災異之談焉申公以詩鳴魯轅固以
詩鳴齊卒無眞見而以關雎正風爲刺可
乎江公受學申公而治穀梁胡毋生見推
仲舒而治公羊互相詆斥而卒無折衷之
punctuated:
欲以窺聖人之意，得乎？自是而後，秦政奮豺狼之心，滅先哲之迹，制挾書之令，極坑焚之慘。儒生抱業以竄，學亡，無復存者。漢興，馬上之習未泯，而挾書之令郎下，齊魯之間稍稍興起。然業有專門而互相詆訾，疏有異義而輒以名家，其紕繆踳駁不可勝言，所謂博而寡要、勞而少功者也。鄭夾漈氏謂：「秦人焚書而書存，諸儒窮經而經絶。」彼蓋慼于秦燔之餘而經有遺文，義疏之起而道無嫡統云爾，亦未免于言之已甚也。
今以漢儒考之，孟喜、梁丘之易，原于商瞿子木而受之田何，猶未免好自稱譽、箴應近幸之非。濟南伏生之書，口授鼂錯，而謂天地人四時爲七政；夏侯勝承之，復倡爲災異之談焉。申公以詩鳴魯，轅固以詩鳴齊，卒無眞見，而以關雎正風爲刺，可乎？江公受學申公而治穀梁，胡毋生見推仲舒而治公羊，互相詆斥，而卒無折衷之
translation_en:
…could they hope thereby to discern the sage’s meaning? Thereafter, Zheng of Qin unleashed his wolfish heart, obliterated the traces of the former sages, instituted the prohibition on possessing books, and carried the horrors of burying scholars and burning books to the utmost. Confucian scholars fled, taking their learning with them; scholarship perished, with nothing remaining. When the Han arose, the habits of rule from horseback had not yet faded, and the prohibition on possessing books was issued [?]. Learning gradually revived in Qi and Lu. Yet scholars formed exclusive schools of learning and disparaged one another; their commentaries offered divergent interpretations, on which they promptly established reputations as distinct schools. Their errors and contradictions were beyond enumeration. This was what is meant by being broad in learning but grasping little of its essentials, laboring much but accomplishing little. Zheng Jiaji said: “The men of Qin burned the books, yet the books survived; the scholars exhaustively studied the Classics, yet the Classics were lost.” He was presumably lamenting that some text of the Classics survived Qin’s burning, whereas, with the rise of explanatory commentaries, the Way had no legitimate line of transmission. Even so, his words were excessive.
Consider now the Han scholars. The traditions of the Book of Changes associated with Meng Xi and Liangqiu originated with Shang Qu, styled Zimu, and were received from Tian He; yet they were not free from the faults of self-praise and prognostication to court imperial favor [?]. Master Fu of Jinan orally transmitted the Book of Documents to Chao Cuo, but interpreted the “seven regulators” as Heaven, Earth, humanity, and the four seasons. Xiahou Sheng inherited this teaching and further promoted discussions of calamities and anomalies. Master Shen won renown in Lu through the Book of Odes, and Yuan Gu won renown in Qi through the same Classic. Yet in the end they lacked true insight and treated “The Ospreys,” a poem of the orthodox Airs, as satire. Could this be acceptable? Master Jiang studied under Master Shen and specialized in the Guliang Commentary; Hu Wusheng, esteemed by Dong Zhongshu, specialized in the Gongyang Commentary. They disparaged and rejected one another, and ultimately had no balanced…

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
見可乎以至高堂生傳士禮十七篇直推
士禮以達天子而河間所獻五十六篇舉
置而不講聖人之全經不復見于天下而
戴德戴勝乃從而刪定之亦非復古之舊
數子之得失悉可考也王通氏謂九師興
而易道微三傳作而春秋散齊魯韓毛詩
之末也大戴小戴禮之衰也其信然矣蓋
以漢興諸儒各信所習是非紛錯準裁靡
定以好惡爲廢興辯訥爲盛衰師匠不經
===
穿鑿附會往往皆碩儒爲之雖謂之窮經
而經絶也亦宜殊不知聖賢之述經以載
道爲主而儒者之傳疏以通經爲要漢之
諸儒大抵各貴其師習舍經而任傳疑心
而信耳目焉爾厥後石渠白虎講其異同
元忌蔡邕急于校正而舛訛疑誤猶有不
盡解者是殆未知求經于道求道于心無
惑其說之日籍籍于天下也有宋聿興當
五百之期適奎聚之運眞儒輩出邵堯夫
punctuated: 見，可乎？以至高堂生傳《士禮》十七篇，直推士禮以達天子，而河間所獻五十六篇舉置而不講，聖人之全經不復見于天下，而戴德、戴勝乃從而刪定之，亦非復古之舊。數子之得失，悉可考也。王通氏謂：「九師興而易道微，三傳作而春秋散，齊魯韓毛，詩之末也；大戴小戴，禮之衰也。」其信然矣！蓋以漢興，諸儒各信所習，是非紛錯，準裁靡定，以好惡爲廢興，辯訥爲盛衰，師匠不經，穿鑿附會，往往皆碩儒爲之。雖謂之窮經，而經絶也亦宜。殊不知聖賢之述經，以載道爲主，而儒者之傳疏，以通經爲要。漢之諸儒，大抵各貴其師習，舍經而任傳，疑心而信耳目焉爾。厥後石渠、白虎講其異同，元忌、蔡邕急于校正，而舛訛疑誤猶有不盡解者。是殆未知求經于道，求道于心，無惑其說之日籍籍于天下也。有宋聿興，當五百之期，適奎聚之運，眞儒輩出，邵堯夫
translation_en:
…discernment—could this be acceptable? Furthermore, Gaotang Sheng transmitted seventeen chapters of the Rites of the Shi, simply extending the rites of the shi rank up to the Son of Heaven, while the fifty-six chapters presented by the Prince of Hejian were all set aside without being expounded. The sages’ complete classic was no longer seen in the world, and Dai De and Dai Sheng subsequently abridged and edited it; this, too, failed to restore its ancient form. The achievements and failings of these several masters can all be examined. Wang Tong said: “When the nine masters arose, the Way of the Changes declined; when the three commentaries were composed, the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals became dispersed. The Qi, Lu, Han, and Mao traditions represent the latter days of the Odes; the Elder Dai and Younger Dai represent the decline of the Rites.” These words are indeed true!

For, with the rise of the Han, the various scholars each trusted what they had learned. Right and wrong became confused, with no settled standard of judgment. Acceptance and rejection depended on likes and dislikes; flourishing and decline depended on eloquence and its absence. Teachers departed from canonical norms, forcing interpretations and contriving connections—practices often perpetrated by eminent scholars themselves. Though they called this exhaustive study of the classics, it was only to be expected that the transmission of the classics should thereby be severed. They utterly failed to understand that the sages and worthies expounded the classics chiefly to convey the Way, and that scholars’ commentaries and subcommentaries should above all make the classics intelligible. The Han scholars generally prized the teachings inherited from their own masters, abandoning the classics and relying on commentaries, doubting their own minds while trusting their ears and eyes, and nothing more.

Later, the discussions at the Shiqu Pavilion and the White Tiger Hall examined their agreements and differences, while Yuan Ji [?] and Cai Yong urgently pursued textual correction. Yet errors, doubtful readings, and misinterpretations remained incompletely resolved. This was presumably because they did not understand how to seek the meaning of the classics in the Way, and the Way in the mind. No wonder their doctrines grew daily more clamorous throughout the world. When the Song arose, it coincided with the five-hundred-year cycle and the auspicious conjunction of planets in the Kui constellation. True Confucian scholars emerged in succession. Shao Yaofu…

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
氏憤紫朱之相奪乃以四府盡經而謂易
始伏羲祖三皇也書序堯舜宗五帝也詩
首文武子三王也春秋述桓文孫五霸也
夫祖宗之評是矣而以子孫名者豈以其
世論哉蓋遡孫子以達宗祖者統系之有
源委也自祖宗以及子孫者道脉之有嫡
傳也所以明四經之同歸而列聖之一心
焉耳其支流蔓衍爲漢爲唐僭經擬傳均
之無取也已自是而寖昌寖熾如日中天
===
漢儒之謬矣六經之疑義一舉而釐正之
無餘也雖然漢儒之功亦有不可盡少者
昔人有云禮失求之野諸子之于六籍多
所發明而言經者籍之以爲考道之資不
猶愈于野哉譬彼田焉不菑之于先則畬
以畬于後今食稻而忘墾藝之初可乎自
今觀之易明于程朱之傳矣書明于蔡沈
之註矣詩有集傳禮有集解而朱子自謂
可以無遺憾可以有補于世矣春秋則又
punctuated:
氏憤紫朱之相奪，乃以四府盡經，而謂《易》始伏羲，祖三皇也；《書》序堯舜，宗五帝也；《詩》首文武，子三王也；《春秋》述桓文，孫五霸也。夫祖宗之評是矣，而以子孫名者，豈以其世論哉？蓋遡孫子以達宗祖者，統系之有源委也；自祖宗以及子孫者，道脉之有嫡傳也。所以明四經之同歸，而列聖之一心焉耳。其支流蔓衍，爲漢爲唐，僭經擬傳，均之無取也已。自是而寖昌寖熾，如日中天，漢儒之謬矣。六經之疑義，一舉而釐正之無餘也。

雖然，漢儒之功亦有不可盡少者。昔人有云：「禮失求之野。」諸子之于六籍，多所發明，而言經者籍之以爲考道之資，不猶愈于野哉？譬彼田焉，不菑之于先，則畬以畬于後？今食稻而忘墾藝之初，可乎？自今觀之，《易》明于程朱之傳矣，《書》明于蔡沈之註矣。《詩》有《集傳》，《禮》有《集解》，而朱子自謂可以無遺憾，可以有補于世矣。《春秋》則又
translation_en:
…Master Shao Yaofu, indignant that purple and vermilion were supplanting one another—that the spurious was displacing the genuine—encompassed the classics within four repositories. He said: “The Changes begins with Fuxi and takes the Three Sovereigns as ancestors; the Documents recounts Yao and Shun and takes the Five Emperors as forebears; the Odes places Wen and Wu first and takes the Three Kings as sons; the Spring and Autumn Annals records Huan and Wen and takes the Five Hegemons as grandsons.” His characterization of ancestors and forebears is sound; but when he calls the others sons and grandsons, can he be speaking merely of their historical periods? Tracing back from grandsons and sons to forebears and ancestors shows that the lineage has a source and successive ramifications. Proceeding from ancestors and forebears down to sons and grandsons shows that the Way has a legitimate line of transmission. This serves only to illuminate the common destination of the four classics and the single mind shared by the successive sages. Their offshoots proliferated into the Han and Tang traditions, presumptuously claiming the status of classics and imitating commentaries; none of these merits acceptance. From this point onward, learning grew ever more flourishing and brilliant, like the sun at its zenith; the Han scholars were mistaken [?]. The doubtful meanings of the Six Classics were clarified and corrected in a single sweep, leaving none unresolved.

Nevertheless, the achievements of the Han scholars cannot all be disparaged. An ancient saying runs: “When ritual is lost, seek it in the countryside.” The various masters shed much light on the Six Classics, and those who discuss the classics draw upon them as resources for investigating the Way. Are they not better still than the countryside? Consider a field: unless it is first broken up, how can it later become cultivated land [?]? Can we now eat rice and forget the initial work of clearing the ground and planting? Viewed from our own day, the Changes has been elucidated through the commentaries of Cheng and Zhu, and the Documents through the annotations of Cai Shen. For the Odes there is the Collected Commentaries, and for the Rites there is the Collected Explanations. Master Zhu himself said that he could have no lingering regrets and that his work could benefit the world. As for the Spring and Autumn Annals, furthermore …

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
程子胡安國相繼而爲之表章斯六經之
學煥然大明使非漢儒專門名家以致力
于先則亦奚所考據以發明于後哉議者
尚欲布其義疏以通之天下後世不爲無
見云爾也故曰漢儒之功亦有不可盡少
者今之學者苟知究漢儒之所以失而求
其麤循宋儒之所以得而詣其精不以其
已明者而徒事于口耳之末必于其未明
者而探索夫精微之藴則會經以心而折
===
疑以道將不止于訓詁辭章之習而進于
極深研幾之學矣不然則是自畫其身于
堂下而敢于是非乎人者吾不知其可也
惟執事進而教之
第三問
楊聯芳
同考試官教諭周　批〔性命才氣之學不明久矣是策能發聖賢之藴𥘉非精學卓識之士耶〕
考試官教諭袁　批〔理明辭復足以發之〕
punctuated:
程子、胡安國相繼而爲之表章，斯六經之學煥然大明。使非漢儒專門名家以致力于先，則亦奚所考據以發明于後哉？議者尚欲布其義疏，以通之天下後世，不爲無見云爾也。故曰：漢儒之功亦有不可盡少者。今之學者苟知究漢儒之所以失而求其麤，循宋儒之所以得而詣其精，不以其已明者而徒事于口耳之末，必于其未明者而探索夫精微之藴，則會經以心而折疑以道，將不止于訓詁辭章之習，而進于極深研幾之學矣。不然，則是自畫其身于堂下，而敢于是非乎人者，吾不知其可也。惟執事進而教之。
第三問
楊聯芳
同考試官教諭周　批〔性命才氣之學不明久矣！是策能發聖賢之藴，𥘉非精學卓識之士耶？〕
考試官教諭袁　批〔理明，辭復足以發之。〕
translation_en:
…Master Cheng and Hu Anguo successively elucidated it, and thus the learning of the Six Classics shone forth with renewed clarity. Had the Han scholars not first devoted their efforts to establishing distinguished schools of specialized learning, what evidence could later scholars have relied upon to elucidate the Classics? Those who advocate further disseminating their explanatory commentaries throughout the world and to later generations are not without insight. Hence I say that the achievements of the Han scholars cannot be wholly discounted.
If scholars today understand how to investigate where the Han scholars went astray and seek out the broad outlines, and follow where the Song scholars succeeded to attain the essentials, they will not merely occupy themselves with the superficial business of oral transmission and memorization concerning what has already been clarified. They must probe the subtle depths of what remains unclear. Then they will comprehend the Classics with their minds and resolve doubts through the Way, advancing beyond the practice of glossing words and composing polished prose to learning that plumbs the depths and examines the incipient workings of things. Otherwise, they merely confine themselves below the hall, yet presume to judge others right or wrong. I cannot see how this is acceptable. I ask only that you, honored sir, guide me forward and instruct me.
Third Policy Question
Yang Lianfang
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: “The learning concerning human nature, Heaven’s decree, ability, and vital force has long remained obscure! This policy essay brings out the profound meanings of the sages and worthies. Is its author not a man of refined learning and outstanding insight [?]?”
Comment by Examiner Yuan, Instructor: “The principles are clear, and the language is moreover adequate to elucidate them.”

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭顧　批〔體認真切〕
天下未有無理之氣而亦未有無氣之理
是故理氣合一而天人之故同異之旨可
以觀其深矣何也天之生斯人也賦之理
以主夫氣稟之氣以載夫理是理也者形
而上之道也人得之以成性而未嘗離夫
氣氣也者形而下之器也人得之以成質
而未嘗外夫理若徒有見于氣而無見于
理則無以達其本然之妙非善觀理者也
===
有見于理而無見于氣則無以識其生質
之殊非善觀氣者也故必究夫天道之本
原而又察其流行之各異則生人之道於
是乎備而諸說之異統乎其同矣執事以
文校士而舉夫人之性命才氣下詢末學
豈非啓以大本大原之學乎愚非其人也
亦嘗攷之載籍而知其說矣粤自孔子而
上其言甚約而其理自具至於孟子始發
其蘊而辨析其歸自後其說寖多而道愈
punctuated:
考試官教諭顧　批〔體認真切〕

天下未有無理之氣，而亦未有無氣之理。是故理氣合一，而天人之故、同異之旨，可以觀其深矣。何也？天之生斯人也，賦之理以主夫氣，稟之氣以載夫理。是理也者，形而上之道也，人得之以成性，而未嘗離夫氣；氣也者，形而下之器也，人得之以成質，而未嘗外夫理。若徒有見于氣而無見于理，則無以達其本然之妙，非善觀理者也；有見于理而無見于氣，則無以識其生質之殊，非善觀氣者也。故必究夫天道之本原，而又察其流行之各異，則生人之道於是乎備，而諸說之異統乎其同矣。執事以文校士，而舉夫人之性命才氣下詢末學，豈非啓以大本大原之學乎？愚非其人也，亦嘗攷之載籍而知其說矣。粤自孔子而上，其言甚約，而其理自具；至於孟子，始發其蘊而辨析其歸。自後其說寖多，而道愈
translation_en:
Examiner Gu, Instructor, comments: 〔His understanding is genuine and precise.〕

In all under Heaven, there has never been material force (qi) without principle (li), nor principle without material force.
