Thus, principle and material force form a unity, through which one may perceive the profound workings of Heaven and humanity and the meaning of their similarities and differences. Why is this so? When Heaven brings human beings into existence, it endows them with principle to govern their material force and with material force to carry their principle. Principle is the Way that is above physical form. Human beings receive it to constitute their nature, yet it is never separate from material force. Material force is the concrete vessel below physical form. Human beings receive it to constitute their physical endowment, yet it is never outside principle. If one perceives only material force and fails to perceive principle, one cannot comprehend the subtlety of its original condition and is no discerning observer of principle. If one perceives principle but fails to perceive material force, one cannot recognize the differences in people's inborn constitutions and is no discerning observer of material force. One must therefore investigate the fundamental source of the Way of Heaven and also examine the differing manifestations of its operation. Only then will one's account of the way human beings come into existence be complete, and the differences among the various explanations be brought together within what they share.

You, honored sir, assess scholars through their writings and have raised the matters of human nature, allotted destiny, capacity, and material force to question a novice such as myself. Is this not an invitation to the study of the great root and ultimate source? Unworthy though I am, I have nevertheless examined the written records and come to understand these explanations. From Kongzi and in earlier times, statements on these matters were very concise, yet their principles were fully present. Only with Mengzi were their hidden implications brought forth and their ultimate import analyzed and distinguished. Thereafter, explanations gradually multiplied, while the Way became ever more…

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
晦是非道之不明也言之異同者淆之也
愚請先論其從出之原次究夫諸說之詳
而終及於會通之妙以爲明問復焉蓋嘗
聞之易曰一陰一陽之謂道繼之者善也
成之者性也夫未始有物之前本有是理
而既始有物之後理自各足其曰繼之者
善蓋言天之畀於人也其曰成之者性蓋
言人之得乎天也方其始出於天而純乎
理者乃造化絪緼之初理未雜乎氣焉爲
===
性之善也爲命之正也爲才之美也爲氣
之清也無非太極之本然所謂萬殊而一
本也而不可以言異及其既屬於人而涉
於氣者則形生神發之後氣有以間乎理
焉則性有純駁矣命有薄厚矣才有善惡
矣氣有昏明矣此其二五之雜揉所謂一
本而萬殊也而不可以言同然有是理即
有是氣有是氣即有是理而朱子乃有先
後同異之說何哉其云先後則曰若論本
punctuated:
晦。是非道之不明也，言之異同者淆之也。愚請先論其從出之原，次究夫諸說之詳，而終及於會通之妙，以爲明問復焉。
蓋嘗聞之，《易》曰：「一陰一陽之謂道，繼之者善也，成之者性也。」夫未始有物之前，本有是理；而既始有物之後，理自各足。其曰「繼之者善」，蓋言天之畀於人也；其曰「成之者性」，蓋言人之得乎天也。方其始出於天而純乎理者，乃造化絪緼之初，理未雜乎氣焉，爲性之善也，爲命之正也，爲才之美也，爲氣之清也，無非太極之本然，所謂萬殊而一本也，而不可以言異。及其既屬於人而涉於氣者，則形生神發之後，氣有以間乎理焉，則性有純駁矣，命有薄厚矣，才有善惡矣，氣有昏明矣。此其二五之雜揉，所謂一本而萬殊也，而不可以言同。
然有是理即有是氣，有是氣即有是理，而朱子乃有先後同異之說，何哉？其云先後，則曰：「若論本
translation_en:
…becomes obscured. This is not because the Way itself lacks clarity; rather, the agreements and disagreements among its interpreters have confused it. I humbly propose first to discuss the source from which these matters arise, next to examine the various explanations in detail, and finally to address the subtle means of reconciling them, thereby answering your discerning question.
I have heard the Book of Changes say: “One yin and one yang are called the Way. What continues it is goodness; what brings it to completion is nature.” Before things first existed, this principle (li) already existed; once things came into existence, each possessed principle in its fullness. “What continues it is goodness” speaks of what Heaven bestows upon human beings; “what brings it to completion is nature” speaks of what human beings receive from Heaven. At its first emergence from Heaven, when it consists purely of principle, this is the initial intermingling of the creative transformations, when principle has not yet become mixed with material force (qi). The goodness of nature, the rectitude of Heaven’s endowment, the excellence of native capacity, and the clarity of material force are all nothing other than the original condition of the Supreme Ultimate. This is what is meant by myriad differences having a single root; one cannot speak of them as different. Once these belong to human beings and involve material force, however—after bodily form arises and spirit becomes active—material force can interfere with principle. Thus nature varies in purity and admixture, Heaven’s endowment in scantness and abundance, native capacity in goodness and badness, and material force in obscurity and clarity. This is the intermixture of the two forces and the five phases: what is meant by a single root giving rise to myriad differences. One cannot speak of them as identical.
Yet wherever there is this principle, there is this material force, and wherever there is this material force, there is this principle. Why, then, does Master Zhu nevertheless speak of priority and posteriority, sameness and difference? In speaking of priority and posteriority, he says: “If we discuss the root…

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
原則有理然後有氣若論稟賦則有是氣
而後理隨以具蓋一以本乎太始之先也
一以明夫化醇之後也夫固渾合而無間
者矣其云同異則曰論萬物之一原則理
同而氣異觀萬物之異體則氣猶相近而
理絕不同蓋一以言天性之與氣質也一
以言知覺之與偏全也亦固性分之必然
者矣至若孟子之道孔子之道也而其言
性或謂之相近而繞言其稟受之體或謂
===
之皆善而直指其本然之良然言近則有
善者存言善則於近者寓殆道同而言異
者也其他曰善固性也惡亦不可不謂之
性曰纔說性時便已不是性皆程子所以
發明人性之旨矣斯言也非謂性本惡也
氣稟雜之則有是善而亦不能無惡也非
謂性非性也與生俱生固謂之性而即涉
於形氣也其理何嘗有不備乎逮夫韓子
原性之篇則又以上中下為三品者未明
punctuated: 原，則有理然後有氣；若論稟賦，則有是氣而後理隨以具。」蓋一以本乎太始之先也，一以明夫化醇之後也，夫固渾合而無間者矣。其云同異，則曰：「論萬物之一原，則理同而氣異；觀萬物之異體，則氣猶相近而理絕不同。」蓋一以言天性之與氣質也，一以言知覺之與偏全也，亦固性分之必然者矣。至若孟子之道，孔子之道也，而其言性，或謂之相近，而繞言其稟受之體；或謂之皆善，而直指其本然之良。然言近，則有善者存；言善，則於近者寓。殆道同而言異者也。其他曰：「善固性也，惡亦不可不謂之性。」曰：「纔說性時，便已不是性。」皆程子所以發明人性之旨矣。斯言也，非謂性本惡也，氣稟雜之，則有是善而亦不能無惡也；非謂性非性也，與生俱生，固謂之性，而即涉於形氣也。其理何嘗有不備乎？逮夫韓子《原性》之篇，則又以上中下為三品者，未明
translation_en:
…origins, principle exists before material force; if discussing what beings receive at birth, this material force exists first, and principle then accompanies it in full.” The former traces back to what precedes the primordial beginning; the latter elucidates what follows the mingling and transformation of material forces. Principle and material force are, indeed, thoroughly united without any separation. As for his discussion of sameness and difference, he says: “Considering the single origin of the myriad things, their principle is the same, while their material force differs. Looking at the different forms of the myriad things, their material force is still similar, while their principles are entirely different.” The former concerns Heaven-endowed nature and material constitution; the latter concerns awareness and perception, and whether principle is received partially or completely. These, too, are necessary distinctions in the natures allotted to beings.
As for the Way of Mengzi, it is the Way of Kongzi. Yet in speaking of human nature, one calls human natures similar, speaking indirectly of the constitution received at birth; the other calls them all good, pointing directly to their original goodness. But speaking of similarity preserves the presence of goodness, while speaking of goodness implies similarity. Thus their Way is the same, though their words differ. Other statements—“Goodness is certainly nature, but evil, too, cannot but be called nature,” and “The moment one speaks of nature, it is already no longer nature”—are all means by which Master Cheng elucidates the meaning of human nature. These words do not mean that nature is originally evil: when the endowment of material force is mixed into it, goodness remains, but evil cannot altogether be absent. Nor do they mean that nature is not nature: what comes into being with a person's birth is indeed called nature, but it already involves bodily form and material force. When has its principle ever lacked completeness?
Turning to Master Han's essay, “An Inquiry into Nature,” his division of human nature into three grades—upper, middle, and lower—fails to grasp…

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
乎相近之義以仁義禮智信爲五性者有
同乎皆善之說要之理無不善而氣有不
齊固其性之大端者焉伊洛之學孟子之
學也而其言命或謂天所賦予以闡夫天
命之原或謂莫致而至以歸諸自然之數
然專於理者不雜于氣專於氣者不病于
理殆言殊而意合者也其他曰有命焉不
謂性有性焉不謂命皆孟子所以究極性
命之歸矣斯言也始云有命者兼理氣而
===
言之所以斷制人心欲人不可過也既云
不謂命者獨就夫氣而論之所以充廣道
心欲人無不及也其義亦何嘗有不周乎
逮夫朱子論命之說則又因舜文之於君
父也而謂係於所遇因顏跖之有壽夭也
而謂係於所稟要之氣有不同而理自隨
之固其命之必至者焉才也者所以效天
下之用者也性既善則才亦善孟子固謂
不善非才之罪矣伊川乃曰性無不善其
punctuated:
乎相近之義；以仁義禮智信爲五性者，有同乎皆善之說。要之，理無不善，而氣有不齊，固其性之大端者焉。伊洛之學，孟子之學也。而其言命，或謂天所賦予，以闡夫天命之原；或謂莫致而至，以歸諸自然之數。然專於理者不雜于氣，專於氣者不病于理，殆言殊而意合者也。其他曰「有命焉，不謂性」，「有性焉，不謂命」，皆孟子所以究極性命之歸矣。斯言也，始云「有命」者，兼理氣而言之，所以斷制人心，欲人不可過也；既云「不謂命」者，獨就夫氣而論之，所以充廣道心，欲人無不及也。其義亦何嘗有不周乎？逮夫朱子論命之說，則又因舜文之於君父也，而謂係於所遇；因顏跖之有壽夭也，而謂係於所稟。要之，氣有不同，而理自隨之，固其命之必至者焉。

才也者，所以效天下之用者也。性既善，則才亦善。孟子固謂「不善非才之罪」矣。伊川乃曰：「性無不善，其
translation_en:
…the meaning of being close to one another in nature. His taking benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, wisdom, and trustworthiness as the five natures accords in some measure with the teaching that all are good. In sum, principle is invariably good, while material force (qi) is uneven: these are indeed the broad essentials of human nature.

The learning of the Yi and Luo schools is the learning of Mengzi. In speaking of destiny, they sometimes call it what Heaven bestows, thereby elucidating the source of Heaven’s mandate; sometimes they call it what arrives without being brought about, thereby attributing it to the natural course of things. Yet an account concerned exclusively with principle does not mix in material force, and one concerned exclusively with material force does not impugn principle. Their words differ, but their meanings agree. Other statements—“There is destiny therein, but the gentleman does not call it nature,” and “There is nature therein, but the gentleman does not call it destiny”—are all means by which Mengzi fully explored the ultimate import of nature and destiny. In these statements, the initial words “there is destiny” speak of principle and material force together. Their purpose is to restrain the human mind, so that people do not go too far. The subsequent words “does not call it destiny” discuss material force alone. Their purpose is to expand the moral mind, so that people do not fall short. How could their meaning ever have lacked completeness?

When Zhuzi discussed destiny, he said, with reference to Shun and Wen in their relations with their sovereigns and fathers, that it depended on what they encountered; with reference to the differing lifespans of Yan Hui and Robber Zhi, he said that it depended on their endowments. In sum, material force differs, and principle follows accordingly: this is indeed what must come to pass as their destiny.

Capacity is that through which effective action is accomplished in the world. Since human nature is good, capacity is also good. Mengzi certainly said, “Doing what is not good is not the fault of one’s capacity.” Yet Yichuan said, “Human nature is invariably good; that which…”

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
所以不善者才也是非有所謬也蓋才發
于性性無不善才出于氣氣則不一此其
所以小異耳至謂氣清則才善氣濁則才
惡者程子也夫旣出於氣矣則禀其清者
其才爲賢爲聖禀其濁者其才爲愚不肖
者宜也又謂君子挾才以爲善小人挾才
以爲不善者溫公也夫旣有所挾矣則以
之爲善善無不至以之爲惡惡無不至者
亦宜也蓋孟子則自其同者而觀之故以
===
爲出於性二子則自其異者而觀之故以
爲雜於惡其意不相遠耳氣也者所以體
天地之塞者也至大至剛孟子固謂吾之
浩然之氣矣而語公孫丑曰是集義所生
者是非有所乖也蓋全於天者不能不壞
于人而修於人者不可不還其天實所以
互發耳至於勉齋所謂氣有昏明則理亦
隨而昏明非以其木之氣盛則仁多而義
少金之氣盛則義多而仁少乎楊雄所謂
punctuated:
所以不善者，才也。是非有所謬也。蓋才發于性，性無不善；才出于氣，氣則不一。此其所以小異耳。至謂「氣清則才善，氣濁則才惡」者，程子也。夫旣出於氣矣，則禀其清者，其才爲賢爲聖；禀其濁者，其才爲愚不肖者，宜也。又謂「君子挾才以爲善，小人挾才以爲不善」者，溫公也。夫旣有所挾矣，則以之爲善，善無不至；以之爲惡，惡無不至者，亦宜也。蓋孟子則自其同者而觀之，故以爲出於性；二子則自其異者而觀之，故以爲雜於惡。其意不相遠耳。

氣也者，所以體天地之塞者也。至大至剛，孟子固謂吾之浩然之氣矣，而語公孫丑曰：「是集義所生者。」是非有所乖也。蓋全於天者，不能不壞于人；而修於人者，不可不還其天。實所以互發耳。至於勉齋所謂「氣有昏明，則理亦隨而昏明」，非以其木之氣盛，則仁多而義少；金之氣盛，則義多而仁少乎？楊雄所謂
translation_en:
…what makes it bad is talent.” This is no error. Talent issues from human nature, and human nature is invariably good; talent also arises from qi, and qi varies. This accounts for the slight difference between these statements. It was Master Cheng who said, “When qi is clear, talent is good; when qi is turbid, talent is bad.” Since talent arises from qi, it is natural that those endowed with clear qi should have the talent to become worthies or sages, while those endowed with turbid qi should have the talent of the foolish and unworthy. It was Sima Guang, Duke Wen, who further said, “The gentleman uses his talent to do good; the petty man uses his talent to do what is not good.” Since they possess talent to employ, it is likewise natural that, when they use it for good, there is no limit to the good they can accomplish, and when they use it for evil, there is no limit to the evil they can accomplish. Mengzi considers talent from the standpoint of what people share, and therefore regards it as issuing from human nature. The other two masters consider it from the standpoint of what differs among people, and therefore regard it as mingled with evil. Their meanings are not far apart.

Qi is that which embodies what fills Heaven and Earth. Supremely great and supremely firm: Mengzi indeed described it as “my vast, flowing qi.” Yet he told Gongsun Chou, “It is produced through the accumulation of righteous deeds.” There is no contradiction here. What is whole as bestowed by Heaven cannot escape impairment through human activity; what is cultivated through human effort must be restored to its heavenly condition. These statements thus illuminate one another. As for Mianzhai’s statement, “Qi may be clouded or clear, and principle accordingly becomes clouded or clear,” is this not because, when the qi of wood predominates, there is more benevolence and less righteousness, whereas when the qi of metal predominates, there is more righteousness and less benevolence? As for what Yang Xiong called…

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
氣也者所適善惡之馬非以其用之於善
則爲善人用之於惡則爲惡人乎蓋勉齋
之語氣也非有戾於集義而楊雄之語氣
也則非所謂浩然其見有淺深耳夫性也
命也才也氣也莫不有是理則莫不有是
氣善乎明道之言曰論性不論氣不備論
氣不論性不明殆有以該乎衆論之極致
而無遺矣吾嘗以是四者而槩論之天授
於人之謂命人受於天之謂性天人未始
===
不一也才所以運乎其氣氣所以發乎其
才才氣未始有離也性命則天理之本原
而統體乎才氣之本才氣則天機之流動
而發揚乎性命之用是固生人之道而不
容於或虧者矣夫何拘於氣稟者物而不
化蔽於物欲者往而不返而人之戕其性
逆其命蕩其才㝠其氣者衆矣此盡性至
命養氣達才之學吾儒之所不容已也夫
性何爲而盡也孟子曰存其心養其性張
punctuated: 「氣也者，所適善惡之馬」，非以其用之於善則爲善人，用之於惡則爲惡人乎？蓋勉齋之語氣也，非有戾於集義；而楊雄之語氣也，則非所謂浩然，其見有淺深耳。夫性也、命也、才也、氣也，莫不有是理，則莫不有是氣。善乎明道之言曰：「論性不論氣，不備；論氣不論性，不明。」殆有以該乎衆論之極致而無遺矣。吾嘗以是四者而槩論之：天授於人之謂命，人受於天之謂性，天人未始不一也；才所以運乎其氣，氣所以發乎其才，才氣未始有離也。性命則天理之本原，而統體乎才氣之本；才氣則天機之流動，而發揚乎性命之用。是固生人之道，而不容於或虧者矣。夫何拘於氣稟者，物而不化；蔽於物欲者，往而不返，而人之戕其性、逆其命、蕩其才、㝠其氣者衆矣！此盡性、至命、養氣、達才之學，吾儒之所不容已也。夫性何爲而盡也？孟子曰：「存其心，養其性。」張
translation_en:
…“Qi is the horse by which one proceeds toward good or evil”—does this not mean that using it for good makes one a good person, while using it for evil makes one an evil person? Mianzhai’s account of qi does not conflict with the accumulation of righteousness; Yang Xiong’s account of qi, however, does not concern what is called the vast, flowing qi. Their insights simply differ in depth. Human nature, Heaven’s mandate, capacity, and qi all possess this principle, and thus all possess this qi. How excellent are Mingdao’s words: “To discuss human nature without discussing qi is incomplete; to discuss qi without discussing human nature is unclear.” These words may well encompass the ultimate import of all these discussions, leaving nothing out.

I have attempted a general account of these four: what Heaven bestows upon human beings is called the mandate; what human beings receive from Heaven is called their nature. Heaven and humanity have never been other than one. Capacity is that through which one’s qi is set in motion; qi is that through which one’s capacity is expressed. Capacity and qi have never been separate. Human nature and Heaven’s mandate are the source of heavenly principle and encompass the foundation of capacity and qi. Capacity and qi are the flowing activity of Heaven’s workings and bring forth the functioning of human nature and Heaven’s mandate. These are indeed the Way of human life, in which no deficiency can be allowed.

Why, then, do those constrained by their endowment of qi become fixed like things and fail to transform, while those obscured by material desires go forth and never return? Many thus injure their nature, defy their mandate, dissipate their capacity, and darken their qi. Hence the learning that fully realizes human nature, attains Heaven’s mandate, nourishes qi, and develops capacity is something we Confucians cannot abandon. How, then, is human nature fully realized? Mengzi said: “Preserve your heart-mind and nourish your nature.” Zhang…

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
子曰善反之則天地之性存焉以此盡性
而清濁厚薄可得而限之耶命何爲而至
也孟子曰莫非命也順受其正子思曰君
子居易以俟命以此立命而貧賤富貴可
得而累之耶欲達其才者吾有得於朱子
矣曰盡其惻隱之才必當至於博施濟衆
盡其羞惡之才必當至於一介不取信斯
言也而脩爲擴充以善其用才有不達者
乎欲養其氣者吾亦得之朱子矣曰率氣
===
在志養氣在直一無不義便自浩然信斯
言也而有事勿忘以篤其功氣有不養者
乎雖然隨處而致力者學也主一而無適
者心也心苟存焉則性自我全命自我立
才自我充氣自我直以之希聖以之希天
皆吾一心之所及也心苟喪焉則性有所
鑿命有所牽才有所滯氣有所餒安于自
棄流于下愚皆吾一心之所致也故夫涵
養省察之功閑邪存誠之道則又進於四
punctuated: 子曰：「善反之，則天地之性存焉。」以此盡性，而清濁厚薄可得而限之耶？命何爲而至也？孟子曰：「莫非命也，順受其正。」子思曰：「君子居易以俟命。」以此立命，而貧賤富貴可得而累之耶？欲達其才者，吾有得於朱子矣。曰：「盡其惻隱之才，必當至於博施濟衆；盡其羞惡之才，必當至於一介不取。」信斯言也，而脩爲擴充，以善其用，才有不達者乎？欲養其氣者，吾亦得之朱子矣。曰：「率氣在志，養氣在直，一無不義，便自浩然。」信斯言也，而有事勿忘，以篤其功，氣有不養者乎？雖然，隨處而致力者，學也；主一而無適者，心也。心苟存焉，則性自我全，命自我立，才自我充，氣自我直。以之希聖，以之希天，皆吾一心之所及也。心苟喪焉，則性有所鑿，命有所牽，才有所滯，氣有所餒。安于自棄，流于下愚，皆吾一心之所致也。故夫涵養省察之功，閑邪存誠之道，則又進於四
translation_en:
…Master Zhang said: “If one is good at returning to it, the nature of Heaven and Earth is preserved.” By fulfilling one’s nature in this way, could one be limited by the clarity or turbidity, richness or thinness of one’s endowment? How does one attain one’s allotted destiny? Mengzi said: “Nothing is outside destiny; one should receive obediently what is proper.” Zisi said: “The gentleman dwells at ease and awaits his destiny.” By establishing one’s destiny in this way, could one be encumbered by poverty and low status, or wealth and high rank? As for developing one’s capacities fully, I have gained an understanding from Master Zhu. He said: “To fulfill one’s capacity for compassion, one must reach the point of extending beneficence widely and aiding the multitude; to fulfill one’s capacity for shame and aversion to wrongdoing, one must reach the point of accepting not even the smallest thing improperly.” If one trusts these words, cultivates and expands these capacities, and thereby puts them to good use, could any capacity remain undeveloped? As for nourishing one’s vital force, I have likewise gained an understanding from Master Zhu. He said: “Directing the vital force depends on the will; nourishing it depends on uprightness. Once there is nothing unrighteous, it naturally becomes vast and flowing.” If one trusts these words, continually applies oneself without forgetting, and thereby makes one’s efforts steadfast, could one’s vital force fail to be nourished?

Nevertheless, what calls for effort in every situation is learning; what holds fast to unity without straying is the heart-mind. If the heart-mind is preserved, then through my own efforts my nature is made whole, my destiny established, my capacities developed, and my vital force made upright. Through it I aspire to sagehood; through it I aspire to Heaven. All these lie within the reach of my single heart-mind. If the heart-mind is lost, however, one’s nature is damaged, one’s destiny constrained, one’s capacities obstructed, and one’s vital force depleted. Becoming content to abandon oneself and sinking into the lowest stupidity—all these are brought about by my own heart-mind. Thus the work of nurturing and examining oneself, and the way of warding off evil and preserving sincerity, go still further than the four…

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
者之大要矣愚生徒事于口耳之末而未
達乎身心之奧所見如斯惟執事矜其愚
而教焉
第四問
晉應槐
同考試官教授萬　批　〔時艱民瘼洞見無遺且考證精詳處斷確當見謂有先憂之志者矣〕
考試官教諭袁　批　〔獲蘇興利此策盡之殆非經生之常談矣錄之以昭適用之才〕
===
考試官教諭顧　批　博雅之學經濟之才
天下有可興之利而亦有可慮之患惟善
計者能圖之夫可興之利莫不有已然之
法也然因襲之弊固有利於前而不能不
壞於後者故善治弊者必原其立法之始
可慮之患固當為未然之防也然法制之
備固有緩於昔而不能不急於今者故善
制變者必豫為可終之圖蓋謀人之國猶
醫者之視病也不胗其受病之原而預防
punctuated:
者之大要矣。愚生徒事于口耳之末，而未達乎身心之奧。所見如斯，惟執事矜其愚而教焉。

第四問
晉應槐
同考試官教授萬批〔時艱民瘼，洞見無遺，且考證精詳，處斷確當，見謂有先憂之志者矣。〕
考試官教諭袁批〔獲蘇興利，此策盡之，殆非經生之常談矣。錄之以昭適用之才。〕
考試官教諭顧批：博雅之學，經濟之才。

天下有可興之利，而亦有可慮之患，惟善計者能圖之。夫可興之利，莫不有已然之法也。然因襲之弊，固有利於前而不能不壞於後者，故善治弊者必原其立法之始。可慮之患，固當為未然之防也。然法制之備，固有緩於昔而不能不急於今者，故善制變者必豫為可終之圖。蓋謀人之國，猶醫者之視病也。不胗其受病之原而預防
translation_en:
…are the great essentials that go beyond these four. This foolish student merely occupies himself with the superficial business of hearing and repeating words, without having grasped the profound workings of body and mind. Such are my views; I ask only that you take pity on my ignorance and instruct me.

Fourth Policy Question
Jin Yinghuai
Associate Examiner Wan, Professor, comments: 〔He sees through the difficulties of the times and the sufferings of the people, leaving nothing unexamined. His investigation of the evidence is also meticulous and thorough, and his judgments sound and appropriate. He may be said to possess the resolve to worry before others do.〕
Examiner Yuan, Instructor, comments: 〔Bringing relief [?] and promoting benefits: this policy essay treats these fully. It is surely beyond the commonplace talk of students of the Classics. It is selected to demonstrate his talent for practical application.〕
Examiner Gu, Instructor, comments: Broad and refined learning; talent for ordering the state and aiding the people.

In the realm there are benefits that can be promoted, but also dangers that warrant concern. Only those skilled in planning can devise measures to address them. For every benefit that can be promoted, there is already an established method. Yet among the abuses arising from perpetuating established practices, there are measures that benefited earlier times but inevitably deteriorate later. Thus those skilled at remedying abuses must trace their legislation back to its beginnings. Against dangers that warrant concern, precautions must certainly be taken before they arise. Yet among the provisions of laws and institutions, there are matters that were less urgent in the past but cannot help being urgent today. Thus those skilled at managing change must devise in advance plans that can be carried through to completion. Planning for another’s state is like a physician examining an illness. If he does not examine the source of the illness and take preventive measures …

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
其元氣之蠹則技無所施不足以起其生
而引人之年不得爲善醫矣今法弊矣而
不尋其始患至矣而不憂其終皆目前之
計也豈得謂之善制治哉夫山西可興之
利屯田鹽法是也而利之容有未興者非
因襲之爲弊乎可慮之患馬政民兵是也
而慮之容有未周者非法制之未備乎愚
書生不知大計然生長兹方目擊桑梓之
弊而竊抱杞人之憂也久矣請據所聞以
爲明問復山西之屯田額設遍於全省而
===
達於
畿甸其爲田幾八百餘萬畝也計存輸幾九
十餘萬石也
國制鎮守之兵以十分之三服農畝而計夫
授田爲自食之計賞罰之例以十二石抵
口分而歲徵六石待不時之需立法之意
欲行之既久則增屯益廣而歲入益充故
民無轉輸之勞而軍遂飽騰之願此寓兵
punctuated:
其元氣之蠹，則技無所施，不足以起其生而引人之年，不得爲善醫矣。今法弊矣，而不尋其始；患至矣，而不憂其終，皆目前之計也，豈得謂之善制治哉？夫山西可興之利，屯田、鹽法是也；而利之容有未興者，非因襲之爲弊乎？可慮之患，馬政、民兵是也；而慮之容有未周者，非法制之未備乎？愚書生不知大計，然生長兹方，目擊桑梓之弊，而竊抱杞人之憂也久矣。請據所聞，以爲明問復。
山西之屯田，額設遍於全省，而達於畿甸。其爲田幾八百餘萬畝也，計存輸幾九十餘萬石也。國制，鎮守之兵以十分之三服農畝，而計夫授田，爲自食之計。賞罰之例，以十二石抵口分，而歲徵六石，待不時之需。立法之意，欲行之既久，則增屯益廣，而歲入益充，故民無轉輸之勞，而軍遂飽騰之願。此寓兵
translation_en:
…the depletion of his vital energy, then the physician’s skills have nowhere to be applied: he cannot restore life and prolong a person’s years, and cannot be called a good physician. Now, when institutions have become corrupt, to fail to examine their beginnings, and when troubles have arrived, to give no thought to their ultimate consequences—these are all calculations confined to the immediate present. How could this be called skillful governance? The benefits that can be developed in Shanxi lie in military agricultural colonies and the salt administration. If some of these benefits remain unrealized, is this not because inherited practices have produced abuses? The troubles that warrant concern lie in horse administration and the militia. If provision against them remains incomplete, is this not because the institutional arrangements are inadequate? I, an ignorant scholar, do not understand grand affairs of state. Yet I was born and raised in this region and have witnessed the abuses afflicting my native place; privately, I have long harbored the anxieties of the man of Qi who feared the sky would fall. Allow me to answer your discerning question on the basis of what I have heard.
Shanxi’s authorized military agricultural colonies are distributed throughout the province and extend into the capital region. Their land amounts to some eight million mu or more, and the grain retained and remitted [?] totals some nine hundred thousand shi or more. Under the dynasty’s regulations, three-tenths of the garrison troops work the fields; land is allotted according to the number of men, enabling them to feed themselves. Under the rules governing rewards and penalties, twelve shi count toward each man’s subsistence allotment, while six shi are collected annually to meet unforeseen needs. The intention behind these regulations was that, after they had operated for some time, the colonies would expand and annual receipts would grow ever more abundant. Thus the people would be spared the toil of transporting supplies, and the troops would fulfill their wish to be well fed and vigorous [?]. This embodies the principle of incorporating soldiers…

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
於農之遺意也邇來升斗之入盡出民力
一兵以上悉仰縣官屯田之弊極矣然豈
法制之原意耶因循之弊積之也屯軍勞
於邊事之繁興而不得力耕以自養正糧
歸於屯種之餘丁而僅徵餘粒以上倉且
豪民巨姓利屯糧之輕也而包佃之弊同
於盜買武弁旗舍幸屯軍之逃也而租課
之入甚於强占是種之者且非餘丁矣勸
課無良法而科擾之害及於雞豚徵輸無
===
常例而折閱之第甚於加賦是存之者亦
不能安於田畝矣名存而實亡誠如執事
之憂者夫見屯未清況望其充拓開退以
興未就之緒耶然今日之急勢且燃眉飛
輓之苦不啻三十鍾而致一石矣而屯田
之議谷終已耶故議而行之其說有四焉
曰稽原額謂新屯卒未置矣而見存之田
不可復畝而正界乎曰課餘丁謂正軍已
遠戍矣而優閒之丁不可勞來以勸相乎
punctuated: 於農之遺意也。邇來升斗之入，盡出民力；一兵以上，悉仰縣官。屯田之弊極矣，然豈法制之原意耶？因循之弊積之也。屯軍勞於邊事之繁興，而不得力耕以自養；正糧歸於屯種之餘丁，而僅徵餘粒以上倉。且豪民巨姓利屯糧之輕也，而包佃之弊同於盜買；武弁旗舍幸屯軍之逃也，而租課之入甚於强占。是種之者且非餘丁矣。勸課無良法，而科擾之害及於雞豚；徵輸無常例，而折閱之第甚於加賦。是存之者亦不能安於田畝矣。名存而實亡，誠如執事之憂者。夫見屯未清，況望其充拓開退，以興未就之緒耶？然今日之急，勢且燃眉，飛輓之苦，不啻三十鍾而致一石矣。而屯田之議谷終已耶？故議而行之，其說有四焉：曰稽原額，謂新屯卒未置矣，而見存之田不可復畝而正界乎？曰課餘丁，謂正軍已遠戍矣，而優閒之丁不可勞來以勸相乎？
translation_en:
…the surviving intent of the ancient practice of embedding soldiers in agriculture. Of late, every peck and pint of revenue has come entirely from the people's labor, and every single soldier depends upon the government for support. The abuses of the military agricultural colonies have reached an extreme. Yet could this have been the original intent of the institutions? These abuses have accumulated through inertia. The colony soldiers are worn out by the constant demands of frontier affairs and cannot devote themselves to farming to support themselves. Responsibility for the regular grain quota falls to the surplus males of military households who cultivate the colonies, yet only the remaining grain is collected for delivery to the granaries. Moreover, powerful commoners and great families take advantage of the light grain levy on colony lands: their monopolization of tenancies is an abuse equivalent to illicit purchase. Military officers, bannermen, and hereditary military scions welcome the flight of colony soldiers: their extraction of rents is worse than forcible occupation. Thus even those who cultivate the land are no longer the surplus males of military households. There are no sound methods for encouraging and supervising cultivation, while oppressive exactions reach even to chickens and pigs. There are no fixed rules for collection and delivery, while the losses incurred [?] are worse than an increase in taxation. Thus even those who remain cannot work their fields in peace. The colonies survive in name but have ceased to exist in substance—just as you, honored sir, have feared.

If even the existing colonies have not been put in order, how can one hope to expand them and open up land [?], thereby advancing this unfinished undertaking? Yet today's emergency is as urgent as fire singeing the eyebrows. The burden of hurried grain transport is such that it costs no less than thirty zhong to deliver a single shi. Can discussion of the military agricultural colonies then simply cease [?]? There are therefore four proposals to deliberate upon and implement. The first is to audit the original quotas. Even if new colonies cannot yet be established, can the existing lands not be remeasured and their boundaries corrected? The second is to supervise the farming of surplus household males. Even though the regular soldiers have gone to distant garrisons, can those household males who remain at leisure not be comforted and encouraged, and urged and assisted in cultivation?

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
曰一甲令謂原額之也兼幷而移坵者必
懲以法不得彼罰而此貸本折之議近齋
而遠負者必剷其平不致甲累而乙休獨
不可裁於今而示之信矣乎曰墾塞田謂
三關以北天城以西田多膏腴而不盡墾
者列柵以為守遊騎以為巡以防寇鈔而
興屯利者獨不可昉於昔而斷然行之矣
乎夫四者皆屯政之所當講者也四說既
行則屯政必舉而軍儲之不濟者未之有
===
也河東之顆鹽結于風日而不煩於煎湅
其額制歲僅三十餘萬引也及續增亦不
越四十二萬引也
國初開中之法既省餽運之勞而坐收實邊
之利掣支之度定以常股之制而無存積
之名立法之意則以天產不齊而歲用有
限故其制之額也甚廉而徵之商也甚便
此官民兩利之中制也邇年以來樂募之
商十無二三鹽課之逋幾至百萬而權鹽
punctuated:
曰一甲令，謂原額之也，兼幷而移坵者，必懲以法，不得彼罰而此貸；本折之議，近齋而遠負者，必剷其平，不致甲累而乙休，獨不可裁於今而示之信矣乎？曰墾塞田，謂三關以北、天城以西，田多膏腴而不盡墾者，列柵以為守，遊騎以為巡，以防寇鈔而興屯利者，獨不可昉於昔而斷然行之矣乎？夫四者，皆屯政之所當講者也。四說既行，則屯政必舉，而軍儲之不濟者，未之有也。
河東之顆鹽，結于風日，而不煩於煎湅。其額制，歲僅三十餘萬引也；及續增，亦不越四十二萬引也。國初開中之法，既省餽運之勞，而坐收實邊之利。掣支之度，定以常股之制，而無存積之名。立法之意，則以天產不齊而歲用有限，故其制之額也甚廉，而徵之商也甚便。此官民兩利之中制也。邇年以來，樂募之商，十無二三；鹽課之逋，幾至百萬，而權鹽
translation_en:
…Next, unify the regulations [?]. This means that, concerning the original allotment [?], those who annex holdings and alter plot boundaries must be punished according to law: one must not be punished while another is excused. In matters of payment in kind or its commuted equivalent, where those nearby enjoy an advantage while those farther away bear the burden [?], the inequity must be eliminated [?], so that one party is not encumbered while another rests at ease. Could these matters not be settled now and the rules shown to be trustworthy? Next, cultivate land along the frontier. North of the Three Passes and west of Tiancheng, much fertile land remains uncultivated. Set up palisades for defense and mounted patrols for surveillance, thereby preventing enemy raids and realizing the benefits of military farming. Could we not follow past precedents and resolutely put this into practice? These four matters all require consideration in administering military agricultural colonies. Once the four proposals are implemented, their administration will surely improve, and military provisions cannot fail to suffice.
The granular salt of Hedong crystallizes through wind and sunlight, without requiring the labor of boiling and refining. Its prescribed annual quota was only a little over 300,000 salt certificates; even after subsequent increases, it did not exceed 420,000. The early dynasty’s system of exchanging grain deliveries for salt certificates saved the labor of transporting provisions while readily securing the benefit of well-provisioned frontiers. Procedures for drawing lots and collecting salt were fixed under the regular-allotment system, with no category of reserve stocks. The intention behind this legislation was that natural production fluctuated, whereas annual consumption was limited. Thus the quota was set quite modestly, and the terms on which merchants were called upon to participate were convenient. This was a balanced arrangement benefiting both government and people. In recent years, however, scarcely two or three merchants in ten have been willing to participate; salt-revenue arrears have approached a million, and the administration of the salt monopoly …

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
之政弊矣是豈法制之初意耶商人之累
貽之也置閏歲之偶獲而餘鹽之議興自
餘鹽議興而司計者藉口以取盈矣償數
歲之積逋而超支之法立自超支法立而
常股者由是而益滯矣況撈採之不精則
美惡殊估請乞之無時則市價攜貳計利
於商者亦已微矣守者未給而復促其見
年之例貨猶未行而已速其還中之銀取
必於官者又太銳矣利盡而蠹生誠如執
===
事所云者夫見年之額已不可登況望其
積附餘羨以補百萬之逋耶但顆鹽之利
昔有成效實錢塞下可省數十郡餽運之
費也而恤商之議可弗講乎故存而恤之
其要有五焉曰時採納謂地力有數不竭
其澤也商貨有限不窮其資也曰實料采
謂撈採之時詰姦易疎以惡作美以尠作
盈皆足病商故勤稽察而賞罰必明則二
弊除矣曰均掣放謂一歲之間平蹋有期
punctuated:
之政弊矣。是豈法制之初意耶？商人之累貽之也。置閏歲之偶獲，而餘鹽之議興；自餘鹽議興，而司計者藉口以取盈矣。償數歲之積逋，而超支之法立；自超支法立，而常股者由是而益滯矣。況撈採之不精，則美惡殊估；請乞之無時，則市價攜貳。計利於商者，亦已微矣。守者未給，而復促其見年之例；貨猶未行，而已速其還中之銀。取必於官者，又太銳矣。利盡而蠹生，誠如執事所云者。夫見年之額已不可登，況望其積附餘羨，以補百萬之逋耶？但顆鹽之利，昔有成效，實錢塞下，可省數十郡餽運之費也。而恤商之議，可弗講乎？
故存而恤之，其要有五焉：曰時採納，謂地力有數，不竭其澤也；商貨有限，不窮其資也。曰實料采，謂撈採之時，詰姦易疎，以惡作美，以尠作盈，皆足病商，故勤稽察而賞罰必明，則二弊除矣。曰均掣放，謂一歲之間，平蹋有期。
translation_en:
…the administration of salt has fallen into disorder. Can this have been the original intention of the regulations? It has been brought about by the burdens imposed on merchants. Provision for the occasional yield of an intercalary year [?] gave rise to the proposal concerning surplus salt. Once this proposal arose, those administering revenue used it as a pretext for extracting the full quota. To discharge arrears accumulated over several years, a system of advance disbursement was established. Once that system was established, salt under the regular allotments became still more delayed. Moreover, when salt is not carefully harvested, good and poor grades command different prices; when requests for grants of salt occur without fixed times, market prices become unsettled. The profit left to merchants is already meager. Those waiting have not yet received their allotments, yet they are again pressed to meet the current year’s prescribed obligations. Their goods have not yet sold, yet they are already hurried to remit the silver for renewed salt contracts. The insistence on securing payment for the government is excessively harsh. Profit disappears and abuses arise, exactly as you have said. If even the current year’s quota cannot be met, how can one expect accumulated additional surpluses to make up arrears of a million? Yet the benefits of granular salt were demonstrably effective in the past: supplying cash to the frontier [?] could save the transport expenses of several dozen prefectures. Can proposals to relieve merchants therefore go undiscussed?
There are five essentials for sustaining and relieving them. The first is timely harvesting and delivery. The land’s productive capacity has its bounds, and its bounty must not be exhausted; merchants’ resources are limited, and their capital must not be drained. The second is honest assessment of the harvest. During harvesting, scrutiny of fraud is easily neglected: inferior salt is passed off as good, and short quantities as full allotments. Both can harm merchants. Thus, if inspections are diligent and rewards and punishments clearly enforced, these two abuses will be eliminated. The third is equitable inspection and release of salt allotments. This means that, within each year, leveling and treading [?] have their appointed times …

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
寡則易齒多則易壅皆足病商故約歲課
而調停適中則二獘除矣曰絕請乞謂多
減價以估而奪商利也曰禁私販謂多窩
居市肆而滯公貨也五者皆鹽法之所當
講者也五弊旣去則商利自厚而官課之
不登者未之有也諸邊牧馬之政我
朝酌古而爲之制
兩畿河南牧之在民陝西遼東牧之在官然
且有茶易之馬馬故諸邊雖不盡仰於官
===
而買補於民者尚有期也山西行太僕寺
之設與陝西遼東等而備禦之馬獨不在
官不在民穽其意與法而失之矣孳牧僅
存乎虛名而買補倚之爲長策於是乎椿
朋不足括於贓罰贓罰不足請於
京運是官之累也官給其一而私倍其二前
運未俵而後買復繼是民之累也蓋民不
皆上産也中人之産不及一馬而室已懸
磬況絡繹而來者不止一馬乎官不皆才
punctuated:
寡則易齒，多則易壅，皆足病商。故約歲課，而調停適中，則二獘除矣。曰絕請乞，謂多減價以估而奪商利也。曰禁私販，謂多窩居市肆而滯公貨也。五者皆鹽法之所當講者也。五弊旣去，則商利自厚，而官課之不登者，未之有也。
諸邊牧馬之政，我朝酌古而爲之制。兩畿、河南牧之在民，陝西、遼東牧之在官，然且有茶易之馬。馬故諸邊雖不盡仰於官，而買補於民者尚有期也。山西行太僕寺之設，與陝西、遼東等，而備禦之馬獨不在官，不在民，穽其意與法而失之矣。孳牧僅存乎虛名，而買補倚之爲長策。於是乎椿朋不足，括於贓罰；贓罰不足，請於京運。是官之累也。官給其一，而私倍其二；前運未俵，而後買復繼。是民之累也。蓋民不皆上産也，中人之産不及一馬，而室已懸磬，況絡繹而來者不止一馬乎？官不皆才
translation_en:
…When quantities are small, the order is easily manipulated [?]; when large, congestion readily occurs. Both can harm merchants. Thus, by setting the annual quota and making suitable adjustments, these two abuses can be eliminated. The fourth measure is to put an end to requests for favors: these frequently involve purchases at reduced valuations, depriving merchants of their profits. The fifth is to prohibit private trafficking: illicit dealers frequently shelter in shops and market premises, holding up the sale of officially authorized salt. All five measures deserve consideration in administering the salt laws. Once these five abuses are eliminated, merchants’ profits will naturally increase; never then would government revenue fall short.
For horse breeding along the frontiers, our dynasty established regulations after considering ancient practices. In the two metropolitan regions and Henan, the people rear the horses; in Shaanxi and Liaodong, the government does so. There are also horses obtained by exchanging tea. Thus [?], although the frontier regions do not depend entirely on government supplies, purchases of replacement horses from the people still take place at fixed intervals. Shanxi’s Branch Court of the Imperial Stud was established on the same basis as those of Shaanxi and Liaodong. Yet responsibility for its defense horses alone rests neither with the government nor with the people: the intent and regulations have been undermined and lost [?]. Breeding and pasturing horses survive in name only, while purchasing replacements is relied upon as a lasting policy. When the reserve and pooled horse funds are insufficient, money is scraped together from confiscations and fines; when these are insufficient, remittances from the capital are requested. This is a burden on the government. The government supplies one share, while private contributions amount to twice that; before one shipment has been distributed, another round of purchases follows. This is a burden on the people. For not all households are wealthy. The property of a household of middling means is worth less than a single horse, and its home is already as bare as a suspended chime stone. How much worse when the demands arrive one after another, for more than a single horse! Nor are all officials capable…

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
良也門攤之較不得其平則控訴無所況
解俵之際倚之爲姦乎及其給馬於軍也
視之若寄蓋稽考之令一疎則藉之爲衣
食之資而芻牧不盡其材耗折之禁一寬
則規免於征調之苦而瘦損不償其直倒
死無日則買補無時山西之民無望其復
蘇矣議者曰招商以緩民力然估多未酬
而商無所利其誰應招耶曰寄養以責有
司然一身而有二役則民不堪命是其爲
害不更烈耶無已則有四計焉曰重僕權
===
謂
國初僕臣之設率皆極選巡部按治比視憲
察載在
聖諭及
勑旨者昭然可考故必得是人以稱點視之職
而後以孳牧之政兼攝之可也曰覈牧地
謂
國初牧地與屯田竝額在在有之令不爲租
punctuated: 良也。門攤之較不得其平，則控訴無所，況解俵之際倚之爲姦乎？及其給馬於軍也，視之若寄。蓋稽考之令一疎，則藉之爲衣食之資，而芻牧不盡其材；耗折之禁一寬，則規免於征調之苦，而瘦損不償其直。倒死無日，則買補無時，山西之民無望其復蘇矣。議者曰：「招商以緩民力。」然估多未酬，而商無所利，其誰應招耶？曰：「寄養以責有司。」然一身而有二役，則民不堪命，是其爲害不更烈耶？無已，則有四計焉。曰：「重僕權。」謂國初僕臣之設，率皆極選，巡部按治，比視憲察，載在聖諭及勑旨者，昭然可考。故必得是人以稱點視之職，而後以孳牧之政兼攝之可也。曰：「覈牧地。」謂國初牧地與屯田竝額，在在有之，令不爲租
translation_en:
…and upright. When assessments apportioned among households [?] are inequitable, there is nowhere to lodge a complaint; how much worse when the transport and distribution of horses become opportunities for fraud? Once horses are issued to the troops, they treat them as merely lodged in their care. If inspection requirements become lax, they use the horses as a source of food and clothing, while failing through proper feeding and pasturing to develop their full capabilities. If prohibitions against losses become lax, they scheme to escape the hardships of military mobilization, yet pay no compensation for the horses’ loss of condition or value. With horses liable to collapse and die at any time, purchases of replacements never cease. The people of Shanxi have no hope of recovering.

Some propose: “Recruit merchants to ease the burden on the people.” Yet much of the assessed price remains unpaid, and merchants have nothing to gain: who would answer the call? Others propose: “Place the horses in foster care and hold the responsible officials accountable.” Yet if one person must perform two services, the people cannot bear the demands. Would this not cause still greater harm?

If action is unavoidable, there are four measures. The first is: “Strengthen the authority of the Court of Imperial Stud.” At the founding of the dynasty, officials appointed to the Court of Imperial Stud were generally selected with the utmost care. They toured their jurisdictions to investigate and administer affairs, with standing comparable to that of censorial inspectors. This is clearly verifiable in the imperial instructions and edicts. Suitable men must therefore be obtained to fulfill the duty of inspecting horses; they may then concurrently assume responsibility for breeding and pasturing them.

The second is: “Verify the pasturelands.” At the founding of the dynasty, pasturelands, like military agricultural lands, had prescribed allocations and existed everywhere. Now [?], unless they have become lands leased out…

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
佃之屯則隱於豪右之門矣況三關附近
又多豐壙水甘草軟之地乎曰定飼法謂
僕臣旣重牧地復覈然後卽水泉便地置
監牧孳種舉圉槽餧養之法明敎駣攻駒
之度悉如陜西遼東監苑之制而酌處之
可也曰嚴點閘謂廉視不實則處補徒費
故嚴爲令格而使作姦犯竊微利爲馬厲
者不得以情貸之可也夫官牧旣興則私
買自省廉視旣嚴則倒損不多馬政庶幾
===
其可興乎嚴科擾之禁而分外之誅求必
法均調停之術而役外之雜調必復此固
去其害中之害也昔人謂寛一分則民受
一分之賜卽此其機乎三關民兵之戍
國初無是制也蓋屛衛之地悉倚雲中屯戍
之卒坐守重鎮軍儲且不需之於民矣況
藉之爲守禦之備矣乎其後以三關險要
切爲禦虜之防而修守之議興然猶未及
於澤潞而歲且四更民猶未甚病也邇來
punctuated: 佃之屯，則隱於豪右之門矣，況三關附近又多豐壙水甘草軟之地乎？曰定飼法，謂僕臣旣重，牧地復覈，然後卽水泉便地置監牧孳種，舉圉槽餧養之法，明敎駣攻駒之度，悉如陜西遼東監苑之制而酌處之可也。曰嚴點閘，謂廉視不實，則處補徒費，故嚴爲令格，而使作姦犯竊微利、爲馬厲者，不得以情貸之可也。夫官牧旣興，則私買自省；廉視旣嚴，則倒損不多，馬政庶幾其可興乎？嚴科擾之禁，而分外之誅求必法；均調停之術，而役外之雜調必復。此固去其害中之害也。昔人謂寛一分則民受一分之賜，卽此其機乎？三關民兵之戍，國初無是制也。蓋屛衛之地，悉倚雲中屯戍之卒，坐守重鎮，軍儲且不需之於民矣，況藉之爲守禦之備矣乎？其後以三關險要，切爲禦虜之防，而修守之議興，然猶未及於澤潞，而歲且四更，民猶未甚病也。邇來
translation_en:
…farmland under tenancy [?], it lies concealed among the holdings of powerful families. Moreover, near the Three Passes there are many broad, open tracts with sweet water and tender grass.

“Establish feeding regulations” means that, once the officials responsible for horses have been accorded due importance and the pasturelands have again been verified, supervised breeding herds should be established on suitable land near springs and streams. Methods of feeding horses in stables and at troughs should be instituted, and standards for schooling young horses and breaking in colts made clear. All this may follow the regulations of the imperial horse pastures in Shaanxi and Liaodong, with adjustments as appropriate.

“Make inspections stringent” means that, if inspections are not conducted honestly, arranging for replacement horses merely wastes resources. Strict regulations should therefore be established, so that those who commit fraud or theft for petty gain and thereby harm the horses cannot be pardoned out of personal consideration. Once official horse breeding flourishes, private purchases will naturally diminish; once inspections become stringent, losses through death will be few. Might the administration of horses then have some prospect of revival?

Strictly enforce the prohibition on harassing exactions, and invariably punish demands beyond prescribed obligations. Ensure equitable arrangements for adjusting service obligations, and invariably exempt people from miscellaneous levies beyond their required service. This would indeed remove the worst of these abuses. People of old said that each measure of leniency brings the people a corresponding measure of benefit. Is this not the opportunity to achieve it?

As for militia garrison duty at the Three Passes, there was no such system at the founding of the dynasty. This defensive region relied entirely on the soldiers stationed in military colonies and garrisons at Yunzhong to hold its major strategic strongholds. Even military provisions were not demanded of the people; how much less were the people themselves relied upon to provide defensive forces! Later, because the strategic terrain of the Three Passes was crucial to defense against the northern invaders, proposals arose to repair the fortifications and guard them. Yet these obligations still did not extend to Zezhou and Luzhou, and there were four rotations each year, so the people were not yet gravely burdened. Recently…

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
則勾及於全省而一歲僅分於兩番名名爲
丁壯實同籍兵名爲修守實同軍戍民始
不勝其苦矣一縣之勾稽騷及合境一人
之資裝費及合甲有司不勝其繁矣夫天
下之重鎮九而山西之重鎮二山西之爲
郡四而邊鎮之爲郡二是以其勢不得以
不亟宣大之供億日滋而三關之備不容
於緩新營之靡費歲增而調遣之役不免
於身是以其民不得以不竭夫民財既不
===
可省民兵又不可恃重關之地寧不可寒
心耶議者謂民丁可罷然額兵有限半脫
尺籍也而奚以恃乎又謂修守可已然虜
踰雲朔如闖門庭也而奚以備乎無已則
有三策焉曰緩雜征謂民用其三則父子
以離今供邊之地不止於三矣沉如材木
之採取料銀之徵解皆額外費也不可緩
之於茲省乎曰議援濟謂庶功興在事役
均今
punctuated:
則勾及於全省，而一歲僅分於兩番，名名爲丁壯，實同籍兵；名爲修守，實同軍戍。民始不勝其苦矣。一縣之勾稽，騷及合境；一人之資裝，費及合甲。有司不勝其繁矣。夫天下之重鎮九，而山西之重鎮二；山西之爲郡四，而邊鎮之爲郡二。是以其勢不得以不亟。宣大之供億日滋，而三關之備不容於緩；新營之靡費歲增，而調遣之役不免於身。是以其民不得以不竭。夫民財既不可省，民兵又不可恃，重關之地，寧不可寒心耶？
議者謂民丁可罷，然額兵有限，半脫尺籍也，而奚以恃乎？又謂修守可已，然虜踰雲朔，如闖門庭也，而奚以備乎？無已，則有三策焉。曰緩雜征，謂民用其三，則父子以離。今供邊之地，不止於三矣。沉如材木之採取、料銀之徵解，皆額外費也，不可緩之於茲省乎？曰議援濟，謂庶功興，在事役均。今
translation_en:
…recruitment now extends throughout the province, with only two rotations in a year. Nominally they are called able-bodied men [the transcription repeats “nominally” here, ?], but in reality they are like registered soldiers; nominally they undertake fortification and defense, but in reality they serve as military garrison troops. The people have consequently become unable to bear their suffering. Recruitment checks in a single county disturb its entire territory; the cost of equipping a single man falls upon his entire jia household group. The responsible officials cannot cope with these burdensome demands. Of the empire’s nine major frontier commands, two are in Shanxi; of Shanxi’s four prefectures, two belong to frontier commands. Thus its circumstances cannot but be urgent. The supplies demanded by Xuanfu and Datong increase daily, while preparations at the Three Passes admit of no delay. Expenditure on the new encampments increases yearly, while the people themselves cannot escape service on deployment. Thus the people cannot but be exhausted. With expenditure from the people’s resources admitting of no reduction, and the civilian militia offering no reliable support, is this region of vital passes not cause for chilling apprehension?
Some argue that civilian recruits can be discharged. Yet the authorized troop strength is limited, and half the soldiers have slipped off the military rolls: on whom, then, could we rely? Others argue that fortification and defense can cease. Yet the enemy crosses Yun and Shuo as though bursting into our own gateway and courtyard: how, then, could we defend ourselves? If there is no alternative, there are three measures. The first is to defer miscellaneous levies. It is said that when three shares [three-tenths of the people’s resources?] are taken, fathers and sons are driven apart. In the regions supplying the frontier today, the burden exceeds three shares. Furthermore [?], such demands as procuring timber and collecting and remitting silver for materials are all expenses beyond the authorized quota. Could these not be deferred in this province? The second is to deliberate on assistance and relief. It is said that the various public undertakings flourish when service obligations are evenly apportioned. Now…

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
畿輔以西大河以北安危視全晉全晉之地
安危視三關此而不輯是中原之㢩脣也
故修守之費不可議派於他省乎曰還額
稅謂通融以時則制用不匱如宣鎮有急
當三關無事也民糧之借顧一時權宜計
耳今三關急矣不可議復於本省矣乎夫
諸役既省則叢負可釋實費既分則力役
不困民病庶幾其少瘳乎以是而獨借其
力焉則必厚其資而使之樂於趨勞也必
===
簡其衆而使之人不浮食也民卽爲兵而
訓練之必精兵皆可戰而器械之必利此
固收其害中之利也昔人謂上不病國中
不害法下不病民卽此其術乎夫是四者
屯田鹽法皆今日濟邊之良儲也馬政民
兵皆今日備邊之實用也誠不可一日而
不講矣然制不更始則不可以圖大故屯
田也鹽法也二政之利所宜亟復者也計
不顧卻則不可以慮終故馬政也民兵也
punctuated:
畿輔以西，大河以北，安危視全晉；全晉之地，安危視三關。此而不輯，是中原之㢩脣也。故修守之費，不可議派於他省乎？曰還額稅，謂通融以時，則制用不匱。如宣鎮有急，當三關無事也，民糧之借，顧一時權宜計耳。今三關急矣，不可議復於本省矣乎？夫諸役既省，則叢負可釋；實費既分，則力役不困。民病庶幾其少瘳乎？以是而獨借其力焉，則必厚其資，而使之樂於趨勞也；必簡其衆，而使之人不浮食也。民卽爲兵，而訓練之必精；兵皆可戰，而器械之必利。此固收其害中之利也。昔人謂，上不病國，中不害法，下不病民，卽此其術乎？
夫是四者，屯田、鹽法，皆今日濟邊之良儲也；馬政、民兵，皆今日備邊之實用也。誠不可一日而不講矣！然制不更始，則不可以圖大，故屯田也、鹽法也，二政之利所宜亟復者也。計不顧卻，則不可以慮終，故馬政也、民兵也，
translation_en:
…west of the metropolitan region and north of the Yellow River, security depends on Shanxi as a whole; the security of Shanxi, in turn, depends on the Three Passes. If this region is not brought to order, it is as though the protective lips of the Central Plain were stripped away [?]. Thus, could we not consider apportioning the costs of repairing and defending the fortifications among other provinces? The third proposal is to restore the regular tax allotment: timely adjustments in the allocation of resources would prevent shortages in expenditure. When the Xuanfu garrison faced an emergency while the Three Passes were at peace, borrowing the people's tax grain was merely a temporary expedient. Now the Three Passes face an emergency. Could we not consider restoring this grain to our own province? Once the various service obligations are reduced, the accumulated burdens can be lifted; once actual expenses are shared, labor service will no longer exhaust the people. Might their distress then be somewhat relieved? If, on this basis, we are to call specifically upon their strength, we must provide them with ample resources so that they willingly undertake the toil. We must select their numbers carefully so that no one consumes provisions without contributing. Once civilians become soldiers, their training must be thorough; when all the soldiers are capable of fighting, their weapons and equipment must be effective. This would indeed secure benefits amid the disadvantages. People of old spoke of neither afflicting the state above, nor impairing the laws in between, nor afflicting the people below. Is this not the method for doing so?
Of these four matters, military agricultural colonies and the salt administration are both valuable sources of supplies for sustaining the frontier today; horse administration and the militia are both practical means of defending it. Truly, they must not go unexamined for even a day! Yet unless institutions are renewed, great undertakings cannot be planned. Thus, the benefits of the two systems—military agricultural colonies and salt administration—should urgently be restored. Unless plans take setbacks into account, their eventual consequences cannot be considered. Thus, as for horse administration and the militia…

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
二法之害所宜長慮者也鼓不調之瑟者
不必易置其絃解而更張之則音無不和
矣處厝火之薪者不可因謂之安徙而豫
防之則勢不及爇矣如是而計不足以興
利謀不足以却害者未之有也不然則前
有可彷之制而猶襲其相因之弊後有無
窮之害而猶幸其目前之安全晉之地吾
未知其所終也已雖然此亦事至而制曲
區而防之耳要亦有本焉本之不先而惟
===
末之圖終亦因循之計非謀國之令圖也
故趙充國便宜罷兵而紛紛之議始解貴
專斷也范祥始制鈔法而邊郡之儲以實
貴閑中也李克用以馬上定河朔而馬以
三萬為多矣韓魏公以義勇威西夏而民
以籍兵為厲矣是皆籌邊者利弊之本實
也故獨斷之計不早則新屯之置終阻於
衆言之淆亂屯田之議不復則鹽本之權
無裨於邊方之待哺養一騎卒當五步兵
punctuated:
二法之害，所宜長慮者也。鼓不調之瑟者，不必易置其絃，解而更張之，則音無不和矣。處厝火之薪者，不可因謂之安，徙而豫防之，則勢不及爇矣。如是而計不足以興利、謀不足以却害者，未之有也。不然，則前有可彷之制，而猶襲其相因之弊；後有無窮之害，而猶幸其目前之安。全晉之地，吾未知其所終也已。

雖然，此亦事至而制，曲區而防之耳。要亦有本焉。本之不先，而惟末之圖，終亦因循之計，非謀國之令圖也。故趙充國便宜罷兵，而紛紛之議始解，貴專斷也；范祥始制鈔法，而邊郡之儲以實，貴閑中也。李克用以馬上定河朔，而馬以三萬為多矣；韓魏公以義勇威西夏，而民以籍兵為厲矣。是皆籌邊者利弊之本實也。故獨斷之計不早，則新屯之置終阻於衆言之淆亂；屯田之議不復，則鹽本之權無裨於邊方之待哺。養一騎卒，當五步兵
translation_en:
…the harms of these two systems require consideration for the long term. Someone playing a se whose strings are out of tune need not replace its strings: loosen and retune them, and every note will be harmonious. Someone keeping fire beneath a pile of fuel must not therefore pronounce it safe: move the fuel and take precautions beforehand, and the danger will never develop into a blaze. There has never been a case in which, with such measures, plans proved inadequate to promote benefits and counsels inadequate to avert harm. Otherwise, although there are earlier institutions to emulate, their accumulated abuses will still be perpetuated; although limitless harm lies ahead, people will still trust to their present security. I cannot tell what will ultimately become of the whole territory of Jin.

Even so, these measures merely respond to events as they arise and guard against them piecemeal [?]. There are also fundamentals. Unless these receive priority, planning solely for secondary matters will ultimately amount to following established routines, rather than an excellent strategy for the state. Thus, only when Zhao Chongguo proposed the expedient of demobilizing the troops did the competing arguments subside: what mattered was decisive authority. When Fan Xiang first instituted the salt-certificate system, the frontier commanderies’ reserves were replenished: what mattered was “xian zhong” [?]. Li Keyong pacified Heshuo on horseback, yet thirty thousand horses were considered numerous. Duke Wei, Han Qi, used the volunteer militia to overawe Western Xia, yet the people regarded enrollment as soldiers as an affliction. These are all fundamental realities concerning the benefits and harms that planners of frontier affairs must consider. Thus, unless a decisive plan is adopted early, the establishment of new military agricultural colonies will ultimately be obstructed by the confusion of competing opinions. Unless proposals for military agricultural colonies are revived, control over salt capital will do nothing to feed the frontier regions awaiting sustenance. Maintaining one cavalry soldier costs as much as maintaining five infantrymen…

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
善禦虜者不廣馬以自恃兵貴土著尤貴
屯駐善守禦者不籍民以積弱故古者今
之鑒也往者來之徵也書曰事不師古匪
説攸聞謀王斷國者可以深長思矣此則
執事事也執事責也而非草茅之所與知
也幸進而教之
第五問
翟廷楠
同考試官教授宋　批〔邊情時務士子類能言之多剿〕
〔陳言惟是蓋以眩觀視窮究本源處分明當獨見此作讀之令人瞿然〕
===
考試官教諭袁　批〔深達時宜不苟作者〕
考試官教諭顧　批〔幾要務根本之論非有見者不〕
〔能道也〕
善謀國者固貴於審天下之勢尤貴於決
天下之幾夫勢者事之有形者也幾者變
之未動者也有形者易制未動者難圖何
也事變之出其來無窮而幾微之萌其朕
莫測善應變者能先見而豫圖之詳察而
punctuated:
善禦虜者，不廣馬以自恃。兵貴土著，尤貴屯駐；善守禦者，不籍民以積弱。故古者，今之鑒也；往者，來之徵也。《書》曰：「事不師古，匪説攸聞。」謀王斷國者，可以深長思矣。此則執事事也，執事責也，而非草茅之所與知也。幸進而教之。

第五問
翟廷楠
同考試官教授宋批〔邊情時務，士子類能言之，多剿〕〔陳言，惟是蓋以眩觀視。窮究本源，處分明當，獨見此作，讀之令人瞿然。〕
考試官教諭袁批〔深達時宜，不苟作者。〕
考試官教諭顧批〔幾要務根本之論，非有見者不〕〔能道也。〕

善謀國者，固貴於審天下之勢，尤貴於決天下之幾。夫勢者，事之有形者也；幾者，變之未動者也。有形者易制，未動者難圖，何也？事變之出，其來無窮，而幾微之萌，其朕莫測。善應變者，能先見而豫圖之，詳察而
translation_en:
Those skilled at resisting the enemy do not expand their horse stocks and rely on them for security. In military forces, local roots are valuable, and settled garrisons especially so; those skilled in defense do not register the common people for military service and thereby compound their weakness. Thus antiquity is a mirror for the present, and past events provide evidence for what is to come. The Book of Documents says: “In conducting affairs, if you do not take antiquity as your teacher, I, Yue, have heard of no such thing.” Those who counsel the king [?] and decide affairs of state should ponder this deeply. These are your affairs, honored sir, and your responsibilities; they are beyond the knowledge of an obscure man outside official service such as myself. I hope you will favor me with instruction.

Fifth Policy Question
Zhai Tingnan

Comment by Associate Examiner Song, Professor: “Candidates generally can discuss frontier conditions and current affairs, but most merely plagiarize established sayings, apparently to dazzle the reader. Only this essay probes matters to their source and proposes clear and appropriate measures. Reading it makes one sit up in surprise.”

Comment by Examiner Yuan, Instructor: “A writer who thoroughly understands the needs of the times and does not write carelessly.”

Comment by Examiner Gu, Instructor: “A discussion of critical matters and fundamental concerns [?]; no one without insight could express this.”

Those skilled in planning for the state certainly value assessing the configuration of affairs throughout the realm, but they value still more making decisions at the first signs of change. The configuration of affairs is what has already taken visible form; the incipient moment is change that has not yet begun to unfold. What has taken form is easy to control, while what has not yet stirred is difficult to plan for. Why is this? Events and changes arise without end, while the traces of their earliest beginnings are impossible to fathom. Those skilled in responding to change can foresee it and plan for it beforehand, examine it closely and…

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
早決之則患銷於未萌禍弭於未著力用
寡而功成多財不匱而事就速天下陰被
其福而莫知其所以然也苟或玩其變而
緩於圖忽其幾而輕於應安未得而危者
至勢已去而憂且成矣豈不大可畏哉知
此可以言禦戎之道矣今夫山西古冀州
地也虞夏雖分而職方未改叔虞受命而
晉國始分山河表裏天下稱雄及其藩籬
自撤犬羊内窺西北與戎遂爲多事歷漢
===
而唐而宋燕雲諸郡淪沒夷狄者四百四
十餘年衣冠汙辱壇裘者二百四十餘年
自天地開闢以來夷狄繹騷之禍莫甚於
此我
太祖高皇帝應運而興掃盪妖氛恢復帝王之
境土重關中國之彝倫華夷之限昭然始
明内外之界截然始定大同特爲重鎭腹
外也山西隷之關南腹内也偏頭西抵於
滑石鴈門東至於平刑寧武設中控制諸
punctuated: 早決之，則患銷於未萌，禍弭於未著，力用寡而功成多，財不匱而事就速，天下陰被其福而莫知其所以然也。苟或玩其變而緩於圖，忽其幾而輕於應，安未得而危者至，勢已去而憂且成矣，豈不大可畏哉！知此，可以言禦戎之道矣。今夫山西，古冀州地也。虞夏雖分，而職方未改；叔虞受命，而晉國始分。山河表裏，天下稱雄。及其藩籬自撤，犬羊内窺，西北與戎遂爲多事。歷漢而唐而宋，燕雲諸郡淪沒夷狄者四百四十餘年，衣冠汙辱壇裘者二百四十餘年。自天地開闢以來，夷狄繹騷之禍莫甚於此。我太祖高皇帝應運而興，掃盪妖氛，恢復帝王之境土，重關中國之彝倫，華夷之限昭然始明，内外之界截然始定。大同特爲重鎭，腹外也；山西隷之關南，腹内也。偏頭西抵於滑石，鴈門東至於平刑，寧武設中，控制諸
translation_en:
…and resolve them early, then troubles will dissolve before they sprout and calamities subside before they become manifest. Little effort will accomplish much; resources will not be exhausted, and affairs will be brought swiftly to completion. All under Heaven will receive these blessings unawares, without knowing how they came about. But if one treats changes carelessly and delays planning, disregards their first signs and responds lightly, danger will arrive before security has been attained. The favorable situation will already have slipped away, and trouble will be taking shape. Is this not greatly to be feared? Understanding this, one may discuss the way to resist the Rong.
Now Shanxi was the territory of ancient Jizhou. Although divisions were made under Yu and Xia, its administrative geography remained unchanged. Only when Shu Yu received his investiture was the state of Jin marked out. With mountains and rivers protecting it within and without, it was renowned throughout the realm for its strength. Once its protective barriers had been dismantled from within, however, the “dogs and sheep” peered into its interior, and dealings with the Rong in the northwest became a source of many troubles. Through the Han, Tang, and Song, the prefectures of Yan and Yun remained submerged under barbarian rule for more than 440 years; the capped and robed people suffered humiliation under those clad in felt and fur [?] for more than 240 years. Since Heaven and Earth first opened, no calamity of barbarian disturbance had been worse than this.
Our Emperor Taizu Gao arose in response to Heaven’s appointed destiny, swept away the baleful influences, restored the territorial domain of the emperors and kings, and renewed the enduring moral order of the Central Realm [?]. Only then did the distinction between Chinese and barbarians become clearly manifest, and the boundary between inside and outside become firmly established. Datong was made a particularly important garrison, outside the heartland. Shanxi, attached to it south of the passes [?], lay within the heartland. Piantou extended west to Huashi; Yanmen reached east to Pingxing; Ningwu was established in the center, commanding the various…

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
鎮聯絡聲援其勢屹立矣夫何頻歲以來
虜益猖獗越邊垣而蕩食入內境以長驅
邊腹之勢未見攸分則防禦之策亦未可
以輕重論也審勢以決其幾其容緩乎昔
晉文公以一隅之地西備強秦南控荊楚
有敵國之憂無中原之助乃能尊周室攘
夷狄主盟諸侯遂霸天下彼何地險之足
恃哉蓋文公廣而儉文而有禮其臣狐趙
輩又皆肅而寬忠而能力君臣同德上下
===
協心城濮一戰有不主夏盟者耶今以全
晉之人力抗蕞爾之狂胡峻三關之保障
爲大同之椅角若有百倍之勢宜戰勝而
守固矣然皆以疆界自私以倖免爲利以
保身爲得計人旣殊心則謀自異用不免
顧此失彼耳曾謂不得人和者而可以地
利自保耶秦用商鞅之策招三晉之人以
併諸侯而空六合漢制郡國有材官騎士
而武帝取之幷冀者得以威絕域而空王
punctuated: 鎮，聯絡聲援，其勢屹立矣。夫何頻歲以來，虜益猖獗，越邊垣而蕩食，入內境以長驅？邊腹之勢未見攸分，則防禦之策亦未可以輕重論也。審勢以決其幾，其容緩乎？昔晉文公以一隅之地，西備強秦，南控荊楚，有敵國之憂，無中原之助，乃能尊周室，攘夷狄，主盟諸侯，遂霸天下。彼何地險之足恃哉？蓋文公廣而儉，文而有禮，其臣狐趙輩又皆肅而寬，忠而能力。君臣同德，上下協心，城濮一戰，有不主夏盟者耶？今以全晉之人力，抗蕞爾之狂胡，峻三關之保障，爲大同之椅角，若有百倍之勢，宜戰勝而守固矣。然皆以疆界自私，以倖免爲利，以保身爲得計。人旣殊心，則謀自異用，不免顧此失彼耳。曾謂不得人和者，而可以地利自保耶？秦用商鞅之策，招三晉之人，以併諸侯而空六合。漢制郡國有材官騎士，而武帝取之幷冀者，得以威絕域而空王
translation_en:
…the garrisons, linking them in mutual support: their strategic position stood firm. Why, then, in recent years have the enemy grown ever more rampant, crossing the frontier walls to plunder provisions and driving deep into the interior? The frontier and the heartland have shown no difference in their vulnerability; defensive measures therefore cannot be ranked as more or less important. Can we afford to delay assessing the situation and determining the critical opportunity for action?

In former times, Duke Wen of Jin held only a corner of the realm. To the west he guarded against mighty Qin, and to the south he held Jing-Chu in check. Troubled by hostile states and without help from the Central Plain, he nevertheless honored the royal house of Zhou, repelled the barbarians, presided over the covenants of the feudal lords, and ultimately became hegemon of all under Heaven. How could natural defenses alone have sufficed for him to rely upon? Duke Wen was generous yet frugal, cultivated and observant of ritual; his ministers, men of the Hu and Zhao lineages, were likewise dignified yet lenient, loyal and capable of strenuous service. Ruler and ministers shared one purpose, and superiors and subordinates worked with one heart. After the battle of Chengpu, how could he have failed to preside over the covenant of the Chinese states?

Now, with the manpower of all Jin to resist a trifling force of fierce northern barbarians, and with the defenses of the Three Passes strengthened to provide mutually supporting positions [?] for Datong, we seem to possess a hundredfold advantage. We ought to prevail in battle and hold firm in defense. Yet everyone treats his own jurisdiction as a private concern, regards escaping harm by luck as a gain, and considers preserving himself a successful strategy. Since their purposes differ, their plans naturally diverge in execution, and they inevitably attend to one place while neglecting another. Can it really be said that those who lack harmony among their people can secure themselves through advantages of terrain?

Qin adopted Shang Yang’s policies and recruited people from the Three Jin, thereby annexing the feudal states and sweeping all rivals from the realm. Under the Han system, the commanderies and kingdoms maintained trained infantry and cavalry. Emperor Wu drew upon those from Bing and Ji and was thus able to project his might into remote regions and empty the royal…

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
庭唐李抱眞之鎭澤潞也籍民三丁選一
壯者給以弓矢農隙習射歲暮都試行其
賞罰三年得精兵二萬遂能雄視山東樹
勛唐室咸以昭義步兵爲天下諸軍冠彼
何兵力之雄若此哉蓋秦有信賞之令漢
有筭賦之制唐有鐲租稅之法人心樂從
戎功易集號令一頒有不順應者乎今則
行伍列諸營也而又召募日增遊技設諸
要也而又調徵歲至其視所招所出所稱
===
最者亦有百倍之勢似有征而無敵矣然
令不足以激其衷制不足以寬其力法不
足以洽其情身爲我役而心非我依不過
冗兵冗食耳曾謂人心未順而可以圖大
事乎蓋地險非不足恃也晉文公無有形
之地險而有無形之地險故其稱霸也易
人心非不易奮也秦漢與唐無全集之人
心而有全勝之人心故其率衆也從凡此
皆善決其幾者也其無敵於人國也不亦
punctuated:
庭。唐李抱眞之鎭澤潞也，籍民三丁，選一壯者，給以弓矢，農隙習射，歲暮都試，行其賞罰。三年得精兵二萬，遂能雄視山東，樹勛唐室，咸以昭義步兵爲天下諸軍冠。彼何兵力之雄若此哉？蓋秦有信賞之令，漢有筭賦之制，唐有鐲租稅之法，人心樂從，戎功易集，號令一頒，有不順應者乎？今則行伍列諸營也，而又召募日增；遊技設諸要也，而又調徵歲至。其視所招、所出、所稱最者，亦有百倍之勢，似有征而無敵矣。然令不足以激其衷，制不足以寬其力，法不足以洽其情，身爲我役，而心非我依，不過冗兵冗食耳。曾謂人心未順，而可以圖大事乎？

蓋地險非不足恃也，晉文公無有形之地險，而有無形之地險，故其稱霸也易。人心非不易奮也，秦漢與唐無全集之人心，而有全勝之人心，故其率衆也從。凡此皆善決其幾者也，其無敵於人國也，不亦
translation_en:
…court. When Li Baozhen of the Tang commanded at Zelu, he registered the adult males and selected one strong man from every three. He supplied them with bows and arrows, had them practice archery during slack periods in farming, and held a general test at the end of the year, administering rewards and punishments accordingly. Within three years he had obtained twenty thousand elite soldiers. He could thus overawe Shandong and win distinction in service to the Tang ruling house. All regarded the Zhaoyi infantry as foremost among the armies of the realm. How did their military strength become so formidable? Qin had orders ensuring trustworthy rewards; Han had its system of poll taxation; and Tang had a law concerning rents and taxes [?]. The people willingly followed, and military achievements were readily attained. Once commands were issued, was there anyone who did not comply?

Today, troops are arrayed in the various camps, yet recruitment increases daily; mobile troops [?] are stationed at strategic points, yet further levies arrive every year. Compared with the men recruited, the forces fielded, and those acclaimed as the finest in those earlier times, our strength is a hundredfold greater: it would seem that we could campaign without encountering a match. Yet our orders do not suffice to stir their hearts, our institutions do not suffice to ease their burdens, and our laws do not suffice to accommodate their feelings. Their bodies serve us, but their hearts do not cleave to us. They are merely superfluous soldiers consuming superfluous provisions. Could one really suppose that great undertakings can be planned before the people's hearts are won?

It is not that defensive terrain cannot be relied upon. Duke Wen of Jin had no tangible defensive terrain, yet he possessed intangible defensive terrain; thus he readily became hegemon. Nor is it that people's hearts are difficult to rouse. Qin, Han, and Tang did not have the hearts of all people gathered to them, yet they possessed hearts set on complete victory; thus, when they led their forces, the men followed. All these were skilled at discerning the decisive moment. Was it not also …

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
宜乎今之築障置戍地險勝矣而所以固
其險者未豫何取於深塹高墉以爲防訓
習日勤兵力奮矣而所以强其力者未充
何取于鼓進金退之爲節旣失其機矣其
奚以應事變之至耶我觀世之言禦戎之
策者不過有五曰豫積貯以時輓運豫之
誠是也不知姦商蠹吏互肆侵漁給散有
名朽腐不可食矣有饑色者不離心乎曰
利器用以備鬭攻利之誠是也不知荷戈
===
負甲枵腹待哺驅策疲騎祇爲敵人資耳
無精力者有鬭志乎曰廣召募以實空虛
廣之誠是也不知令申未閑攣孚無素脉
親上忠長之義者可以責其暴虎馮河之
勇乎曰嚴斥堠以明耳目明之誠是也聞
風而慄望塵而奔敵來則莫知所禦敵去
則尾逐其後斥堠果足以警人心乎曰多
間諜以察情僞察之誠是也我之所給不
足以慊其欲敵之所利每足以結其心欲
punctuated: 宜乎？今之築障置戍，地險勝矣，而所以固其險者未豫，何取於深塹高墉以爲防？訓習日勤，兵力奮矣，而所以强其力者未充，何取于鼓進金退之爲節？旣失其機矣，其奚以應事變之至耶？我觀世之言禦戎之策者，不過有五：曰豫積貯以時輓運，豫之誠是也，不知姦商蠹吏互肆侵漁，給散有名，朽腐不可食矣，有饑色者不離心乎？曰利器用以備鬭攻，利之誠是也，不知荷戈負甲，枵腹待哺，驅策疲騎，祇爲敵人資耳，無精力者有鬭志乎？曰廣召募以實空虛，廣之誠是也，不知令申未閑，攣孚無素，脉親上忠長之義者，可以責其暴虎馮河之勇乎？曰嚴斥堠以明耳目，明之誠是也，聞風而慄，望塵而奔，敵來則莫知所禦，敵去則尾逐其後，斥堠果足以警人心乎？曰多間諜以察情僞，察之誠是也，我之所給不足以慊其欲，敵之所利每足以結其心，欲
translation_en:
…is this not fitting? Today, barriers are built and garrisons established, giving us formidable terrain; yet preparations for securing those advantages have not been made. What use, then, are deep moats and high walls as defenses? Training and practice are pursued diligently each day, and military strength is roused; yet the means of sustaining that strength remain inadequate. What use, then, are drums signaling advance and gongs signaling retreat? Having already missed the critical opportunity, how can we respond when unforeseen events arrive?

I observe that the strategies people now propose for resisting hostile peoples amount to no more than five. First, they say: stockpile provisions in advance and transport them at the proper times. Preparing in advance is indeed right. Yet they fail to recognize that unscrupulous merchants and corrupt officials freely join in embezzlement: distributions exist in name, while the grain has rotted and cannot be eaten. Will men who bear the signs of hunger not become disaffected?

Second, they say: sharpen weapons and improve equipment in preparation for combat and assault. Improving them is indeed right. Yet they fail to recognize that men bearing spears and armor wait for food with empty bellies, driving on exhausted mounts, only to furnish resources to the enemy. Can men without energy possess the will to fight?

Third, they say: expand recruitment to fill depleted ranks. Expanding it is indeed right. Yet they fail to recognize that the men are unfamiliar with repeatedly proclaimed orders, that bonds of trust have not been established [?], and that they do not understand the duty of loving their superiors and remaining loyal to their commanders [?]. Can such men be expected to show the courage of those who attack tigers barehanded and cross rivers on foot?

Fourth, they say: tighten scouting and watchkeeping to make our eyes and ears more discerning. Improving their discernment is indeed right. Yet men tremble at rumors and flee at the sight of dust. When the enemy comes, they do not know how to resist; when the enemy leaves, they trail behind. Can scouting and watchkeeping really suffice to put men's hearts on the alert?

Fifth, they say: employ more spies to distinguish the true situation from deception. Investigating is indeed right. Yet what we provide is insufficient to satisfy their desires, while the benefits the enemy offers are often enough to win their allegiance. To wish…

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
其腹心我也難矣不反爲敵之間諜乎凡
此五者皆禦戎之不可少者而其要其幾
其務則不在是也然則擇將帥者其急務
乎固人心者其大幾乎明賞罰者其至要
乎明於此三者始可以言安攘之道矣嘗
聞將者國之輔也輔周則國强是擇將固
不可以不慎而任將尤不可以不專也不
聞上不制於天下不制於地中不制於人
乎今文墨所拘動或掣肘機宜每由於遠
===
決號令常至於兩從不以身貴而賤人則
以獨貴而違衆不以三軍爲衆而輕敵則
以受命爲重而捐生求其戰勝於外功成
於內也亦難矣擇將者其可輕乎民者邦
之本也本固則邦寧是民力固不能以不
用而民心亦不可以或悖也不聞視卒如
嬰兒可與赴深谿視卒如愛子可與之俱
死乎今將所指麾多不從移號令不樂於
聞動衆不樂於戰不和於國何以出軍不
punctuated:
其腹心我也，難矣！不反爲敵之間諜乎？凡此五者，皆禦戎之不可少者，而其要、其幾、其務，則不在是也。然則擇將帥者，其急務乎？固人心者，其大幾乎？明賞罰者，其至要乎？明於此三者，始可以言安攘之道矣。
嘗聞：「將者，國之輔也；輔周則國强。」是擇將固不可以不慎，而任將尤不可以不專也。不聞「上不制於天，下不制於地，中不制於人」乎？今文墨所拘，動或掣肘，機宜每由於遠決，號令常至於兩從。不以身貴而賤人，則以獨貴而違衆；不以三軍爲衆而輕敵，則以受命爲重而捐生。求其戰勝於外，功成於內也，亦難矣！擇將者，其可輕乎？
民者，邦之本也；本固則邦寧。是民力固不能以不用，而民心亦不可以或悖也。不聞「視卒如嬰兒，可與赴深谿；視卒如愛子，可與之俱死」乎？今將所指麾，多不從移；號令不樂於聞，動衆不樂於戰。不和於國，何以出軍？不
translation_en:
…for them to give us their heartfelt loyalty is difficult indeed! Might they not instead become spies for the enemy? All these five measures are indispensable for resisting the frontier foes, yet the essential requirements, the critical factors, and the tasks that demand attention lie elsewhere. Is selecting commanders, then, the urgent task? Is securing people’s allegiance the great determining factor? Is making rewards and punishments clear the foremost requirement? Only when these three are understood can one begin to speak of the way to secure peace within and repel enemies without.
I have heard it said: “The general is the support of the state; when that support is sound, the state is strong.” Thus one must certainly exercise care in selecting a general, and still more must one give him undivided authority when entrusting him with command. Have you not heard: “Above, he is not constrained by Heaven; below, he is not constrained by Earth; in between, he is not constrained by men”? Today, bound by paperwork, he is hampered whenever he acts. Decisions about opportunities and expedient action are frequently made far away, and orders often leave him serving two authorities. If he does not despise others because of his own high standing, he defies the multitude because he alone enjoys distinction; if he does not underestimate the enemy because his armies are numerous, he throws away his life because he considers his commission weighty. To expect him to win battles abroad and bring success to the state at home is difficult indeed! Can the selection of generals be treated lightly?
The people are the foundation of the state; when the foundation is firm, the state is tranquil. Thus, although the people’s strength must necessarily be employed, their hearts must never be alienated. Have you not heard: “Treat your soldiers as infants, and you may go with them into deep ravines; treat your soldiers as beloved sons, and you may die together with them”? Today, those whom generals command mostly fail to follow their direction [?]. They have no wish to hear orders, and when the troops are mobilized, they have no wish to fight. Without harmony within the state, how can an army be sent forth? Without …

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
和於軍何以出陣不和于陣何以進戰不
和於戰何以決勝欲其致身盡節一月三
捷也亦難矣固人心者又其可緩乎賞罰
者國家之大柄人心所視以爲去留者也
賞功不可以踰時罰罪不可以遺昵不聞
法令不明賞罰不信金之不止鼓之不進
雖百萬何益于用乎令有功者未必賞而
賞者未必當其功有罪者未必罰而罰者
未必當其罪此所以冒功之獘日滋而血
===
戰之績不奏逗遛之風益熾而豪傑之志
愈隳欲其寇小至張聲勢以遏其入寇大
至謀其大以邀其功亦鮮矣明賞罰者又
非其所當急者乎誠能懲既往之失以作
維新之圖選任得其人事情無所匿功罪
彰於覈實之辨賞罰決于指示之嚴則食
雖未足而壯氣猶足以直前也器雖未精
而制挺或可以決勝也兵雖莫助而感恩
者重信而思義也警雖報頻而效死者奮
punctuated: 和於軍，何以出陣？不和于陣，何以進戰？不和於戰，何以決勝？欲其致身盡節，一月三捷也，亦難矣。固人心者，又其可緩乎？賞罰者，國家之大柄，人心所視以爲去留者也。賞功不可以踰時，罰罪不可以遺昵。不聞法令不明，賞罰不信，金之不止，鼓之不進，雖百萬何益于用乎？令有功者未必賞，而賞者未必當其功；有罪者未必罰，而罰者未必當其罪。此所以冒功之獘日滋，而血戰之績不奏；逗遛之風益熾，而豪傑之志愈隳。欲其寇小至，張聲勢以遏其入；寇大至，謀其大以邀其功，亦鮮矣。明賞罰者，又非其所當急者乎？誠能懲既往之失，以作維新之圖，選任得其人，事情無所匿，功罪彰於覈實之辨，賞罰決于指示之嚴，則食雖未足，而壯氣猶足以直前也；器雖未精，而制挺或可以決勝也；兵雖莫助，而感恩者重信而思義也；警雖報頻，而效死者奮
translation_en:
…if there is no harmony within the army, how can it deploy in battle formation? If there is no harmony in the ranks, how can it advance to fight? If there is no harmony in battle, how can it secure victory? To expect the soldiers to devote themselves utterly, fulfill their loyalty, and win three victories in a single month would indeed be difficult. Can securing their allegiance, then, be delayed? Rewards and punishments are the state's great instruments of authority; people look to them in deciding whether to stay or leave. Meritorious service must be rewarded promptly, and punishment for wrongdoing must not spare favorites. Have you not heard that when laws and orders are unclear and rewards and punishments untrustworthy, soldiers do not halt at the gong or advance at the drum, and even a million men are of no practical use? As things stand [?], those with merit are not necessarily rewarded, and rewards do not necessarily match their merit; those guilty of wrongdoing are not necessarily punished, and punishments do not necessarily match their offenses. This is why fraudulent claims of merit multiply daily, while bloody fighting yields no achievements; the habit of delaying and hanging back grows ever more prevalent, while the resolve of brave and outstanding men declines still further. To expect them, when raiders arrive in small numbers, to make a show of force and bar their entry, or, when raiders arrive in strength, to devise a major strategy and thereby win distinction, is to expect what seldom occurs. Is clarifying rewards and punishments not, then, an urgent priority?

If we can truly take past failures as a warning and devise plans for renewal, select and appoint the right men, allow no facts to remain concealed, establish merit and guilt through scrutiny of the actual circumstances, and determine rewards and punishments through strict directives, then, although provisions may still be insufficient, the soldiers' fighting spirit will suffice to carry them straight ahead. Although their weapons may still lack refinement, even wooden clubs [?] may secure victory. Although no troops come to their aid, those grateful for favors received will value keeping faith and think of their duty. Although alarms are reported frequently, those ready to give their lives will rouse themselves…

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
怒而思勇也以之守險而險自固先人有
以奪人之氣以之興兵而兵自强不戰而
有以屈人之心威聲動揚精神迅發以振
王靈以一
國勢不在於轉移之間乎夫是之謂決其幾
也若探本而論之則
朝廷者元氣也內也邊鎮者四肢也外也善
理身者必先調其元氣元氣充實則脉絡
通而肢體益暢護四肢所以重元氣也
===
畿輔者堂室也內也邊鎮者垣墉也外也善
治家者必先閎其堂室堂室隆深則扃牖
嚴而垣墉益密崇垣墉所以衛堂室也內
外輕重緩急在審其幾而已矣方今
聖天子德備中和
功冒覆載以天下爲一家而愛之者無不至以
中國爲一身而保之者無不周
賞之所及
恩眞同雨露也
punctuated:
怒而思勇也。以之守險，而險自固，先人有以奪人之氣；以之興兵，而兵自强，不戰而有以屈人之心。威聲動揚，精神迅發，以振王靈，以一國勢，不在於轉移之間乎？夫是之謂決其幾也。
若探本而論之，則朝廷者，元氣也，內也；邊鎮者，四肢也，外也。善理身者，必先調其元氣；元氣充實，則脉絡通而肢體益暢。護四肢，所以重元氣也。
畿輔者，堂室也，內也；邊鎮者，垣墉也，外也。善治家者，必先閎其堂室；堂室隆深，則扃牖嚴而垣墉益密。崇垣墉，所以衛堂室也。內外輕重緩急，在審其幾而已矣。
方今聖天子德備中和，功冒覆載，以天下爲一家而愛之者無不至，以中國爲一身而保之者無不周。賞之所及，恩眞同雨露也。
translation_en:
…roused to anger and intent on acting courageously. Employ them to defend strategic passes, and those passes will naturally be secure; by acting before the enemy, one can break the enemy’s spirit. Employ them to undertake military operations, and the army will naturally be strong; without fighting, one can subdue the enemy’s resolve. With the fame of our might spreading and our spirit swiftly rising, could we not, in the course of this transformation, invigorate royal authority and unite the strength of the realm? This is what is meant by taking decisive action at the critical juncture.
If we probe the root of the matter, the court is the vital energy of the body: it is the interior. The frontier garrisons are its four limbs: they are the exterior. One who tends the body well must first regulate its vital energy. When that energy is abundant, the channels flow freely and the limbs move with greater ease. Protecting the four limbs is a means of safeguarding the vital energy.
The capital region is the halls and chambers of a house: it is the interior. The frontier garrisons are its enclosing walls: they are the exterior. One who manages a household well must first enlarge its halls and chambers. When these are lofty and deep, the doors and windows are secure, and the enclosing walls provide still tighter protection. Raising the enclosing walls is a means of defending the halls and chambers. In weighing interior against exterior, greater against lesser importance, and what can wait against what is urgent, all depends on discerning the critical juncture.
Today, the sagely Son of Heaven possesses in full the virtues of equilibrium and harmony, and his achievements extend everywhere beneath Heaven and upon Earth. He regards all under Heaven as one family, and there is no limit to his loving care for it; he regards the Central Realm as one body, and leaves nothing outside his comprehensive protection. Wherever his rewards reach, his beneficence is truly like rain and dew.

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
罰之所加
威眞若雷霆也臣民奔走服從者誰有後先此
其固人心之明驗乎執事倘不厭其聽尚
有芹忱以爲
廟謨獻
punctuated: 罰之所加，威眞若雷霆也。臣民奔走服從者，誰有後先？此其固人心之明驗乎？執事倘不厭其聽，尚有芹忱，以爲廟謨獻。
translation_en: …Where punishment falls, imperial might is truly like thunder. Among officials and commoners hastening to obey, who lags behind another? Is this not clear proof that the people’s allegiance has been secured? If you, gentlemen in charge, do not weary of listening, I still have a humble, heartfelt offering to contribute to the court’s deliberations.

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
山西鄉試錄後序
山西古冀州域堯舜生焉皐
夔稷契相與唐虞其治而精
一執中之學此開也多士後
堯舜以生唐虞家學亡弗聞
矣其聞之親于四方宜亡弗
深于四方矣皐夔稷契非當
===
時所登庸之士乎今夫山川
冀也風氣冀也乃人才獨不
冀不稷契皐夔亟見豈二帝
之澤熄耶然道在人心風師
百世觀于其文可以知帝澤
矣文純正謹嚴憲聖人之經
而不詭于道其語渾朴其氣
punctuated:
山西鄉試錄後序

山西，古冀州域，堯舜生焉，皐夔稷契相與唐虞其治，而精一執中之學此開也。多士後堯舜以生，唐虞家學亡弗聞矣。其聞之親于四方，宜亡弗深于四方矣。皐夔稷契，非當時所登庸之士乎？

今夫山川，冀也；風氣，冀也。乃人才獨不冀，不稷契皐夔亟見，豈二帝之澤熄耶？然道在人心，風師百世，觀于其文，可以知帝澤矣。文純正謹嚴，憲聖人之經而不詭于道，其語渾朴，其氣
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shanxi Provincial Examination

Shanxi lies within the territory of ancient Jizhou. Yao and Shun were born here, and Gao, Kui, Ji, and Xie together established the governance of Tang and Yu. Here began the teaching of refined discernment, singleness of purpose, and holding fast to the Mean. The many scholars born after Yao and Shun have all heard the teachings handed down in the households of Tang and Yu. Since their acquaintance with these teachings is more intimate than that of scholars elsewhere, their understanding should also be deeper. Were Gao, Kui, Ji, and Xie not the men who were then raised to office?

Now, the mountains and rivers are those of Ji; its prevailing influences are those of Ji. Yet its men of talent alone are unlike those of Ji, and figures such as Ji, Xie, Gao, and Kui do not frequently appear [?]. Can the beneficent legacy of the two emperors have died out? Yet the Way resides in human hearts, and their influence instructs a hundred generations. By examining these scholars’ writings, one can discern the emperors’ legacy. Their writing is pure and correct, careful and rigorous; it takes the sages’ classics as its standard and does not depart from the Way. Its language is simple and unadorned, and its vital force…

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
雄勁其思精恪其色蒼鬱宛
然篤茅茨土階之風遊深山
鹿豕間意象亂松巨石撑柱
峭立不假雕琢有時游龍怒
蛟沛江漢而下之嶷嶷鬚角
變現觥觵非上世之璞未盡
散耶是不于其質也可商于
===
其忠也可夏于其古也可虞
可唐耶非山川非帝澤之以
耶昔者蒸民狉狉然鳥獸野
爾堯舜神后始以其經綸之
文文之生之以農成之以敎
要之以刑久之以樂先天而
生其心開物而前其性民未
punctuated:
雄勁，其思精恪，其色蒼鬱，宛然篤茅茨土階之風，遊深山鹿豕間，意象亂松巨石，撑柱峭立，不假雕琢。有時游龍怒蛟，沛江漢而下之，嶷嶷鬚角，變現觥觵，非上世之璞未盡散耶？是不于其質也可商，于其忠也可夏，于其古也可虞可唐耶？非山川、非帝澤之以耶？
昔者蒸民狉狉然，鳥獸野爾。堯舜神后，始以其經綸之文文之，生之以農，成之以敎，要之以刑，久之以樂，先天而生其心，開物而前其性。民未
translation_en:
…vigorous and forceful; its thought is precise and earnest, its coloring deep and luxuriant. It vividly embodies the simple ethos of thatched roofs and earthen steps, roaming among deer and wild swine in the deep mountains. Its imagery is of tangled pines and immense rocks, standing like pillars, sheer and upright, without recourse to carving or polishing. At times it is like a roaming dragon or an enraged water dragon, surging down the Jiang and Han rivers, whiskers and horns towering, its transformations imposing [?]. Is this not the uncarved jade of high antiquity, not yet wholly dispersed? Could it not, in its substance, belong to the Shang; in its loyalty, to the Xia; and in its antiquity, to the age of Yu or Tang [?]? Is this not owing to the mountains and rivers, and to the emperors’ beneficence [?]?
In ancient times, the multitude lived in an untamed state, wild as birds and beasts. Yao and Shun, those sage rulers, first brought them refinement through the civilizing patterns by which they ordered the world. They sustained them through agriculture, perfected them through instruction, restrained them through punishments, and made their transformation endure through music. Anticipating Heaven, they awakened their hearts; opening up the world of things, they guided their nature forward. The people had not yet…

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
知邪以直事其上而已民未
知巧以拙事其上而已民未
知僞以慤事其上而已此皐
夔稷契之相爲皡皡者也當
是時其文也以道德君子謂
之化爲周末之文也世降而
周民志寖廣其欲四熾聖人
===
又出其禮義廉恥是非之心
示之創制立法懸大防于天
下當是時其文也以政治民
始則之君子斯謂之文矣秦
原既褻帝王跡蕪於是尚辭
令爲縱橫捭闔巧譎相射卒
爲戰國君子曰其末也弊文
punctuated: 知邪，以直事其上而已；民未知巧，以拙事其上而已；民未知僞，以慤事其上而已。此皐、夔、稷、契之相爲皡皡者也。當是時，其文也以道德，君子謂之化。爲周末之文也，世降而周，民志寖廣，其欲四熾，聖人又出其禮義廉恥是非之心示之，創制立法，懸大防于天下。當是時，其文也以政治，民始則之，君子斯謂之文矣。秦原既褻，帝王跡蕪，於是尚辭令，爲縱橫捭闔，巧譎相射，卒爲戰國。君子曰：「其末也弊，文
translation_en:
…knew no perversity and merely served their superiors with uprightness; the people knew no cunning and merely served their superiors with simplicity; the people knew no deceit and merely served their superiors with sincerity. This was the radiant simplicity brought about through the assistance of Gao, Kui, Ji, and Xie. At that time, cultural refinement proceeded through the Way and virtue; the gentleman called it moral transformation.

As for the cultural refinement of the late Zhou, as the ages declined into the Zhou, the people’s ambitions gradually expanded, and their desires blazed in every direction. The sages then further revealed to them their hearts’ sense of ritual propriety, righteousness, integrity, shame, right, and wrong.
