They created institutions and established laws, setting great barriers before all under Heaven. At that time, cultural refinement proceeded through government, and the people began to take it as their standard. This the gentleman called cultural refinement.

Once the Qin plain had been profaned [?] and the traces of the ancient emperors and kings had become overgrown, men came to prize persuasive speech, pursuing vertical and horizontal alliances and the arts of opening and closing negotiations, assailing one another with cunning and deceit. This culminated in the Warring States. The gentleman said: “In its final stage it became corrupt; cultural refinement …

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
禍之爾漢興設科士以制策
唐以聲律宋以經義君子曰
藝焉文則吾不知也
天啓
聖祖
秦期篤生
握符膺運
===
龍德正中
服堯舜之道拓唐虞之文以
君師萬方百八十餘年于茲肆我
皇上
堯仁舜孝
湯敬文一
兼體帝王之文
punctuated:
禍之爾。漢興，設科士以制策；唐以聲律，宋以經義。君子曰：「藝焉，文則吾不知也。」
天啓聖祖，秦期篤生，握符膺運，龍德正中，服堯舜之道，拓唐虞之文，以君師萬方，百八十餘年于茲。肆我皇上，堯仁舜孝，湯敬文一，兼體帝王之文。
translation_en:
…brought calamity upon it, that is all. When the Han arose, it established examinations to select scholars through policy questions issued by imperial command; the Tang used tonal patterns and prosody, and the Song, interpretations of the Classics. The gentleman says: “These are skills; whether they constitute true cultural refinement, I do not know.”
Heaven brought forth the Sagely Founder, born in the Qin period [?], who grasped the token of sovereignty and received Heaven’s allotted destiny. His dragon virtue was upright and centered. He practiced the Way of Yao and Shun and extended the culture of Tang and Yu, serving as sovereign and teacher to all lands. More than 180 years have now elapsed. Thus our present Emperor, possessing Yao’s benevolence, Shun’s filial piety, Tang’s reverence, and King Wen’s single-mindedness, embodies together the cultural virtues of the ancient emperors and kings.

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
經緯
天地之大
通于神明
光于齋貊然猶
章顯元獻
式熙
帝載廟堂輔佐諸臣卽不敢必天
===
下之有淳民而後皐夔稷契
之治始興亦不敢必天下之
無淳民而自蘄夫稷契皐夔
之治蓋務爲皡皡之文者相
無窮也一時青衿之士皆有
以仰見其
精一執中之傳
punctuated: 經緯天地之大，通于神明，光于齋貊。然猶章顯元獻，式熙帝載。廟堂輔佐諸臣，卽不敢必天下之有淳民而後皐夔稷契之治始興，亦不敢必天下之無淳民而自蘄夫稷契皐夔之治。蓋務爲皡皡之文者，相無窮也。一時青衿之士，皆有以仰見其精一執中之傳，
translation_en: …ordering the vastness of Heaven and Earth, communicating with the spirits, and casting his light upon the Zhai and Mo peoples [?]. Yet he still brings eminent worthies to prominence, thereby advancing the imperial enterprise. The ministers assisting him at court dare not insist that the world must first possess people of simple virtue before government like that of Gao Yao, Kui, Ji, and Xie can arise; nor dare they insist that the world lacks people of simple virtue and merely aspire on their own to government like that of Ji, Xie, Gao Yao, and Kui. For those striving to foster radiant culture provide assistance without end [?]. The students of the time can all look up and perceive his transmission of the teaching to remain discerning and single-minded and hold fast to the Mean…

title: 嘉靖三十四年山西鄉試錄
text:
放勳重華之盛思蚤夜焉無自
醜于賔興以來吐握帝澤旣
行
聖化尤渥以是知冀士之速肖爲
易易也豈惟冀哉于梁于雍
于兖于天下抑又可知也夫
士一也其脩文之責一也冀
===
則有皐夔稷契而爲之前信
未可以淺薄爲者矣多士勉
乎哉
河南汝寧府光州光山縣儒
學教諭袁〔文星〕謹序
punctuated:
放勳重華之盛，思蚤夜焉，無自醜于賔興，以來吐握。帝澤旣行，聖化尤渥，以是知冀士之速肖爲易易也。豈惟冀哉？于梁，于雍，于兖，于天下，抑又可知也。夫士一也，其脩文之責一也。冀則有皐夔稷契而爲之前信，未可以淺薄爲者矣。多士勉乎哉！
河南汝寧府光州光山縣儒學教諭袁〔文星〕謹序。
translation_en:
…the flourishing age of Fangxun and Chonghua [Yao and Shun]. Let them reflect upon this morning and night, bringing no disgrace upon themselves when worthies are honored and recommended, and thereby eliciting the welcome accorded to worthy men [alluding to the Duke of Zhou interrupting his meals and bathing to receive them]. Imperial bounty has already spread, and the sage sovereign’s transforming influence is especially abundant. From this we know how very easy it will be for the scholars of Ji to conform swiftly to these exemplars. And why only Ji? The same may be understood of Liang, Yong, Yan, and all under Heaven. Scholars are alike, and alike is their responsibility to cultivate learning. Ji has Gao, Kui, Ji, and Xie as prior testimony to this; its scholars must not conduct themselves superficially. Strive, you many scholars!
Respectfully prefaced by Yuan Wenxing, Instructor of the Confucian School of Guangshan County, Guang Zhou, Runing Prefecture, Henan.
